especially right at the beginning of the course.
And I did struggle with it.
I thought it'd be hard,
but actually I found it all quite straightforward.
What did you think about diet and nutrition?
OK, I suppose.
Do you remember what they told us about pet food
and the fact that there's such limited checking into whether or not it's contaminated?
I mean in comparison with the checks on food for humans,
I thought that was terrible.
I think the module that really impressed me was the animal disease one,
when we looked at domesticated animals in different parts of the world,
like camels and water buffalo and alpaca.
The economies of so many countries depend on these,
but scientists don't know much about the diseases that affect them.
Yes,
I thought they'd know a lot about ways of controlling and eradicating those diseases,
but that's not the case at all.
I loved the wildlife medication unit.
Things like helping birds that have been caught in oil spills.
That's something I hadn't thought about before.
Yeah, I thought I might write my dissertation on something connected with that.
Right. So, actually I was thinking...
So, hello everyone.
My name's Lou Miller and I'm going to be your tour guide today
as we take this fantastic boat trip around the Tasmanian coast.
Before we set off, I just want to tell you a few things about our journey.
Our boats aren't huge as you can see.
We already have three staff members on board
and on top of that,
we can transport a further fifteen people, that's you - around the coastline.
But please note if there are more than nine people on either side of the boat,
we'll move some of you over, otherwise all eighteen of us will end up in the sea!
We've recently upgraded all our boats.
They used to be jet black,
but our new ones now have these comfortable dark red seats and a light-green exterior
in order to stand out from others and help promote our company.
This gives our boats a rather unique appearance, don't you think?
We offer you a free lunchbox during the trip
and we have three types.
Lunchbox 1 contains ham and tomato sandwiches.
Lunchbox 2 contains a cheddar cheese roll
and Lunchbox 3 is salad-based and also contains eggs and tuna.
All three lunchboxes also have a packet of crisps and chocolate bar inside.
Please let staff know which lunchbox you prefer.
I'm sure I don't have to ask you not to throw anything into the sea.
We don't have any bins to put litter in,
but Jess, myself or Ray, our other guide, will collect it from you after lunch
and put it all in a large plastic sack.
The engine on the boat makes quite a lot of noise so before we head off,
let me tell you a few things about what you're going to see.
This area is famous for its ancient lighthouse,
which you'll see from the boat as we turn past the first little island.
It was built in 1838 to protect sailors
as a number of shipwrecks had led to significant loss of life.
The construction itself was complicated
as some of the original drawings kept by the local council show.
It sits right on top of the cliffs in a very isolated spot.
In the nineteenth century there were many jobs there,
such as polishing the brass lamps,
chopping firewood and cleaning windows, that kept lighthouse keepers busy.
These workers were mainly prison convicts until the middle of that century
when ordinary families willing to live in such circumstances took over.
Some of you have asked me what creatures we can expect to see.
I know everyone loves the penguins,
but they're very shy and, unfortunately, tend to hide from passing boats,
but you might see birds in the distance, such as sea eagles,
flying around the cliff edges where they nest.
When we get to the rocky area inhabited by fur seals,
we'll stop and watch them swimming around the coast.
They're inquisitive creatures so don't be surprised if one pops up right in front of you.
Their predators, orca whales, hunt along the coastline too,
but spotting one of these is rare.
Dolphins, on the other hand,
can sometimes approach on their own or in groups as they ride the waves beside us.
Lastly, I want to mention the caves.
Tasmania is famous for its caves
and the ones we'll pass by are so amazing that people are lost for words when they see them.
They can only be approached by sea.
but if you feel that you want to see more than we're able to show you,
then you can take a kayak into the area on another day
and one of our staff will give you more information on that.
What we'll do is to go through a narrow channel,
past some incredible rock formations
and from there we'll be able to see the openings to the caves,
and at that point we'll talk to you about what lies beyond.
Hello?
Oh hello. My name's Jan.
Are you the right person to talk to about the Buckworth Conservation Group?
Yes, I'm Peter. I'm the secretary.
Good. I've just moved to this area, and I'm interested in getting involved.
I was in a similar group where I used to live.
Could you tell me something about your activities, please?
Of course.
Well, we have a mixture of regular activities and special events.
One of the regular ones is trying to keep the beach free of litter.
A few of us spend a couple of hours a month on it,
and it's awful how much there is to clear.
I wish people would be more responsible and take it home with them.
I totally agree.
I'd be happy to help with that.
Is it OK to take dogs?
I'm afraid not, as they're banned from the beach itself.
You can take them along the cliffs, though. And children are welcome.
Right.
We also manage a nature reserve, and there's a lot to do there all year round.
For example, because it's a popular place to visit,
we spend a lot of time looking after the paths
and making sure they're in good condition for walking.
I could certainly help with that.
Good.
And we have a programme of creating new habitats there.
We've just finished making and installing nesting boxes for birds to use,
and next we're going to work on encouraging insects,
they're important for the biodiversity of the reserve.
They certainly are.
Oh, and we're also running a project to identify the different species of butterflies that visit the reserve.
You might be interested in taking part in that.
Sure.
I was involved in something similar where I used to live,
counting all the species of moths.
I'd enjoy that.
Another job we're doing at the reserve is replacing the wall on the southern side,
between the parking area and our woodshed.
It was badly damaged in a storm last month.
OK.
Then as I said, we have a programme of events as well, both at the weekend, and during the week.
Right.
I presume you have guided walks?
I'd like to get to know the local countryside, as I'm new to the area.
Yes, we do. The next walk is to Ruston Island, a week on Saturday.
We'll be meeting in the car park at Dunsmore Beach at low tide,
that's when the sands are dry enough for us to walk to the island without getting wet.
Sounds good.
The island's a great place to explore.
It's quite small, and it's got a range of habitats.
It's also an ideal location for seeing seals just off the coast, or even on the beach.
OK.
And is there anything we should bring, like a picnic, for instance?
Yes, do bring one, as it's a full-day walk.
And of course it'll be wet walking across and back,
so make sure your boots are waterproof.
I must buy a new pair, there's a hole in one of my current ones!
Well, I'd definitely like to come on the walk.
Great.
Then later this month we're having a one-day woodwork session in Hopton Wood.
I've never tried that before.
Is it OK for beginners to take part?
Definitely.
There'll be a couple of experts leading the session,
and we keep the number of participants down, so you'll get as much help as you need.
Excellent!
I'd love to be able to make chairs.
That's probably too ambitious for one day!
You'll be starting with wooden spoons,
and of course learning how to use the tools.
And anything you make is yours to take home with you.
That sounds like fun.
When is it?
It's on the 17th, from 10 a.m. until 3.
There's a charge of £35, including lunch
or £40 if you want to camp in the wood.
I should think I'll come home the same day.
Well, I'd certainly like to join the group.
We all know about the role of carbon dioxide in causing global warming.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #1

challenges.content: Obviously, society needs to reduce the release of carbon dioxide, otherwise known as CO2.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #2

challenges.content: This gas comes from the burning of fossil fuels, such as coal and oil,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #3

challenges.content: and it is virtually impossible for society to prevent, or even limit such activity.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #4

challenges.content: Our need for energy and power is just too great.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #5

challenges.content: Instead, a more practical idea is to collect the carbon dioxide from the burning process,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #6

challenges.content: for example, directly from the chimneys of power stations,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #7

challenges.content: and somehow prevent this gas from being released into the environment.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #8

challenges.content: To do that, you need to store it somehow, and that has to be essentially forever.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #9

challenges.content: It is perhaps for this reason that many believe that,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #10

challenges.content: rather than storing the carbon dioxide as a gas,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #11

challenges.content: it is better to react it with metal oxides, such as magnesium or calcium,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #12

challenges.content: which results in the formation of a hard carbonate material.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #13

challenges.content: The gas is, in effect, turned into a stable and unreactive solid,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #14

challenges.content: which can simply be dumped anywhere.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #15

challenges.content: This process actually occurs naturally, although very very slowly,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #16

challenges.content: and is one cause of the surface limestone in the world.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #17

challenges.content: But this slow reaction speed is the problem.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #18

challenges.content: Even when enhancing this process through high temperature and pressure,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #19

challenges.content: or pre-treatment of the mineral, it is still far too slow to be economical.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #20

challenges.content: One other technique which has been suggested is to pump the gas to the bottom of the ocean,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #21

challenges.content: where it would react with compounds in the seawater, forming carbonic acid.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #22

challenges.content: However, this alternative has now been ruled out.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #23

challenges.content: The CO2 may be removed from the atmosphere,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #24

challenges.content: but the high oceanic acidity which would result raises its own set of problems,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #25

challenges.content: mostly with all the delicate life and the intricate food chains in the seawater,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #26

challenges.content: some on which we ourselves depend,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #27

challenges.content: and that's something which no one wants to experiment with.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #28

challenges.content: Perhaps because of the lack of alternatives,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #29

challenges.content: the most commonly discussed solution to the problem of disposing of carbon dioxide is to pump the gas underground -
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #30

challenges.content: a technique known as 'geosequestration'.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #31

challenges.content: In this system, the CO2, for example,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #32

challenges.content: could be pumped into underground pockets within depleted oil wells, or disused coal tunnels.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #33

challenges.content: This carries, however, three serious disadvantages,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #34

challenges.content: namely: the risk of leaks, the considerable costs involved,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #35

challenges.content: and finally, the unproven effectiveness.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #36

challenges.content: Let us look at those three disadvantages in detail.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #37

challenges.content: Firstly, there is the risk of leaks.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #38

challenges.content: Although the gas would be deep and sealed over by masses of rock and earth,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #39

challenges.content: the huge pressures in these spaces would turn the gas into a liquid state
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #40

challenges.content: capable of moving through rock fissures or faults.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #41

challenges.content: This could allow the gas to eventually be released to the surface.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #42

challenges.content: Since CO2 is heavier than air,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #43

challenges.content: and thus pushes oxygen aside,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #44

challenges.content: such leaks could result in the suffocation of thousands, or tens of thousands of people -
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #45

challenges.content: certainly not a consequence to be taken lightly.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #46

challenges.content: Natural CO2 leakage from volcanic build-up has already witnessed such deadly events.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #47

challenges.content: The other problem of geosequestration is the cost.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #48

challenges.content: The time and effort spent on materials and construction,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #49

challenges.content: primarily the pipework through which the gas would travel, does not come cheaply.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #50

challenges.content: So, if this system were to be implemented in, say, coal-fired power plants,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #51

challenges.content: the extra cost would have to be paid by the electricity user,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #52

challenges.content: whose bills would almost double as a consequence.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #53

challenges.content: Few people are prepared to pay this much simply to make a small dent on the effects of global warming.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #54

challenges.content: And this leads to the final problem.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #55

challenges.content: The most basic question is whether geosequestration actually reduces global warming.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #56

challenges.content: The problem here is that the energy needed to create
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #57

challenges.content: and drive the sequestration process would require approximately
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #58

challenges.content: a quarter of a coal-fired electricity plant's output.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #59

challenges.content: In other words, the plant would have to burn one quarter more of its coal
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #60

challenges.content: just to account for the sequestration of the carbon dioxide,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #61

challenges.content: and with coal producing other noxious pollutants,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #62

challenges.content: such as sulphur, ash, and heavy metals,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #63

challenges.content: the environment is hardly benefited at all.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #64

challenges.content: Nevertheless, there are many active experimental efforts underway,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #65

challenges.content: primarily in oil production sites.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #66

challenges.content: These are small but intensively monitored and analysed.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #67

challenges.content: All we can say now is that the jury is still out on whether underground carbon storage will one day be feasible.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 4 - challenge #68

challenges.content: Hi, Nicole.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #1

challenges.content: As you know, we've got to decide on the best ways this university can reduce its waste.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #2

challenges.content: You inspected the eastern campus, and I did the western buildings.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #3

challenges.content: Did you do all the interviews as well?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #4

challenges.content: Yes, I interviewed all the staff, who made some good observations,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #5

challenges.content: and I interviewed some of the students.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #6

challenges.content: The students said little that was interesting.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #7

challenges.content: They don't seem to care that much.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #8

challenges.content: It was the cleaners, surprisingly, who revealed the most relevant facts.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #9

challenges.content: That's not surprising to me.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #10

challenges.content: They empty all the bins, so they see the waste first-hand,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #11

challenges.content: whereas the staff just throw things away without thinking.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #12

challenges.content: What item was most commonly disposed of?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #13

challenges.content: Well, it really depended on where I interviewed.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #14

challenges.content: In the cafeteria precinct,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #15

challenges.content: obviously paper plates and cups were thrown away all over the place.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #16

challenges.content: There was almost no attempt at recycling.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #17

challenges.content: However, across the university in general,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #18

challenges.content: it was paper copying that filled up most bins,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #19

challenges.content: far more than plastic, or other forms of waste.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #20

challenges.content: Do people care about this, then?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #21

challenges.content: Well, some do, if you can believe them.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #22

challenges.content: I must have interviewed about 30% of customers in the cafeteria,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #23

challenges.content: and the results were mixed.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #24

challenges.content: Out of all the people I interviewed, well over half,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #25

challenges.content: maybe about 55% of them, were quite honest about it,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #26

challenges.content: telling me that they had little concern.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #27

challenges.content: The other fraction, 45%, were more troubled.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #28

challenges.content: Yes, but do they do anything about it?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #29

challenges.content: Surprisingly, quite a significant percentage do do something,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #30

challenges.content: even if they aren't particularly concerned.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #31

challenges.content: I mean, small things.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #32

challenges.content: About 10% bring their own cups to the cafeteria, for example,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #33

challenges.content: and at least 1/3 said they use recycling bins,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #34

challenges.content: so, in total, it's an equal split between those who do something, or those who don't.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #35

challenges.content: So why do so many people remain inactive,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #36

challenges.content: particularly over an issue they should care about more?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #37

challenges.content: I think they do care, and many of them are prepared to do something.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #38

challenges.content: Obviously, there's an element of laziness,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #39

challenges.content: but I'd say that it's relatively small.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #40

challenges.content: If they knew what to do, and if stringent systems existed,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #41

challenges.content: or if the importance of this was made clearer to them,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #42

challenges.content: I'm sure you'd see a much larger percentage of people actively working towards helping our environment.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #43

challenges.content: Well, there's cause for optimism, at least.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #44

challenges.content: Clearly then, there's a significant waste of paper here at this university,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #45

challenges.content: so I've worked out one practical suggestion which could help reduce it -
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #46

challenges.content: specifically, the waste from the excess photocopying.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #47

challenges.content: Let me hear it, then.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #48

challenges.content: Ah obviously, for a start,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #49

challenges.content: we've got to ensure that people, including the staff,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #50

challenges.content: without exception, copy both sides of a page.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #51

challenges.content: We can't tolerate single-sided copying. It's just far too wasteful.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #52

challenges.content: Absolutely. Just more trees being chopped down.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #53

challenges.content: But as people are doing copying,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #54

challenges.content: there may be adjustments, and practice copying,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #55

challenges.content: producing single-sided copies or blank pages not wanted and not intended for use.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #56

challenges.content: These need to be deposited into a tray for intended recycling -
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #57

challenges.content: you know, for recopying onto the blank side of the page.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #58

challenges.content: But people don't usually do that.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #59

challenges.content: I'm afraid it's just human nature.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #60

challenges.content: No matter how unimportant the copying is, they prefer to use fresh paper.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #61

challenges.content: Yeah, I agree with you,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #62

challenges.content: which is why you need to display these papers right in front of everyone,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #63

challenges.content: with a clear sign, 'Please Reuse', to make it easy for them to do so.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #64

challenges.content: They still won't do it.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #65

challenges.content: I know. That's why you take some of these papers, and regularly stack them inside the copier,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #66

challenges.content: in a special tray, once a day, say, in the morning.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #67

challenges.content: Well, that's getting better, making it easier for them to use the paper,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #68

challenges.content: but still, I'm afraid many won't.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #69

challenges.content: That's why you allow everyone to select this tray when copying.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #70

challenges.content: You distribute numbers or codes to every person,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #71

challenges.content: giving them special access to this recycling tray.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #72

challenges.content: Every time they use papers from this, it's tallied up to their account.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #73

challenges.content: I know I'm sounding a bit negative, or even cynical here...
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #74

challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #76

challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #77

challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 3 - challenge #78

challenges.content: Hello, everyone. Now, you know why I'm here.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 2 - challenge #1

challenges.content: You all work in a factory, and in this environment,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 2 - challenge #2

challenges.content: there always remains a significant possibility of accidents happening,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 2 - challenge #3

challenges.content: in which case, first aid will be necessary.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 2 - challenge #4

challenges.content: What is first aid?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 2 - challenge #5

challenges.content: It is the provision of emergency on-site care when an injury occurs,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 2 - challenge #6

challenges.content: and it is essential for everyone to know, if only simply, the steps which must be followed.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 2 - challenge #7

challenges.content: There are, of course, minor injuries which may happen,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 2 - challenge #8

challenges.content: not needing further medical care beyond the intervention of the first-aider,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 2 - challenge #9

challenges.content: but you can never be sure, thus the following steps must always be followed.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 2 - challenge #10

challenges.content: These can be abbreviated to the words "Dr ABC",
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 2 - challenge #11

challenges.content: in other words. D-R-A-B-C.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 2 - challenge #12

challenges.content: The 'D' stands for "danger", and that's the first issue to keep in mind.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 2 - challenge #13

challenges.content: When an accident happens, immediately ascertain that the environment is safe -
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 2 - challenge #14

challenges.content: that, for example, nothing else will fall or break or cause accidents.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 2 - challenge #15

challenges.content: If you, the first-aider, are also injured, the problem is even worse.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 2 - challenge #16

challenges.content: The 'R' stands for 'respond'.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 2 - challenge #17

challenges.content: You must then ascertain the best response.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 2 - challenge #18

challenges.content: Once all the danger has been eliminated, and the distress calls sent out,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 2 - challenge #19

challenges.content: the appropriate action is, obviously, to help the injured party.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 2 - challenge #20

challenges.content: Alright, that leads to 'A', which stands for "airway".
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 2 - challenge #21

challenges.content: In order to stay alive, all people need to have an open airway to allow breathing.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 2 - challenge #22

challenges.content: A conscious person will automatically clear their own airway,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 2 - challenge #23

challenges.content: but if unconscious, this may not happen.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 2 - challenge #24

challenges.content: The brain is stopped or hindered from properly directing the body
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 2 - challenge #25

challenges.content: and, obviously, in the worst case, death can result,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 2 - challenge #26

challenges.content: for this reason, the injured person is normally put into the 'recovery' position -
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 2 - challenge #27

challenges.content: placed on the side, tilting the head back, and ensuring that there are no blockages in the mouth.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 2 - challenge #28

challenges.content: To free any such blockages, the back can be slapped,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 2 - challenge #29

challenges.content: or the chest compressed, allowing anything to be spat out.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 2 - challenge #30

challenges.content: Now that the airway is free, check for 'B' or 'breathing'.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 2 - challenge #31

challenges.content: If breathing is not happening, or is irregular,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 2 - challenge #32

challenges.content: the first-aider may have to assist with what is technically known as cardiopulmonary resuscitation,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 2 - challenge #33

challenges.content: or more commonly, CPR.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 2 - challenge #34

challenges.content: This involves breathing for the patient, through mouth-to-mouth contact,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 2 - challenge #35

challenges.content: while periodically massaging the heart through compressions to the chest.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 2 - challenge #36

challenges.content: This combination allows blood, and oxygen, to flow around the body, keeping the patient alive,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 2 - challenge #37

challenges.content: hopefully until medics, such as doctors, advanced first-aiders, or ambulance staff, arrive.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 2 - challenge #38

challenges.content: Now, it's certainly good to have knowledge of emergency first aid
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 2 - challenge #39

challenges.content: but. obviously, the best situation is simply not to have accidents occur in the first place,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 2 - challenge #40

challenges.content: for that, you need to be aware of safety issues,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 2 - challenge #41

challenges.content: but just saying "be aware" does not usually achieve much.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 2 - challenge #42

challenges.content: It is more important to have an appointed person whose job is to ensure awareness and work-safety.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 2 - challenge #43

challenges.content: Safety inspections would obviously be part of their job,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 2 - challenge #44

challenges.content: whereby they can make sure, for example, that the first-aid boxes are fully equipped.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 2 - challenge #45

challenges.content: Another idea is to put posters on the walls,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 2 - challenge #46

challenges.content: but, interestingly, research has proven that these tend to be ignored,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 2 - challenge #47

challenges.content: becoming just part of the wallpaper - seen, but not put into practice.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 2 - challenge #48

challenges.content: It is much better if everyone is just instilled to not be reckless,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 2 - challenge #49

challenges.content: that is, to not rush into situations without thinking about the possibility of accidents,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 2 - challenge #50

challenges.content: and instilling this mindset is part of the job of the safety officer.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 2 - challenge #51

challenges.content: Some other suggestions are ongoing first-aid training,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 2 - challenge #52

challenges.content: and "no accident" reward or star systems.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 2 - challenge #53

challenges.content: These have had some success, but nothing beats a regular meeting, say, once a month,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 2 - challenge #54

challenges.content: in which the subject of safety is brought to the attention of everyone,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 2 - challenge #55

challenges.content: and any outstanding issues related to this are thoroughly discussed.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 2 - challenge #56

challenges.content: Let's go for a picnic.
That's a great idea! Where shall we go?
Let's go to the park.
How far is it?
About a mile.
Is it a nice place?
Sure. It has picnic tables and a beautiful lake.
Good. I'll make some sandwiches.
I'll bring soda and cookies.
The kids will love it.
Now let's see... Vine Street is that way...
Yes, just turn left at this corner.
To Bridge Street?
Is that street Bridge Street?
Yes. There is a sign. Can you see that?
Oh, you're right. Well, I have to go to Jay Street.
I think the next one is Jay Street.
Oh, right. Let's turn left at the next corner.
Diana! This street is College Street, not Jay Street.
Oh... uh, go straight ahead one more block!
Are you sure? It's already 4:20!
I should have taken a cab!
That's gratitude for you!
Come in... come in. It's Miss Wallace, isn't it?
Yes, that's right. How do you do?
How do you do? Please take a seat.
Thank you very much.
Well, I've got your application form here.
I just want to check the information... is that all right?
Yes, of course.
Now, you're 28, aren't you?
Yes, I am.
And you aren't married, are you?
No, I'm not... yet; I'm engaged.
Uh, huh. You didn't go to university?
No, I didn't, but I went to technical college.
And I started work when I was 20.
I see. You can speak Spanish, can't you?
Yes, I can... but I can write it better than I can speak it.
Is there any other language you can speak?
Yes, I can speak a little French.
You've been to Argentina, haven't you?
Yes, I have... and to France.
So I see... but you haven't been to the Middle East, have you?
No, I'm afraid I haven't, but I'd like to.
Good, because there is a demand for multi-lingual people in this job.
I think you will do just fine!
Thank you so much! I won't disappoint you!
Raymond!
Oh, hi, Grace! How have you been?
Good! I hear you've been to Toronto for a few days.
Yes. I just got back yesterday.
Did you have a nice visit?
Really nice. It was very good going around downtown and shopping.
And I saw the Toronto Blue Jays game at Skydome.
It seems that Toronto is a very exciting city.
My brother Stanley was there, too.
You've met Stanley, haven't you?
Sure. I met him when he was here in Hamilton last year.
What's he doing these days? Still teaching baseball?
Yes, as a matter of fact, he just began to teach elementary school.
Great. How's everything with his kids?
Have you met my nieces?
Yes, they visited you once in the summer, didn't they?
Right. They're both fine.
I haven't seen them in a long time. They must be really big.
Well, they will come over this Christmas.
Let's have a great Christmas party together.
That's a good idea.
Teresa! What a surprise! What are you doing here?
Timothy! I don't believe it!
I'm going to see my daughter. She will marry this weekend. How about you?
I'm going to visit my parents.
When is your daughter's wedding?
Sunday.
Wow! This Sunday is the 45th wedding anniversary of their wedding, too.
This is a surprise!
Anyway, where is your train leaving from?
My train leaves from Platform 3, over there.
How long will you...
Now leaving from Platform 3, train for Vancouver.
That's my train. I have to run. Sorry we didn't get more time to talk.
That's OK. I'll see you when you get back.
Have a good time, and say congratulations to your parents!
Have you heard about the good news in the Wallace family?
No, I've been out of town.
Mrs Wallace went into the hospital last night and gave birth to a baby girl seven hours later.
That's very good. But they already have a little girl, don't they?
No, they have a 5-year-old boy.
So they wanted a girl this time, right?
Yes, they wanted a girl for a long time.
Was it natural childbirth?
No, she had to have a caesarean.
Did you hear about the Smith family?
No, what happened?
Mrs. Smith passed away this morning.
That's a shame. What from?
Heart attack, I think.
That's a terrible thing.
Yes. Mrs Smith went into hospital last night by ambulance and died this morning.
Had she been suffering from heart disease?
Yeah. Mrs Smith had it for five years before she died.
Did they try surgery?
She had two operations, but they weren't effective.
I feel sorry for Mr. Smith.
Do you smoke? I've never known that.
When did you start smoking?
I started smoking when I was eighteen.
So, how long have you been a smoker?
I've smoked for twenty years.
How many cigarettes do you smoke a day?
I smoke two packs of cigarettes a day.
Have you ever tried to quit?
Yes, I have quit twice: once when I was expecting my baby, Paul,
and the other time when I had a bad sore throat.
But I had a hard time.
If you knew what it was doing to your lungs,
you would think twice about it!
Hello?
Sandy? Is that you?
Yes, uh-huh. Who's this?
It's Gill.
Gill? Gill who?
What do you mean, "Gill who?" Gill Dixon, of course.
Oh, Gill, I'm sorry.
Yes. We had a date last night.
Where were you? I waited for one hour.
Oh, I'm sorry, Gill. I couldn't come.
Couldn't come! Why not?
Well, I had to pack my stuff for my trip.
Why didn't you call me?
I wanted to call you, but... uh... I couldn't remember your phone number.
And now I'm going to forget yours!
Mr. Adams, have you seen this ad in the Recruit News?
Yes, I saw it, but I'm not interested in finding a new job.
I've been here since I graduated from my university.
I like working here.
Really? I've only been here one year, and I'm already tired of doing the same thing every day.
I'm afraid of getting really bored.
Oh, come on! It's not that bad.
Wherever you work, you have to do the same thing every day to a certain degree.
Well, what's more, I've been working about ten hours a day since last month.
But you've been getting paid more money for it, haven't you?
Yes, but I'm not interested in making more money.
I'm going to apply for another job.
What kind of job?
A secretarial job.
Well, good luck.
Thank you very much!
I thought that movie was terrific, didn't you?
I don't know. It didn't seem to have any meaning.
Come on. It seems that you expect intellectual stimulation from every movie.
challenges.explanation: intellectual stimulation: something that makes you think

challenges.content: I just think that a good movie should have a central theme at least.
Yes. But it doesn't hurt you to watch a funny movie once in a while.
Relax and enjoy it!
You're right. I'm too serious sometimes.
Are you ready?
Grace is still in her room.
She needs to rush. We don't have enough time.
What time does the movie begin?
It starts at 7:30.
What's the time now?
About 7:10.
There's no hurry. It only takes ten minutes by car to get there.
I know, but there aren't enough parking spaces around the theatre.
Well, I'd better tell Grace to hurry up.
She can take hours to get ready.
Can I get some tickets for plays?
Yes. Is there a specific play that you want to see?
What plays are on tonight?
Cats. But it's sold out.
Are there any seats left for tomorrow night?
Yes. How many tickets do you want?
Two, please.
Where would you like to sit?
I'm not sure.
Well, here's a seating plan of the concert hall.
How much is it in the middle section?
$50! That's a little too expensive for us.
How much is it in the back?
That's fine. What time does the play start?
At 7 o'clock.
What time will the play be over?

Hello.
Where do you wanna go?
70 Maple Street, please.
70 Mibble Street?
No, Maple street.
Maple Street... let's see...
Is that near St. David Street?
I don't know. I've only been here one week.
Oh, where are you from?
Toronto.
Can you help me, officer?
I'll try. What's the problem?
I can't get into my car.
Where are your keys?
They're in the car.

How can you do that?
With a coat hanger. It's easy.
Where can we get a coat hanger?
There's one in the police car. Wait here.

11:30 I'm going now. Bye.

Ah-choo!
God bless you!

You have a cold?

To pay for her education?

challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #1

challenges.content: Can I just talk to you about something?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #2

challenges.content: Our new flatmate - Anders - is not quite what I had hoped
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #3

challenges.content: I was wondering if you shared my concerns about some of his behaviour.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #4

challenges.content: Ah, yes, Tom, I know what you mean, but we can't be entirely negative.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #5

challenges.content: He has good points. I mean, at least he's quiet.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #6

challenges.content: He doesn't play loud music all night, or bother others, or turn his TV up, disturbing everyone.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #7

challenges.content: Sure, he's quiet, but remember our last flatmate?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #8

challenges.content: He'd say 'hi' to you, and smile, and treat everyone politely.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #9

challenges.content: In comparison, this new guy is very impolite.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #10

challenges.content: He just grunts in reply, and sometimes ignores me altogether.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #11

challenges.content: I guess that's just his way, y'know, just his character.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #12

challenges.content: I don't think he realises he's being impolite, and it shouldn't matter to us too much.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #13

challenges.content: We can just ignore him, too, and quietly live our own lives.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #14

challenges.content: But his friends are hard to ignore, when they visit.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #15

challenges.content: I know what you mean, but how often does that happen?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #16

challenges.content: I rarely see them, maybe once or twice a month.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #17

challenges.content: If they came more often, it might be a problem,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #18

challenges.content: but as it is, such rare visits don't matter so much.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #19

challenges.content: Wouldn't you say so?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #20

challenges.content: Well, I'm not sure, since it's very obvious when they're here because of all the cigarette smoke in the house.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #21

challenges.content: It stinks up the place, and you know we don't allow smoking on the premises.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #22

challenges.content: Well, I've never seen them doing this.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #23

challenges.content: Maybe they do it outside.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #24

challenges.content: Perhaps we can talk to Anders about it.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #25

challenges.content: Always remember, though, in one respect, he's a good tenant.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #26

challenges.content: And it's the most important aspect.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #27

challenges.content: The previous flatmate would always pay the rent late.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #28

challenges.content: I know what you're going to say. This guy pays promptly.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #29

challenges.content: But there's more to being a good tenant than prompt payment.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #30

challenges.content: I mean, you need to turn off the TV, clean up your dishes, dress respectably, be polite, and so on.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #31

challenges.content: I guess what I'm saying is that, basically, you need to co-operate with the others,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #32

challenges.content: and this new guy fails significantly in this respect.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #33

challenges.content: Okay, I suppose you have a point there.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #34

challenges.content: I tell you what, Tom, why don't we talk to our new flatmate, Anders, about these issues?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #35

challenges.content: If we throw him out, we'll have to go to all the trouble of finding another flatmate,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #36

challenges.content: who might not necessarily be much better.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #37

challenges.content: So, let's give the current guy a chance.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #38

challenges.content: Here. I've got a piece of paper, so let's make a short list of issues to discuss with him.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #39

challenges.content: Get it out into the open.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #40

challenges.content: Sure. We'll give him one more chance.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #41

challenges.content: So, write, 'Communication', and let's tell him to...
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #42

challenges.content: Well, we can't change a person's personality overnight,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #43

challenges.content: so why don't we have a weekly tenants' meeting, and we can just ask him to attend?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #44

challenges.content: That way we can get to know him better.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #45

challenges.content: I'll write 'attend meeting', and we can take it from there.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #46

challenges.content: Okay, but we have to tell him about his friends.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #47

challenges.content: They can't just do whatever they want.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #48

challenges.content: Write a heading 'friends' and then write 'don't smoke, anywhere, inside or outside'.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #49

challenges.content: Well, instead of being so direct, and possibly causing offense,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #50

challenges.content: I'll just write, 'follow rules',
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #51

challenges.content: and verbally mention the rules:
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #52

challenges.content: TV off by 10 pm, no loud music, or bad behaviour, including smoking.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #53

challenges.content: Okay, do that, but I still think we need to specifically mention that last issue.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #54

challenges.content: You know how I can't stand the habit,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #55

challenges.content: so I'd like this to be another and separate point. Cigarettes! Strictly forbidden!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #56

challenges.content: And it's important to include the 'strictly' here.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #57

challenges.content: We can't pussyfoot around too much.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #58

challenges.content: Sometimes directness is necessary.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #59

challenges.content: Okay, I'll write that... 'forbidden'...
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #60

challenges.content: Okay. And what about cleaning duties?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #61

challenges.content: Anders is a little too relaxed about that.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #62

challenges.content: Dishes are sometimes not washed, dirty tea cups are left around the place, and so on.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #63

challenges.content: So, write 'must do better!'
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #64

challenges.content: Yeah, again Tom, he might take that personally, and it could cause a scene.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #65

challenges.content: I'd rather be general. I'll write 'must be done'
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #66

challenges.content: and I'll tell him that that's for everyone, not just him. Okay?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #67

challenges.content: Okay. As long as he gets the message.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 6 - Part 1 - challenge #68

challenges.content: If you consider the farms of old - the type your father or grandfather grew up on,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #1

challenges.content: they were small and labour-intensive, requiring lots of workers.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #2

challenges.content: In addition, they often had a diversity of products,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #3

challenges.content: be that animal or vegetable - say, cows and sheep,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #4

challenges.content: or oranges and lemons, with some peaches,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #5

challenges.content: and a few chickens on the side, for the production of eggs.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #6

challenges.content: The many workers involved raised their families, who needed products and support services,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #7

challenges.content: such as medical clinics and schools,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #8

challenges.content: so the small country towns had mercantile activity,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #9

challenges.content: store fronts, and community participation, with all ages present and a distinct town culture.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #10

challenges.content: And how it has changed!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #11

challenges.content: Travel to any small country town in virtually any developed country,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #12

challenges.content: and you will often see that these places are now somewhat forlorn and deserted,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #13

challenges.content: lacking life and vigour.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #14

challenges.content: Many of the residents have long since moved towards the big cities,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #15

challenges.content: so the country areas have become depopulated, and their downtowns empty.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #16

challenges.content: This phenomenon is so predictable and widespread that it even has a name,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #17

challenges.content: rural flight, or rural exodus,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #18

challenges.content: and it has produced some fairly predictable problems.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #19

challenges.content: As for the causes of rural exodus, the most obvious is the industrialisation of agriculture.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #20

challenges.content: This comes in two aspects,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #21

challenges.content: one of them being monocultural farming practices.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #22

challenges.content: What this means is that it is now more efficient to have one product, and focus on its needs almost exclusively.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #23

challenges.content: So, for example, animal husbandry will usually involve a single type of animal, say pigs,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #24

challenges.content: but with huge factory farming techniques,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #25

challenges.content: or, in other words, the second aspect: economies of scale.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #26

challenges.content: This means instead of 200 pigs, there'll be 2000,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #27

challenges.content: tightly fitted into small pens or cages,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #28

challenges.content: with high density waste disposal and automatic feeding systems.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #29

challenges.content: Yet despite this huge size, it can all be controlled by just a dozen farm workers pushing the right button.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #30

challenges.content: You might not like it, but in a competitive market,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #31

challenges.content: the cheaper the overheads, the better, and one can't argue with market economics.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #32

challenges.content: It's simply the way of the modern world,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #33

challenges.content: and it has changed the face of rural districts, mostly for the worst.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #34

challenges.content: We can talk at length about the problem of rural exodus, but what about solutions?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #35

challenges.content: Well, there is certainly some cause for hope,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #36

challenges.content: since many are now feeling the negatives of increasing urbanisation,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #37

challenges.content: negatives which the countryside generally does not have.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #38

challenges.content: Thus, tourism, for example, is certainly one avenue of revenue and revitalisation.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #39

challenges.content: The most important consideration here is that the local residents themselves participate in developing such initiatives,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #40

challenges.content: and deciding what happens, since outsiders, be they state government or city-based planners,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #41

challenges.content: do not fully understand the local settings,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #42

challenges.content: the possibilities which may be on offer, or the town culture,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #43

challenges.content: since even small rural areas can be highly distinctive from neighbouring ones.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #44

challenges.content: For example, the Daylesford area has developed a tourist industry based on the natural springs there,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #45

challenges.content: putting forward the angle that this water is relaxing and revitalising for the health.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #46

challenges.content: There has been the development of spas, saunas, and small-scale accommodation within its picturesque hillsides.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #47

challenges.content: And another solution is to utilise the predominant local product.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #48

challenges.content: This takes advantage of the fact that many city-people are developing a dislike for factory-produce and packaged foodstuffs.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #49

challenges.content: They are becoming interested in products that can be sold directly to them, at a cheaper price,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #50

challenges.content: while preserving all the freshness from the tree or animal.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #51

challenges.content: It is important here that the country area is not only characterised by a specific product,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #52

challenges.content: but markets this idea well.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #53

challenges.content: For example, many areas of country Victoria have developed widespread grape-growing and winemaking facilities,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #54

challenges.content: and encourage wine tasting tourism -
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #55

challenges.content: now a thriving industry, with an international patronage.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #56

challenges.content: Similarly, Harcourt is famous for apples,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #57

challenges.content: Shepparton for mature cheeses,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #58

challenges.content: and Mildura for its citrus products.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #59

challenges.content: Such strategies, done well, give hope that rural areas can revitalise somewhat,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #60

challenges.content: and once again be lively and interesting places to live in.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 4 - challenge #61

challenges.content: Well gentlemen, we've almost finished our second semester at this university.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #1

challenges.content: What do you think of all the courses we attend?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #2

challenges.content: On the whole, I'd say they're quite good,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #3

challenges.content: apart from Social History, which I find to be a little too inexact.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #4

challenges.content: Yes, the lecturer's style is also very very dull.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #5

challenges.content: I certainly agree with you there,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #6

challenges.content: although I would say that the textbook is more interesting. 'Welfare State'.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #7

challenges.content: The subtitle says, 'An examination of social development in the 20th century.'
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #8

challenges.content: Yes, 'Welfare State' is a good book, but look how many pages it has.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #9
IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #10

challenges.content: I agree. It's just too long to be easily read.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #11

challenges.content: Far too long, although it's certainly well written in parts.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #12

challenges.content: Yes, and if you compare it to the textbook for Cultural Studies, what's it called?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #13

challenges.content: 'Inner Views', I think.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #14

challenges.content: No, that's the book for Media Studies, and we finished that subject last semester.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #15

challenges.content: The book you're thinking of is 'In Perspective'.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #16

challenges.content: Sorry, you're right. 'In Perspective'.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #17

challenges.content: And the subtitle says, 'A comparison of social groups.'
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #18

challenges.content: Somewhat interesting, wouldn't you say?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #19

challenges.content: Well, mildly so, as is the subject,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #20

challenges.content: dealing as it does with such a wide variety of issues,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #21

challenges.content: but the book itself certainly oversimplifies a very complex subject.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #22

challenges.content: I agree. I also got annoyed at its constant oversimplification.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #23

challenges.content: Life is more complicated than what it suggests.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #24

challenges.content: Yes, but what you call 'oversimplifying' may well be considered 'clarifying'.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #25

challenges.content: Look at this other textbook, 'Government in Action'.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #26

challenges.content: Some may say that it also oversimplifies,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #27

challenges.content: but it must do so in order to present a coherent picture of an equally complex subject.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #28

challenges.content: 'Government in Action'? Which subject...?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #29

challenges.content: It's the textbook for 'Political Theory'.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #30

challenges.content: Oh, I hate politics.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #31

challenges.content: That's why I don't like the 'Active Leadership' subject, either.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #32

challenges.content: And most of the stuff in that 'Political Theory' textbook is based on the American system.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #33

challenges.content: You see, it's written by Americans, so it's not even relevant to us here.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #34

challenges.content: I'd agree with you there,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #35

challenges.content: it's not relevant to us at all, since our government uses the Westminster system.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #36

challenges.content: Yes, I suppose that is a problem.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #37

challenges.content: Well, it seems we all have certain criticisms about the textbooks we're using,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #38

challenges.content: but at the same time, we all like some elements, at least, of the subjects we're studying.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #39

challenges.content: What's your favourite subject, David?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #40

challenges.content: I'm not sure. I like Political Theory, but...
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #41

challenges.content: Cultural Studies is by far the best, even better than Political Theory,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #42

challenges.content: which I also like, but just not as much.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #43

challenges.content: Why do you say that, Steve?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #44

challenges.content: I was thinking, perhaps, Social History is worth considering as best.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #45

challenges.content: Social History is good, but I made my choice because the subject is relevant to this modern society.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #46

challenges.content: But so is Social History, and I like the historical element,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #47

challenges.content: which the other subjects lack.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #48

challenges.content: Even Political Theory examines history only briefly, and in a very narrow way,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #49

challenges.content: so I'd say Social History is the most rewarding for me.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #50

challenges.content: What about you, Susan?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #51

challenges.content: I think Social History is certainly very good,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #52

challenges.content: but Political Theory is, in fact, the best,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #53

challenges.content: since basically, every human system boils down to politics.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #54

challenges.content: So, despite a certain irrelevancy in the details,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #55

challenges.content: the basic message remains as relevant as ever.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #56

challenges.content: Oh Susan, you can't be serious.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #57

challenges.content: Let's ask Olive, again.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #58

challenges.content: She's over there.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #59

challenges.content: Olive! Which subject do you think is the best?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #60

challenges.content: Ah, a difficult question.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #61

challenges.content: I'm very interested in culture,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #62

challenges.content: so Cultural Studies is certainly my cup of tea,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #63

challenges.content: but I'm politically active also, and hope to pursue this as a career,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #64

challenges.content: so Political Theory would be the one I'd pick.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #65

challenges.content: I don't believe it. Even with that irrelevant textbook?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #66

challenges.content: Don't listen to him, Olive; you have a right to your own opinion.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 3 - challenge #67

challenges.content: Hello there.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #1

challenges.content: I was asked to tell you about the extent of the damage to the main building, caused by the recent storm.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #2

challenges.content: Oh, that's right. I take it that most of the damage is just to the main building?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #3

challenges.content: It is indeed, since the building is so old.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #4

challenges.content: However, luckily, the damage is minor,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #5

challenges.content: and all of it can be fixed in one day, given that we have five people in our team.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #6

challenges.content: What will you be doing first? I understand you start at 8 in the morning.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #7

challenges.content: That's right,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #8

challenges.content: and we were going to remove the fallen tree,
