challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #9

challenges.content: but we've been told there are exams that morning,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #10

challenges.content: and I'm sure the sound of those saws and other heavy equipment will disturb all the students,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #11

challenges.content: so instead we'll fix that leaky roof.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #12

challenges.content: That's a 4-hou job, since it involves substantial repair,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #13

challenges.content: not like fixing broken windows, which can be done quite quickly.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #14

challenges.content: So you'll fix the broken window after that, from midday?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #15

challenges.content: We could do that,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #16

challenges.content: but since we'll be working in the ceiling, it's more logical to get rid of those birds' nests there.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #17

challenges.content: It's a small job but will require crawling inside the ceiling cavity,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #18

challenges.content: which is not an easy exercise, so that will take about an hour.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #19

challenges.content: But this is good, since by that time the exams should be over,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #20

challenges.content: and we can address that tree which has been blown over,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #21

challenges.content: after our 1-hour lunch break of course.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #22

challenges.content: It will be quite noisy dealing with that, but it will be finished by three o'clock.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #23

challenges.content: Some of our staff will then leave to fix things on another site,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #24

challenges.content: an office nearby needs a new window,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #25

challenges.content: but two of us, including myself, will remain here to paint over that discoloured patch of wall in your office.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #26

challenges.content: Oh good, it looks so horrible at the moment.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #27

challenges.content: Well, we'll certainly make it look good once again,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #28

challenges.content: and in the last hour of our working day, we'll fix up that problem with the wiring.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #29

challenges.content: Apparently the power doesn't go to one of the classrooms.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #30

challenges.content: Probably some water has gotten into the fuse box,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #31

challenges.content: so we'll just change a few wires, and clean up the moisture, and it should be fine.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #32

challenges.content: I certainly appreciate all the effort you and your team are taking to fix things here,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #33

challenges.content: but I do have one request.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #34

challenges.content: And what is that?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #35

challenges.content: You said you're going to paint the back wall in my office.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #36

challenges.content: Will it be the same colour as before?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #37

challenges.content: Yes, we'll make it a nice white colour.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #38

challenges.content: Well that's the point. I'd prefer it to be yellow, to match the furniture.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #39

challenges.content: The furniture is orange, actually, but I think yellow is a nice match.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #40

challenges.content: Can you do that?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #41

challenges.content: We can certainly do that. Yellow it is.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #42

challenges.content: Certainly a prettier colour than just plain white,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #43

challenges.content: or the blue in my kitchen at home for that matter.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #44

challenges.content: And we can leave the paint can with you, in case you need to do some touch-ups,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #45

challenges.content: or if the stain reappears.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #46

challenges.content: I'll just leave it in the garden shed, the one next to the main classroom.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #47

challenges.content: And incidentally, about those birds in the ceiling.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #48

challenges.content: I was just investigating, and I heard the chirping of little baby birds in there,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #49

challenges.content: so there must be some young ones in a nest.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #50

challenges.content: I just thought you'd like to know that we can give them to a wildlife reserve.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #51

challenges.content: There's one in the next suburb, so that should not be too much trouble.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #52

challenges.content: Or you could give them to one of our teachers.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #53

challenges.content: I have a colleague who can raise them.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #54

challenges.content: I would say the wildlife reserve is a better option,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #55

challenges.content: since the people there are used to dealing with animals,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #56

challenges.content: and as for that fallen tree, we'll cut it up into small pieces
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #57

challenges.content: and that can be firewood in my house, so that won't be wasted either,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #58

challenges.content: although the smoke will cause some pollution,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #59

challenges.content: but I have a special licence for my fireplace, so no one can object to that.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #60

challenges.content: I've noticed also that the university has a garden bin, for the smaller items,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #61

challenges.content: leaves and sticks and bark, and so on,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #62

challenges.content: so we can dispose of material in that, also.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #63

challenges.content: You do have some waste piles out the back,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #64

challenges.content: but a proper garden bin means that the material will be recycled,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #65

challenges.content: and that's better for the environment, so you can rest assured we will use that.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 2 - challenge #66

challenges.content: Okay, Ella. As you know, the deadline for this project is the end of the month, so we'd better plan it well.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #1

challenges.content: Yes, I've already been thinking along those lines,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #2

challenges.content: and I've decided we should divide this project into three phases:
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #3

challenges.content: the Pre-phase, then Phase 1, and then Phase 2,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #4

challenges.content: with strict deadlines involved for each one.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #5

challenges.content: Given that we have to finish this quickly, that sounds good. Tell me more.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #6

challenges.content: The Pre-phase is the simplest.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #7

challenges.content: We just need to allocate a space or a place to do our planning,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #8

challenges.content: and this space will need to be quite big.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #9

challenges.content: Sure, and we have to decide on the equipment needed as well.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #10

challenges.content: Remember the last project, when we didn't have enough projectors to present our ideas?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #11

challenges.content: We lost lots of time there.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #12

challenges.content: Yes, that was a bad start.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #13

challenges.content: That's why, after the Pre-phase is finished, I've allocated a mere three days for Phase One.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #14

challenges.content: That will involve drawing the plans.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #15

challenges.content: We'll need Jenna to help us.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #16

challenges.content: And Marco.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #17

challenges.content: Yes, but not Susan.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #18

challenges.content: Susan is just far too busy to participate, as much as I'd like her in the team.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #19

challenges.content: Let's just take Fred instead. He'll do.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #20

challenges.content: Sure. Fred's not as experienced as Greg, but I agree, he'll do fine for this job.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #21

challenges.content: Then it's straight into Phase 2, collecting, collating, analysing, and preparing the final report.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #22

challenges.content: Can we do that in five days?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #23

challenges.content: I think that's optimistic, which is why I scheduled six.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #24

challenges.content: That's almost a week! Do we have that much time?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #25

challenges.content: We do, and with the right people, six days should see the job done.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #26

challenges.content: Who are the people for this phase? Arthur and Rob, right?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #27

challenges.content: No, Arthur's got other things to do, and Rob's on leave,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #28

challenges.content: so Mike alone will be the main man on this part.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #29

challenges.content: He's done it before, so it should be fine.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #30

challenges.content: But he may need some help with the smaller tasks.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #31

challenges.content: Someone who is good with detail and procedures.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #32

challenges.content: Hmmm. Peter's not free at the moment, so I can arrange Leo to chip in some time and advice.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #33

challenges.content: Leo's very useful, particularly under pressure.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #34

challenges.content: And that's everything sorted!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #35

challenges.content: Well done Ella. This report should certainly be ready in time.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #36

challenges.content: Okay, Ella, you've done a good job with the basic time frame of this project, but what about specifics?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #37

challenges.content: What sort of specifics?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #38

challenges.content: Well, things like information gathering.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #39

challenges.content: Are we going to use questionnaires like we did last time?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #40

challenges.content: I was thinking of using the Internet to ask people to give their views,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #41

challenges.content: but you often get such silly responses when you do that.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #42

challenges.content: I'm of the view that the best way to find out things is to ask people directly,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #43

challenges.content: so that's what we'll do.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #44

challenges.content: Okay, but that will take longer.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #45

challenges.content: We'll probably even have to do some of the work at home.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #46

challenges.content: No, I don't think so, as long as we stay back at work for some after-hours meetings.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #47

challenges.content: Well, that's better than coming in early.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #48

challenges.content: No one functions well in the morning.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #49

challenges.content: Also, the final report will need at least two appendices.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #50

challenges.content: Not only that, we'll have to attach a small booklet to the end,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #51

challenges.content: containing printouts of the relevant parts from all the foreign websites we accessed.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #52

challenges.content: That will take even more time.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #53

challenges.content: Are you sure we can meet this deadline?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #54

challenges.content: Yep, I've worked it all out, and I'm confident we can do it.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #55

challenges.content: Phase 1 should be finished by the 5th,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #56

challenges.content: leaving Phase 2 to begin about the 8th or 9th.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #57

challenges.content: Now, there's a public holiday on the 10th,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #58

challenges.content: Meaning that everything should be able to be submitted on the 15th,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #59

challenges.content: and after that, we can relax,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #60

challenges.content: and celebrate on the 25th when the Design Division gives us approval to go ahead.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #61

challenges.content: Hah, you're assuming that the Design Division will approve this, and that's not guaranteed at all.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #62

challenges.content: Oh come on Marcus, be positive.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #63

challenges.content: You know this should be approved,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #64

challenges.content: in fact, I'm even planning the celebration when this is all over.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #65

challenges.content: Oh yeah, what's on the agenda, then?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #66

challenges.content: Well, we definitely don't want a party in the office, do we?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #67

challenges.content: We'll want to get away from this place,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #68

challenges.content: and we're all too busy with our own lives and families to find a mutual time free for a dinner party,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #69

challenges.content: so I thought we'd just buy some nice expensive gifts for everyone who participated.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #70

challenges.content: We can just give these to the people here in the office.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #71

challenges.content: That sounds fine to me, but make sure they're not too expensive.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #72

challenges.content: The Budget Department will never approve the cost.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #73

challenges.content: Don't worry; I know how much I can get away with.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #74

challenges.content: Alright. I'll leave that with you.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 5 - Part 1 - challenge #75

challenges.content: When considering the smallest unit of matter - the atom
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 4 - challenge #1

challenges.content: most people know of electrons, protons, and neutrons,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 4 - challenge #2

challenges.content: but almost none know of another particle,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 4 - challenge #3

challenges.content: even though they are constantly emitted from the sun in the trillions,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 4 - challenge #4

challenges.content: with 100 to 200 billion of them regularly passing through your body every second.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 4 - challenge #5

challenges.content: To repeat, that's not thousands, not millions, but billions, every second.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 4 - challenge #6

challenges.content: You don't feel them because they are small,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 4 - challenge #7

challenges.content: in fact, so tiny that we can barely detect their presence at all.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 4 - challenge #8

challenges.content: These mysterious particles are called neutrinos.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 4 - challenge #9

challenges.content: Despite such an abundance, detecting them is a huge undertaking,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 4 - challenge #10

challenges.content: and there are many reasons for this.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 4 - challenge #11

challenges.content: Firstly, the neutrino itself is so small that you need to eliminate absolutely all other particles around.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 4 - challenge #12

challenges.content: To do this, you need what is called a clean room,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 4 - challenge #13

challenges.content: one that has an extremely low level of dust, microbes, floating particles, or chemical vapours.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 4 - challenge #14

challenges.content: You probably don't know it, but the air around you right now has almost 40 million particles per cubic meter.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 4 - challenge #15

challenges.content: In contrast, the cleanest of clean rooms has less than 10.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 4 - challenge #16

challenges.content: The second problem is that you also need an environment with absolutely no background radiation.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 4 - challenge #17

challenges.content: At the surface of the Earth, such radiation is all around,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 4 - challenge #18

challenges.content: from the sun and sky, and from TVs and communication devices.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 4 - challenge #19

challenges.content: The only way to screen out all that is to go underground, and I mean deep underground.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 4 - challenge #20

challenges.content: For example, the Sudbury Neutrino Observatory in Canada uses an old nickel mine, one of the deepest in the world,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 4 - challenge #21

challenges.content: and puts the Observatory in its lowest tunnel, more than two kilometers below the surface.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 4 - challenge #22

challenges.content: At such depths, stray radiation is sufficiently screened out to allow neutrinos only to pass by.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 4 - challenge #23

challenges.content: The final problem is that you need an elaborate detection system,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 4 - challenge #24

challenges.content: and this apparatus is huge,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 4 - challenge #25

challenges.content: and its installation in this deep underground cavity presents quite a headache.
challenges.explanation: cavity: a hole, an empty space in a solid object
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 4 - challenge #26

challenges.content: Holding such a weighty construction safe and secure requires complex engineering work,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 4 - challenge #27

challenges.content: such as rock-bolting and support structuring.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 4 - challenge #28

challenges.content: This obviously requires great care, and takes a lot of effort.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 4 - challenge #29

challenges.content: So, I've told you about the difficulty in detecting neutrinos.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 4 - challenge #30

challenges.content: They are tiny, virtually weightless, have no electric charge,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 4 - challenge #31

challenges.content: and hardly interact with anything at all.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 4 - challenge #32

challenges.content: Yet we can detect them, and to see how, let's consider the Sudbury installation once again.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 4 - challenge #33

challenges.content: The detector there consists of a spherical container filled with heavy water.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 4 - challenge #34

challenges.content: This rests inside another vessel filled with normal water,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 4 - challenge #35

challenges.content: which helps support the weight of the inner sphere,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 4 - challenge #36

challenges.content: as well as providing further shielding from any stray radiation.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 4 - challenge #37

challenges.content: At the edge of this inner sphere are about 10,000 electronic detectors.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 4 - challenge #38

challenges.content: These are extremely sensitive, able to multiply a hundred million times any electric current which occurs.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 4 - challenge #39

challenges.content: So, as the neutrinos pass through this sphere of water,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 4 - challenge #40

challenges.content: there is a very very very small chance that one of them may hit a water molecule.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 4 - challenge #41

challenges.content: To increase the likelihood of this, two strategies are used.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 4 - challenge #42

challenges.content: One. the larger the sphere of water, the better,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 4 - challenge #43

challenges.content: and the Sudbury tank holds not 10 tons, not 100 tons, but 1000 tons.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 4 - challenge #44

challenges.content: Two, the water is special, consisting as it does of heavier molecules.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 4 - challenge #45

challenges.content: So, what happens is this.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 4 - challenge #46

challenges.content: If the neutrino hits the water molecule, the neutrino is absorbed,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 4 - challenge #47

challenges.content: but the molecule itself splits apart, producing a tiny electric current.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 4 - challenge #48

challenges.content: It is this which is detected, and analysed, giving key information about the neutrino.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 4 - challenge #49

challenges.content: The final question is why do we care about these elusive particles?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 4 - challenge #50

challenges.content: Well, just think,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 4 - challenge #51

challenges.content: they can pass right through the core of our sun at the speed of light without being affected or losing strength.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 4 - challenge #52

challenges.content: No other form of radiation can do that,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 4 - challenge #53

challenges.content: meaning that the knowledge we get about neutrinos can help us to control them.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 4 - challenge #54

challenges.content: With this ability, we can probe the centre of our Earth,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 4 - challenge #55

challenges.content: the inner layers of our sun, and the outer limits of our solar system,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 4 - challenge #56

challenges.content: and that makes it all worth the effort.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 4 - challenge #57

challenges.content: Hi, Emily. What did you think of that lecture?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #1

challenges.content: A bit hard to follow, but I have some good lecture-listening note-taking strategies which really help,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #2

challenges.content: so I can review the lecturer's message later.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #3

challenges.content: Lecture-listening note-taking strategies? Review it later?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #4

challenges.content: That sounds interesting.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #5

challenges.content: I must admit, I struggle a bit to take down the gist of what I hear.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #6

challenges.content: Look at my notes.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #7

challenges.content: Well, I can see a basic problem immediately.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #8

challenges.content: You're writing full words, such as 'century' when all you need is a 'C',
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #9

challenges.content: And don't write 'increase'; just draw an 'up' arrow.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #10

challenges.content: And why write 'thousand' when a 'th' will do?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #11

challenges.content: I see. Just use symbols. That's not a bad idea at all.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #12

challenges.content: It's the most basic strategy, allowing you to record information at a faster pace.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #13

challenges.content: These lecturers can talk faster than others, too,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #14

challenges.content: so you don't want to waste any time.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #15

challenges.content: But you need to be very familiar with your set of symbols.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #16

challenges.content: Why?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #17

challenges.content: Because you'll have to look at these notes days, weeks, or even months afterwards,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #18

challenges.content: when you begin writing your essay,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #19

challenges.content: so you'll need to be able to interpret them at a later stage.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #20

challenges.content: I think I can do this, even by looking at your notes.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #21

challenges.content: 'Immed' must mean immediately.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #22

challenges.content: But regarding the lecture as a whole,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #23

challenges.content: I knew the professor would be giving a set of specific recommendations,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #24

challenges.content: and comparing two alternative approaches, so I formatted my page in advance,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #25

challenges.content: adding the features consistent with the nature of what I was going to hear.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #26

challenges.content: I think I need an example of what you mean.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #27

challenges.content: Well, look at my page.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #28

challenges.content: Before the lecture, I drew large headings saying 'recommendations'.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #29

challenges.content: You should always draw these, and I drew a table saying, 'Approach 1' and 'Approach 2'.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #30

challenges.content: At the end I drew a flowchart,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #31

challenges.content: as obviously the final recommendation would be a step-by-step approach.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #32

challenges.content: Then I was prepared in advance to simply fill in the spaces.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #33

challenges.content: Wow! Now that's clever.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #34

challenges.content: Your advice about note taking sounds great, but I still have one question, Emily.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #35

challenges.content: How are you able to design your page in advance?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #36

challenges.content: I mean, how can you predict the nature of the talk,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #37

challenges.content: and know which design is likely to work best?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #38

challenges.content: It's rather obvious when you think about it.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #39

challenges.content: What's your next lecture about?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #40

challenges.content: Legal Studies.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #41

challenges.content: Well, that suggests to me that you'll need a flowchart,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #42

challenges.content: since the judicial system has a very logical 'do this first, do that second' approach,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #43

challenges.content: which must be followed in that order,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #44

challenges.content: y'know, all the processes that happen in the courtroom,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #45

challenges.content: and the procedures that must take place to ensure complete legality.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #46

challenges.content: Sure. That's the way law is, very linear and orderly,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #47

challenges.content: but what about Culture Studies?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #48

challenges.content: That's just a mass of comparisons of different cultures.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #49

challenges.content: Which tells you that you will need a table, where, in tabular form, you can efficiently write down information.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #50

challenges.content: But often the lecture's not that simple.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #51

challenges.content: The professor throws in a really complex mix of ideas.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #52

challenges.content: Then use a spider graph, like the web a spider makes,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #53

challenges.content: where there's a central idea around which you attach all the associated thoughts, and ideas, and impressions.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #54

challenges.content: I see. I think I understand.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #55

challenges.content: And that would be very quick, too; very efficient.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #56

challenges.content: I like that. But what about Management Theory?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #57

challenges.content: How would you approach that?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #58

challenges.content: The same as with Culture Studies.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #59

challenges.content: I'd use a network, which is basically the same as a spider graph, linking thoughts,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #60

challenges.content: although this time there are directions involved.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #61

challenges.content: It is this element that makes it different,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #62

challenges.content: the fact that the thoughts go one way and not the other.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #63

challenges.content: Okay... has directions.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #64

challenges.content: It sounds logical.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #65

challenges.content: What about the other subjects, such as Political Science?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #66

challenges.content: There's no predictable order to that.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #67

challenges.content: Well, for that I'd just put my notes in a line,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #68

challenges.content: that is, in linear, or straight-line fashion,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #69

challenges.content: and these notes would use symbols, of course, to save time.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #70

challenges.content: Okay, that just leaves Mass Media.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #71

challenges.content: For that, I wouldn't have any special design at all.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #72

challenges.content: As you say, sometimes it's impossible to predict in what way lecturers will present their information,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #73

challenges.content: in which case the best you can do is pre-write headings,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #74

challenges.content: but not specific, just general,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #75

challenges.content: as in Main One, Main Two, Sub One, Two, and Three, and so on.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #76

challenges.content: Okay.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #77

challenges.content: But always be prepared to adapt to the nature of the talk,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #78

challenges.content: using any one of the other methods if it becomes appropriate at the time.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 3 - challenge #79

challenges.content: Welcome to the library, or the I.L.C., which means Independent Learning Centre,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #1

challenges.content: and let me explain about some of its facilities.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #2

challenges.content: We're standing here at the entry gates, next to the borrowing desk.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #3

challenges.content: That's where you check out any books,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #4

challenges.content: but you are also advised to study in the library here,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #5

challenges.content: since most of our material cannot be borrowed.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #6

challenges.content: Thus, we have Seating along the middle of the library,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #7

challenges.content: and in that far corner in front of us. on the left,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #8

challenges.content: we have the Quiet Reading Section, for some serious reading activity.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #9

challenges.content: We used to have the computers there
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #10

challenges.content: but then realised that that corner was very quiet,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #11

challenges.content: and thus better suited for the purpose it now has.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #12

challenges.content: The computers were instead shifted to a more central location,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #13

challenges.content: right beside us here, on the left.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #14

challenges.content: Again, somewhat confusingly,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #15

challenges.content: this area once housed the Newspaper and Magazine Section,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #16

challenges.content: but the people in the Quiet Reading Area had to walk too far to collect this literature,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #17

challenges.content: so it was moved to right beside them, in the adjacent corner.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #18

challenges.content: So, feel free to read the newspapers there.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #19

challenges.content: But the reference books, those huge weighty dictionaries, atlases, and encyclopedias,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #20

challenges.content: were all situated at the opposite end of the building, against the wall.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #21

challenges.content: This was because they weren't generally that popular,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #22

challenges.content: and we wanted more space for the magazine racks,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #23

challenges.content: always a favourite with readers.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #24

challenges.content: Okay, as well as reading, you need to work on your listening skills,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #25

challenges.content: and for that you need the Audio Section.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #26

challenges.content: Again, such an activity needs a quiet area,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #27

challenges.content: so we put this in the last remaining corner, up there on your right, as you can see.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #28

challenges.content: There are CD players and headphones, so just borrow the listening packs,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #29

challenges.content: sit down there, and listen away.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #30

challenges.content: Right, that just leaves the main library.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #31

challenges.content: In other libraries, that's often right beside the Newspaper and Magazine Section,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #32

challenges.content: allowing freedom to choose from all genres of literature,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #33

challenges.content: but here, we've got them further apart.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #34

challenges.content: For the main library, just follow your nose,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #35

challenges.content: past the Central Seating there, and it's there among all that shelving,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #36

challenges.content: upon which you'll find an abundance of interesting books and listening packs to use.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #37

challenges.content: Now, I'd like to tell you a bit more about an excellent service offered in the I.L.C. here
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #38

challenges.content: that we call the 'Special Sessions'.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #39

challenges.content: What can you do in them?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #40

challenges.content: For a start, many of you need practice in speaking English.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #41

challenges.content: and for that we hold a special Discussion Session, led by a teacher.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #42

challenges.content: That can be noisy, in fact, we hope that it is noisy,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #43

challenges.content: since that would mean many people are talking.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #44

challenges.content: It's in the Central Seating area,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #45

challenges.content: and it used to be from 10:30 to 1:30.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #46

challenges.content: but we found that the noise was disturbing the regular I.L.C patrons,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #47

challenges.content: so we shortened and moved this discussion to the morning,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #48

challenges.content: 9 am time slot, when fewer people are in the centre.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #49

challenges.content: It goes for one and a half hours.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #50

challenges.content: Alright, what about Writing Skills?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #51

challenges.content: Well, we can help you there with another teacher.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #52

challenges.content: Now, writing is a fairly quiet activity,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #53

challenges.content: so that teacher stations him or herself in the Quiet Reading area
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #54

challenges.content: from 1:30 until 3.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #55

challenges.content: The 10:30-to-midday time slot cannot have a teacher for such writing skills,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #56

challenges.content: as they are all teaching in the morning.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #57

challenges.content: For this reason, of course, there cannot be an on-call teacher in the morning either,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #58

challenges.content: although many people would like one, particularly the 10.30-to-noon crowd,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #59

challenges.content: having just finished their early morning class.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #60

challenges.content: These students all have to wait until midday onwards,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #61

challenges.content: when, for three hours, a teacher will be stationed in the Audio Section,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #62

challenges.content: ready to deal with all those questions.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #63

challenges.content: Until recently, we had another teacher doing the 3-pm-to-6-pm time slot,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #64

challenges.content: in the Central Seating,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #65

challenges.content: but all the noise interfered with the late users of the I.L.C., so we had to cancel that.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #66

challenges.content: Also noisy can be the Language Exchange,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #67

challenges.content: where local students who want to learn your language will help you practise English.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #68

challenges.content: This is generally done in pairs,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #69

challenges.content: so the noise level is low enough not to need this exchange to run at 9 am,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #70

challenges.content: but at the more congenial time of 10:30, among the Central Seating.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #71

challenges.content: That must finish by 1:30 though,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #72

challenges.content: after which quieter and more individual activities take place.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 2 - challenge #73

challenges.content: Hello?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #1

challenges.content: Hello? Who is this?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #2

challenges.content: Hello. I'm a representative of the Tallyho Survey Company,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #3

challenges.content: and I'd like to ask you a few questions regarding exercise.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #4

challenges.content: Ah, that's an interesting subject.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #5

challenges.content: Yes, we think so, too.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #6

challenges.content: But I'm afraid I'm a bit busy at the moment.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #7

challenges.content: Don't worry. This will only take about four minutes at the most.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #8

challenges.content: It's 10:25 now, so it will all be over by 10:30.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #9

challenges.content: Well... alright, if it's that short.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #10

challenges.content: It will be.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #11

challenges.content: So, one of the first things I need to know is where you are,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #12

challenges.content: that is, which suburb or area of the city?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #13

challenges.content: The last client was in Blackburn, for example.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #14

challenges.content: Blackburn. That's close to me. I'm in Box Hill.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #15

challenges.content: Another eastern suburb then.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #16

challenges.content: I have a friend in Box Hill, too. Interesting place.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #17

challenges.content: Now, I need your approximate age for this survey.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #18

challenges.content: Are you younger than 20, between 20 and 29, 30 and 39, and so on?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #19

challenges.content: I'll turn 40 in a few months,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #20

challenges.content: so that puts me in the 40 to 49 age group.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #21

challenges.content: Well, that's in a few months, so right now you're in the 30 to 39.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #22

challenges.content: Oh, right. So put that then.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #23

challenges.content: Okay. Now, I need to know your occupation.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #24

challenges.content: The last caller was a housewife, for example; the one before that a teacher.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #25

challenges.content: I used to be a teacher, too, teaching cookery.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #26

challenges.content: And now?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #27

challenges.content: Now you can just put 'domestic duties'.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #28

challenges.content: Actually, I hope to begin a new job soon, as a cook,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #29

challenges.content: but that won't be for some time yet.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #30

challenges.content: I have to wait for my husband's restaurant to open.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #31

challenges.content: Cook? That sounds interesting,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #32

challenges.content: but it's 'domestic duties' for now.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #33

challenges.content: Okay, that just leaves some information about your family.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #34

challenges.content: This is not obligatory at all, so if you don't want to answer, that's fine.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #35

challenges.content: What sort of information, exactly?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #36

challenges.content: Oh, it's very broad.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #37

challenges.content: Married, with children; single mother, that sort of thing.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #38

challenges.content: The last customer said she was a single mother.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #39

challenges.content: I'm married, and not a mother. Put 'married, no children'.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #40

challenges.content: I'm married with children, myself.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #41

challenges.content: But I'll put in your details, and that finishes the profile,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #42

challenges.content: and just leaves the actual survey itself, if you're ready to proceed.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #43

challenges.content: Alright, let's begin the survey now, about your exercise habits.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #44

challenges.content: I'm afraid I don't exercise much at all.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #45

challenges.content: Well, the main question is in what form you take your exercise, however little that may be,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #46

challenges.content: for example, in just cleaning. Do you clean the house?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #47

challenges.content: My husband does the cleaning, actually,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #48

challenges.content: but I walk to the supermarket and shops very often, up to four times a week.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #49

challenges.content: I'll put that then, unless there's something else.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #50

challenges.content: Nothing else, really. But I diet. I'm very strict about what I eat.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #51

challenges.content: Oh, and I do yoga, although that's not very energetic,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #52

challenges.content: more a form of relaxation, and to tighten my muscles.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #53

challenges.content: They're both important, of course,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #54

challenges.content: but what about sport?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #55

challenges.content: Do you undertake any sporting activities?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #56

challenges.content: This could be very infrequent. In the past, for example.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #57

challenges.content: My husband plays basketball at the local school, and I sometimes watch.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #58

challenges.content: When he was younger he was in a basketball team, but I never participated.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #59

challenges.content: Have you done anything at all?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #60

challenges.content: I used to hike in a nearby national park.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #61

challenges.content: Well that's a definite physical activity, so I'll put that - but not basketball.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #62

challenges.content: Alright, that just leaves future exercise intentions.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #63

challenges.content: Do you plan, or expect to do, at some stage, any form of exercise?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #64

challenges.content: I once dreamt of doing modern dance, but that's never going to happen.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #65

challenges.content: Realistically, I'm thinking about going swimming, at the local aquatic centre,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #66

challenges.content: although my husband thinks we should just jog.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #67

challenges.content: I can't see myself doing that, though, too tiring.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #68

challenges.content: I can understand.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #69

challenges.content: I used to jog, too, and it really makes you sweat.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #70

challenges.content: I'd say swimming's a much better option.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #71

challenges.content: But I'll be starting this job as a cook in my husband's restaurant.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #72

challenges.content: I imagine I'll be very tired doing all those late shifts.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #73

challenges.content: But if I have any energy left over, I might go to the aquatic centre to release some stress.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #74

challenges.content: Alright. Well, that's the end of the survey.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #75

challenges.content: Thank you very much for your time.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 4 - Part 1 - challenge #76

challenges.content: If there is one natural feature which has long fascinated man, it is caves
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #1

challenges.content: those natural underground spaces into which people can enter.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #2

challenges.content: No known cave in the world can exist without it being extensively explored,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #3

challenges.content: whether it be in remote areas, such as the Clearwater Cave in Borneo,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #4

challenges.content: or immensely long and difficult, such as Mammoth Cave in America,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #5

challenges.content: or perhaps the most challenging: those caves below the water table, full with water,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #6

challenges.content: in which case the exploration is known as cave diving.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #7

challenges.content: Whatever the case, if the caves are known,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #8

challenges.content: as complex and difficult as they usually are, they will be explored.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #9

challenges.content: The formal name for the study of caves is speleology,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #10

challenges.content: and involves many disciplines, such as chemistry,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #11

challenges.content: geology, biology, and cartography,
challenges.explanation: cartography: the science or practice of drawing maps.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #12

challenges.content: or the science of making accurate maps,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #13

challenges.content: since the largest caves can be hundreds of kilometers long and highly complicated.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #14

challenges.content: If the exploration is just for fun, the activity is known as caving,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #15

challenges.content: but with the difficulties and dangers involved,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #16

challenges.content: the average caver is often involved with one of these speleological sciences.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #17

challenges.content: As for the number of caves in the world,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #18

challenges.content: research suggests that only a fraction have been found and documented,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #19

challenges.content: mostly in the areas in which caving has long been a popular activity,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #20

challenges.content: such as in America, France, or Australia.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #21

challenges.content: China, for example, has huge areas of limestone bedrock,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #22

challenges.content: prime material for cave formation,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #23

challenges.content: and logically must contain among the largest number of caves in the world,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #24

challenges.content: yet only few are documented due to the lack of interest in caving there.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #25

challenges.content: Thus, as exploration continues, new caves will be discovered,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #26

challenges.content: and it is likely that the numbers could radically change in the future.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #27

challenges.content: With caves being such mysterious and intriguing places,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #28

challenges.content: the obvious question concerns how they form.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #29

challenges.content: The most common cause is the effect of slightly acidic water
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #30

challenges.content: in a process called 'dissolution'.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #31

challenges.content: Here, water seeps into the ground, and down through rock masses.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #32

challenges.content: If this rock is soluble, the water dissolves some of it,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #33

challenges.content: and over time, the passage expands to become a cave, or cave system.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #34

challenges.content: The largest and most common of these involves limestone,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #35

challenges.content: although other materials are possible, including gypsum, marble, and even salt.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #36

challenges.content: Now, if the cave is formed at the same time as the rock, it is called a primary cave,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #37

challenges.content: and the most common of these are lava tubes.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #38

challenges.content: When lava from volcanoes flows downhill,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #39

challenges.content: the topmost surface cools and solidifies first,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #40

challenges.content: leaving the hotter lava to continue to flow beneath.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #41

challenges.content: If most of this eventually flows out, a hollow tube is left.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #42

challenges.content: The country Iceland, has some excellent caves of this type,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #43

challenges.content: and even far-flung Australia has a few.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #44

challenges.content: Finally, there are sea caves, formed from waves pounding into coastal cliffs,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #45

challenges.content: and eroding into fault lines, or softer rock.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #46

challenges.content: These caves are usually the shortest, about 50 meters at most,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #47

challenges.content: since the erosive action of the waves can only reach a certain distance.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #48

challenges.content: However, it is limestone caves which will always be the most interesting.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #49

challenges.content: This is due to the presence of limestone formations.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #50

challenges.content: As the groundwater seeps downward through the ceiling of the caves,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #51

challenges.content: it encounters a different pressure and temperature,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #52

challenges.content: causing it to deposit a small amount of its dissolved calcium carbonate.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #53

challenges.content: Over time, through the action of millions of drops,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #54

challenges.content: this deposition process results in ever-growing masses,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #55

challenges.content: known as stalactites (if hanging from the ceiling),
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #56

challenges.content: or stalagmites (if growing from the floor).
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #57

challenges.content: Alternatively, the water may flow over a large surface of rock, forming flowstone,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #58

challenges.content: and with other sorts of processes,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #59

challenges.content: can result in beautiful milky-white formations of astonishing complexity.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #60

challenges.content: One of the best examples of this,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #61

challenges.content: as well as of what surprising discoveries may yet await,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #62

challenges.content: is the Lechuguilla Cave in New Mexico.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #63

challenges.content: In the 1950s, some cavers heard the sound of wind underneath some large boulders on the cave floor,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #64

challenges.content: a clear sign of a deeper passageway.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #65

challenges.content: It took until 1984 for a group of cavers to gain permission to start digging,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #66

challenges.content: and two years later, in 1986,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #67

challenges.content: they broke through into a walkable passageway,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #68

challenges.content: unlocking one of the longest cave systems in the world,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #69

challenges.content: the deepest in America,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #70

challenges.content: and some of the most beautiful formations ever found.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #71

challenges.content: Unusually, many of these were yellow with sulphur,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #72

challenges.content: suggesting that the caves were a result of hydrogen-sulfide from nearby oil deposits.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #73

challenges.content: This was forced through fracture lines,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #74

challenges.content: combining with existing groundwater to form sulfuric acid,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #75

challenges.content: dissolving the limestone from the bottom up,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #76

challenges.content: instead of the normal top-down seepage which characterises most limestone cave formations.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 4 - challenge #77

challenges.content: Okay, we've got to decide who to promote to Leading Education Officer.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #1

challenges.content: Someone from the arts faculty, I suppose.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #2

challenges.content: Well, it can be from any faculty, since the position requires more general skills:
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #3

challenges.content: handling personnel, settling disputes, and motivating them to focus on the task.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #4

challenges.content: It was the last position which involved computer knowledge, not this one.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #5

challenges.content: Surely computer knowledge would help.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #6

challenges.content: So too would knowledge in the arts.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #7

challenges.content: Sure, it would help, but the key criterion is being able to direct the staff appropriately.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #8

challenges.content: So, it doesn't matter then from which faculty we select our candidates?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #9

challenges.content: Not really, but I've already looked at those from computing, and rejected them all.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #10

challenges.content: Why?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #11

challenges.content: They're all too new, lacking in sufficient experience,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #12

challenges.content: whereas these ones from the business faculty are longtimers,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #13

challenges.content: so we'll take someone from there.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #14

challenges.content: I suppose you're right.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #15

challenges.content: The arts faculty doesn't present much in the way of suitable candidates either.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #16
