challenges.content: But we'll still have to train the person - teach the ropes, as they say.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #17

challenges.content: And he or she will have to expect to do overtime, as needed.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #18

challenges.content: Of course. It can get so busy that, if we were open on the weekend,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #19

challenges.content: they'd have to work then as well.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #20

challenges.content: Just as well we're a Monday to Friday university, right?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #21

challenges.content: Right!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #22

challenges.content: But are you sure these people will actually want the job?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #23

challenges.content: The salary isn't such an improvement on their current ones.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #24

challenges.content: I know, but there are benefits.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #25

challenges.content: You get overtime rates, a nice place to put your car,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #26

challenges.content: as well as additional petrol money if you drive for company purposes,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #27

challenges.content: which they'll probably be required to do.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #28

challenges.content: But those benefits are quite limited,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #29

challenges.content: especially given all the work and responsibility involved.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #30

challenges.content: People often don't like that.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #31

challenges.content: They prefer the creative freedom of less-senior teaching positions.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #32

challenges.content: Yeah I know,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #33

challenges.content: but these candidates should realise that if they do this job well, there'll be more promotions down the line.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #34

challenges.content: you know how everyone likes having their own office, right?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #35

challenges.content: Sure.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #36

challenges.content: Well, that would come after a few years,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #37

challenges.content: if they're prepared to work hard and grow with the university.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #38

challenges.content: Yes, that should attract these people.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #39

challenges.content: Well, that's enough talk about the job.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #40

challenges.content: What about the actual candidates?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #41

challenges.content: How many do we have?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #42

challenges.content: Ah, I've narrowed it down to four...
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #43

challenges.content: ah, just using their first names, that's Steven, Abdul, Lek, and Oscar.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #44

challenges.content: As you said, there's quite a bit of experience between them, about 34 years in all.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #45

challenges.content: What's the exact breakdown of figures?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #46

challenges.content: Abdul and Steven both have seven years,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #47

challenges.content: Lek has one more, and Oscar is the most experienced, at 12.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #48

challenges.content: But who's the most qualified?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #49

challenges.content: Steven and Abdul have an MBA
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #50

challenges.content: sorry! Abdul's got something called a M.B.P.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #51

challenges.content: some foreign thing which translates as Master of Business Practice.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #52

challenges.content: I'm not sure what that is, but does he do the job well?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #53

challenges.content: Very well, apparently
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #54

challenges.content: better than Lek and Oscar, who hold a degree and some certificates, respectively.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #55

challenges.content: But we have to think about any drawbacks,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #56

challenges.content: y'know, possible issues with any of them.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #57

challenges.content: I asked their respective deans for feedback, and I found out that Steven, the younger one, drinks a bit.
challenges.explanation: dean: the head of a college or university faculty or department.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #58

challenges.content: So, he has a problem with alcohol?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #59

challenges.content: No, he never drinks to excess,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #60

challenges.content: but at the bar he's often expressed his intention of moving on, of teaching abroad.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #61

challenges.content: Ah, he's not stable.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #62

challenges.content: Not stable at all, apparently.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #63

challenges.content: We'll never know for how long he'll hold the job.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #64

challenges.content: We need stable personnel,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #65

challenges.content: and people without family problems, or sick relatives, like the last guy we promoted.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #66

challenges.content: What about Abdul then? Will he do?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #67

challenges.content: He might do, except his English language ability is limited.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #68

challenges.content: It's functional, but a bit broken, and meaning is sometimes lost.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #69

challenges.content: That's not the problem with the next candidate, Lek, who has good language ability,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #70

challenges.content: but this job involves handling people,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #71

challenges.content: and his dean says Lek's attitude is bad.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #72

challenges.content: In what way?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #73

challenges.content: His manners are okay, and he's interested in his job,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #74

challenges.content: but he believes there should always be adequate leisure in life.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #75

challenges.content: He definitely won't work overtime and complains a lot already about his job,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #76

challenges.content: but this last candidate, Oscar, is probably not the right one, either.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #77

challenges.content: Why not?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #78

challenges.content: Not another problem with language?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #79

challenges.content: His first language isn't English, but he speaks it well enough.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #80

challenges.content: He's stable, with a good attitude, but his age is the problem.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #81

challenges.content: Age is not a problem. That would be ageism, and I don't believe in that.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #82

challenges.content: But with his age comes health problems as well,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #83

challenges.content: and serious one is that.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #84

challenges.content: Oh, that might be an issue then.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 3 - challenge #85

challenges.content: Hello everyone, and welcome to the "Fit for Life" Health Centre,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 2 - challenge #1

challenges.content: a place which, as the name suggests, is not just for short-term solutions,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 2 - challenge #2

challenges.content: but rather, intends to put you on a sensible and achievable footing for the rest of your life.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 2 - challenge #3

challenges.content: And that's how we're different.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 2 - challenge #4

challenges.content: For example, we could immediately put you on a harsh exercise program,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 2 - challenge #5

challenges.content: expecting you to work out every day, but such a plan would see you quickly lose interest.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 2 - challenge #6

challenges.content: That's why the initial step is a one-and-a-half-hour consultation,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 2 - challenge #7

challenges.content: in which your lifestyle, current situation, and long-term goals, are all thoroughly analysed.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 2 - challenge #8

challenges.content: Now, an important part of this consultation involves analysing what you eat.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 2 - challenge #9

challenges.content: There's no point exercising here, and losing weight, then putting it all back on, later.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 2 - challenge #10

challenges.content: You will need to show self-control and discipline in your diet, and we'll work on that.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 2 - challenge #11

challenges.content: Similarly, we'll put you on an exercise regime suitable for your level of fitness,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 2 - challenge #12

challenges.content: so that will involve a test, where we will take you through some activities,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 2 - challenge #13

challenges.content: then measure your heart rate and blood pressure to determine how fit you are.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 2 - challenge #14

challenges.content: This will be monitored during every subsequent consultation,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 2 - challenge #15

challenges.content: along with your exercise schedule,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 2 - challenge #16

challenges.content: and that occurs monthly, and not half-yearly, as with many other centres.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 2 - challenge #17

challenges.content: As to our actual exercise machines and programs,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 2 - challenge #18

challenges.content: you will have to decide whether it is muscle mass,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 2 - challenge #19

challenges.content: stamina, or general fitness, that you want to develop.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 2 - challenge #20

challenges.content: Think about which of these three you want to target,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 2 - challenge #21

challenges.content: and we'll design a specific program for you,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 2 - challenge #22

challenges.content: but remember, bulging muscles aren't necessarily suitable for everyone.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 2 - challenge #23

challenges.content: Sometimes it's better to think in terms of two simple concepts:
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 2 - challenge #24

challenges.content: muscle definition and stamina;
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 2 - challenge #25

challenges.content: or, if you are female, being fit and healthy, in both mind and body.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 2 - challenge #26

challenges.content: Now, if you're going to work out at this gym,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 2 - challenge #27

challenges.content: you'll need to think about your reasons for exercising,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 2 - challenge #28

challenges.content: so let's consider that in more detail.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 2 - challenge #29

challenges.content: Muscle mass is certainly popular with the guys, probably seeking, to impress the girls,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 2 - challenge #30

challenges.content: and with muscles comes the confidence to do that, right?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 2 - challenge #31

challenges.content: Well, for that, you'll need our high-stress weight units, where pumping iron is all the rage.
challenges.explanation:
pumping iron: slang word for "exercising with weights"

(to be) all the rage: very popular
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 2 - challenge #32

challenges.content: Moving on to other benefits, one of the main ones is beating the tension of life, right,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 2 - challenge #33

challenges.content: and the longer the exercise is, the greater the rewards in this respect.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 2 - challenge #34

challenges.content: Thus, playing squash can certainly help, and so can swimming,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 2 - challenge #35

challenges.content: but what's much better, as every jogger will tell you, is their activity,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 2 - challenge #36

challenges.content: so we have ample jogging machines, and they're always popular.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 2 - challenge #37

challenges.content: They can provide good fitness too, as can the yoga classes;
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 2 - challenge #38

challenges.content: however, again, let's not forget playing squash,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 2 - challenge #39

challenges.content: which, I would say, is the optimum way to improve your general wellbeing.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 2 - challenge #40

challenges.content: Such an active, energetic game, plus the competitive element,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 2 - challenge #41

challenges.content: drives you forward into high levels of health and fitness.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 2 - challenge #42

challenges.content: These, of course, are the ultimate purposes of being here,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 2 - challenge #43

challenges.content: but remember, the centre is full of like-minded people,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 2 - challenge #44

challenges.content: all of whom are interesting to meet, and valuable sources of information.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 2 - challenge #45

challenges.content: The yoga classes have a pre- and post-meeting session,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 2 - challenge #46

challenges.content: so you'll certainly meet others there,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 2 - challenge #47

challenges.content: although they'll all be yoga enthusiasts,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 2 - challenge #48

challenges.content: which limits the range somewhat.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 2 - challenge #49

challenges.content: But whether doing yoga, swimming, or exercising, everyone showers, right,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 2 - challenge #50

challenges.content: so those facilities are where you'll hear all sorts of interesting conversations, and really get to know people
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 2 - challenge #51

challenges.content: not like the front-desk area,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 2 - challenge #52

challenges.content: which is mostly empty as patrons go immediately inside to do their exercise.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 2 - challenge #53

challenges.content: Of course, the front desk can answer all your questions,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 2 - challenge #54

challenges.content: and has information brochures, and such like,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 2 - challenge #55

challenges.content: but for knowing more about a greater variety of subjects and community concerns,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 2 - challenge #56

challenges.content: look at the notice board in the yoga studio,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 2 - challenge #57

challenges.content: where there's a huge array of papers, leaflets, and articles, all for you to read and consider.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 2 - challenge #58

challenges.content: Hello. Is this the Triple A Employment agency?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #1

challenges.content: Yes.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #2

challenges.content: Hi. I rang before. My name's Andrew. Andrew Peterson.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #3

challenges.content: I rang you earlier and gave you my personal details.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #4

challenges.content: If you remember, I'm that student looking for work during the summer holidays.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #5

challenges.content: Oh, sure. Actually, I have your file right here.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #6

challenges.content: But... we still need to add some further information.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #7

challenges.content: Yeah, that's what they told me, and that's why I'm ringing.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #8

challenges.content: What do you need to know?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #9

challenges.content: Well, we have to know your main level of education. It's a degree, I suppose.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #10

challenges.content: Yes, but I'm still doing it, in engineering. It's quite interesting.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #11

challenges.content: Some of my friends are studying computing though, so I'm interested in that, also.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #12

challenges.content: Well, I'll just write in your main degree subject. Engineering.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #13

challenges.content: We usually have a demand in computing though.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #14

challenges.content: Have you worked with computers before?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #15

challenges.content: No. I just do some programming for fun at the university,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #16

challenges.content: but I almost got a job as a computer designer once.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #17

challenges.content: Actually, the only job I've ever had was as a car salesman, believe it or not.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #18

challenges.content: Well, at least you've had experience dealing with customers.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #19

challenges.content: What about hobbies though?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #20

challenges.content: Sometimes they can help develop useful skills.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #21

challenges.content: Ummm... in my free time I don't do much - mostly study.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #22

challenges.content: I play chess occasionally at the university chess club.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #23

challenges.content: That's right next to the tennis courts,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #24

challenges.content: but I'm not interested in that.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #25

challenges.content: Chess helps develop analytical skills, so I'll put that down.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #26

challenges.content: Of course, it's your main skills that employers want to know about
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #27

challenges.content: What would you say they are?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #28

challenges.content: Well, I'm in my third year now, studying electrical machines and generating systems,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #29

challenges.content: but I'd say electronics is my best skill
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #30

challenges.content: much better than, say, my machine skills, which aren't so good, actually.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #31

challenges.content: Okay... machine skills are in demand, but so too are electronic ones,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #32

challenges.content: so we might be able to find you a part-time job in that field.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #33

challenges.content: But what sort of money do you expect to get?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #34

challenges.content: Oh, anything really.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #35

challenges.content: I'd want the standard payment, let's say.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #36

challenges.content: What's normal? 1,000 a month? 1,500?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #37

challenges.content: I'll just put $1,200, okay?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #38

challenges.content: That's fine by me.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #39

challenges.content: When can you start? Say, within two days?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #40

challenges.content: Easily! Actually, less.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #41

challenges.content: In fact, just give me a ring, and I'll be able to start immediately,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #42

challenges.content: although I admit it'll take me a few days to get used to getting up early in the morning.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #43

challenges.content: Okay! That's just about it,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #44

challenges.content: unless you'd like to add anything else which may help with your application?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #45

challenges.content: Ah, not really.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #46

challenges.content: I ride a motorbike, but that's unimportant.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #47

challenges.content: I'm friendly, but every applicant claims that, right?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #48

challenges.content: I can speak another language.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #49

challenges.content: Ah, that might be useful, depending on the language.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #50

challenges.content: Is it Chinese? A Chinese speaker would go down well.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #51

challenges.content: Spanish, I'm afraid.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #52

challenges.content: You see, I grew up with some friends who came from South America.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #53

challenges.content: Okay, I'll write that down, but I don't think it will help that much, sorry to say.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #54

challenges.content: Well, thanks for your help, and hopefully I'll get a job soon,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #55

challenges.content: but can I just ask one more question?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #56

challenges.content: Sure!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #57

challenges.content: What, basically, are employers looking for when they interview someone?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #58

challenges.content: Oh, many things.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #59

challenges.content: Being hardworking, diligent, and focused on your job is good,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #60

challenges.content: but surprisingly, it often means you can't see the bigger picture,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #61

challenges.content: or provide suggestions which help the company move forward.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #62

challenges.content: That requires thinking for yourself, outside the box as they say,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #63

challenges.content: and being free of the standard ways of approaching tasks.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #64

challenges.content: Employers certainly value that.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #65

challenges.content: I guess experience must help, though?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #66

challenges.content: It depends. If it involved a routine job, one which didn't exercise your mind,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #67

challenges.content: it might not mean that much at all.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #68

challenges.content: But since companies are basically composed of people,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #69

challenges.content: it is important to be able to get along with others.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #70

challenges.content: There's no point in hiring someone whom the other employees don't like, right?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #71

challenges.content: That just causes problems,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #72

challenges.content: in fact, I would say that being friendly and approachable ranks far more highly than your academic qualifications.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #73

challenges.content: Okay, and that's all assessed at the interview, right?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #74

challenges.content: Yes, and your qualifications, experience, and approach to the job,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #75

challenges.content: such as whether you can do different things, work overtime, or do long hours as needed.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #76

challenges.content: But those latter qualities are pretty much standard.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #77

challenges.content: What may be more important is based on the fact that things inevitably go wrong.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #78

challenges.content: Mistakes are made, and someone's got to fix them in a way that creates the least disturbance.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #79

challenges.content: People with demonstrated abilities to do this are certainly regarded highly.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #80

challenges.content: I see. That's very interesting!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 3 - Part 1 - challenge #81

challenges.content: In the night sky, the stars appear to revolve around the Earth,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #1

challenges.content: rising in the east, and disappearing in the west.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #2

challenges.content: The Earth itself seems solid, fixed, and stable,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #3

challenges.content: and such common sense perception suggests that the Earth is the centre of the universe.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #4

challenges.content: This is known as "geocentrism", with geo meaning Earth,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #5

challenges.content: and all pre-modern civilisations drew this conclusion.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #6

challenges.content: We now know, of course, that the Earth revolves around the sun,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #7

challenges.content: and this is called "heliocentrism", with helio meaning sun,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #8

challenges.content: but historically, it took quite a while for this to be deduced.
challenges.explanation: deduce: to reach an answer or a decision by thinking carefully about the known facts.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #9

challenges.content: As early as the third century BC,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #10

challenges.content: an ancient Greek astronomer, Aristarchus of Samos,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #11

challenges.content: proposed heliocentrism, but received little support from his peers.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #12

challenges.content: Similarly, throughout subsequent history, isolated individuals proposed this new idea,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #13

challenges.content: but again, no one was listening.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #14

challenges.content: Geocentrism just seemed too logical to refute.
challenges.explanation: refute: prove something to be wrong or false.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #15

challenges.content: Geocentrism also fitted the views of the established Christian church,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #16

challenges.content: who could quote biblical passages such as 'the world also shall be stable, that it be not moved'.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #17

challenges.content: Those who dared to disagree were subject to accusations of heresy
challenges.explanation: heresy: having a belief that is against the principles of a particular religion
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #18

challenges.content: often with dire punishments to follow.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #19

challenges.content: The trouble was, as the night sky was observed more closely,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #20

challenges.content: that simple revolution of the stars proved not so simple at all.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #21

challenges.content: In relation to the other stars, some steadily wandered in given directions,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #22

challenges.content: then sometimes reversed for months, and disappeared altogether.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #23

challenges.content: They were called planets, meaning 'wanderers'.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #24

challenges.content: In addition, the position of the sun and moon altered slightly over the year,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #25

challenges.content: and comets, those mysterious glowing spots, would come and go.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #26

challenges.content: In order to predict the motion of the planets,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #27

challenges.content: and accurately serve the primary purpose of navigation for sailing ships,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #28

challenges.content: increasingly elaborate mathematical models were needed -
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #29

challenges.content: a sure sign that something was not quite right.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #30

challenges.content: Heliocentrism, or the belief that the sun is the centre of the solar system,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #31

challenges.content: still needed a mathematically-sound description before it could be scientifically accepted,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #32

challenges.content: and it was a Polish astronomer, Nicolaus Copernicus,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #33

challenges.content: who, in 1543, first published this.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #34

challenges.content: This event is sometimes referred to as the Copernican revolution.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #35

challenges.content: Copernicus himself certainly feared the consequences of his proof,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #36

challenges.content: knowing full well it might invoke the anger of the established church.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #37

challenges.content: Probably for this reason, he waited until the last year of his life,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #38

challenges.content: when he was sick and dying, to release his findings.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #39

challenges.content: In addition, the preface of the book,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #40

challenges.content: written by a respected member of the church,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #41

challenges.content: stated that the model was not necessarily correct.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #42

challenges.content: As a result of this, there was no "revolution" whatsoever,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #43

challenges.content: in fact, the book received scant attention in the subsequent decades,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #44

challenges.content: apart from a few irate clergy men who angrily dismissed the whole scheme as irrelevant.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #45

challenges.content: Yet the following generations of astronomers did not always fare so well.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #46

challenges.content: The Italian scientist, Galileo, got into trouble,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #47

challenges.content: as did a fellow Italian, with the surname Bruno, Giordono Bruno,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #48

challenges.content: who was burnt at the stake,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #49

challenges.content: yet ultimately, nothing could slow the spread of heliocentrism across Europe.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #50

challenges.content: It formed the basis of Isaac Newton's great work on the motion of the planets,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #51

challenges.content: a work which implied that even the sun, around which the Earth circled,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #52

challenges.content: was itself in motion around a common centre of gravity.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #53

challenges.content: No discourse about heliocentrism could finish without mentioning that,
challenges.explanation: discourse: a speech or piece of writing about a subject
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #54

challenges.content: somewhat unbelievably, there still exists those today who choose to believe that the Earth is the centre of the universe.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #55

challenges.content: Modern geocentrism is usually the result of literal interpretations of the Bible,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #56

challenges.content: which is the cornerstone of these people's beliefs.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #57

challenges.content: They, therefore, also believe in creationism,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #58

challenges.content: that is, that a God created everything,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #59

challenges.content: and while we may smile at this,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #60

challenges.content: it is sobering to consider that surveys have revealed that up to 10% of British people,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #61

challenges.content: 12% of Europeans. 20% of the USA,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #62

challenges.content: and 25% of the Middle East,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #63

challenges.content: still hold the belief that the sun revolves around the Earth.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #64

challenges.content: One can only wonder what Copernicus would have thought of this.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 4 - challenge #65

challenges.content: Hi, Ms Harris. Here we are, talking once again.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #1

challenges.content: Well, I'm always willing to help out wherever possible.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #2

challenges.content: Is anything troubling you?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #3

challenges.content: Well, your advice last week about writing summaries was very useful,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #4

challenges.content: and I'm using these summaries a lot in order to prepare my final master's thesis.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #5

challenges.content: But you're having problems, right?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #6

challenges.content: Yes, I have a few issues to discuss.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #7

challenges.content: Obviously I want a good essay, and I want to achieve high marks.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #8

challenges.content: But I'm not sure on the best way to start.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #9

challenges.content: That's an easy question.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #10

challenges.content: Start with a topic, but not one that I necessarily suggest,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #11

challenges.content: but one that you want to explore.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #12

challenges.content: You'll always write better when doing so on a topic you're interested in,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #13

challenges.content: not one imposed upon you by others.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #14

challenges.content: Well, I'm interested in management theory.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #15

challenges.content: Then pursue that.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #16

challenges.content: However, that alone is far too broad.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #17

challenges.content: Break it into various current areas of discussion and relevance,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #18

challenges.content: then look more carefully at one of them -
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #19

challenges.content: say, management and cultural differences,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #20

challenges.content: or management and motivation,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #21

challenges.content: or other aspects, such as the role of salary, group cohesion, or leadership.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #22

challenges.content: I would say I'm interested in group cohesion,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #23

challenges.content: that is, how people interact in the workplace.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #24

challenges.content: Well, that's a start,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #25

challenges.content: but you can't then just write planlessly,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #26

challenges.content: without defining exactly what you intend to do within the area you've chosen.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #27

challenges.content: You'll have to think of a thesis, and this statement could be of several types.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #28

challenges.content: Such as what?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #29

challenges.content: Oh, you could argue a point, something that you believe in;
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #30

challenges.content: or discuss an issue, looking at its various perspectives;
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #31

challenges.content: or critique the opinions of others, pointing out the pitfalls and flaws.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #32

challenges.content: The thesis statement will make that very clear because it will say,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #33

challenges.content: in simple terms, what you intend to achieve in your essay.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #34

challenges.content: I see. And then I can just begin writing, right?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #35

challenges.content: Wrong!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #36

challenges.content: If your essay is going to be clear, it needs to be logical and organised,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #37

challenges.content: and this means you'll need an outline.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #38

challenges.content: This could be written as a flowchart, or spider graph,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #39

challenges.content: that is, a series of connected lines,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #40

challenges.content: but whatever shape the outline takes,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #41

challenges.content: there must be a sense of progress, in, more or less, a straight line, towards a goal.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #42

challenges.content: And then my essay will be good?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #43

challenges.content: With such progression, definitely
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #44

challenges.content: as long as you do achieve everything that you set out to do,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #45

challenges.content: as specified in the beginning, okay?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #46

challenges.content: Well, Ms Harris, your advice about essay writing all sounds very useful:
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #47

challenges.content: solid, and step by step, so I'll certainly follow that.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #48

challenges.content: But can you tell me in more general terms,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #49

challenges.content: what constitutes the best essay?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #50

challenges.content: Oh, there are many aspects to consider,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #51

challenges.content: but one of the most important is certainly, original thinking.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #52

challenges.content: The best essays are written by people who think for themselves,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #53

challenges.content: and not just copy or imitate established views.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #54

challenges.content: I think I can do that.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #55

challenges.content: But remember, you can't just give a list of unsupported assertions.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #56

challenges.content: There needs to be support as well -
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #57

challenges.content: a chain of logic linking each step in your argument.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #58

challenges.content: Right!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #59

challenges.content: Yet that alone is not enough.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #60

challenges.content: Your argument may be logically sound, but is it practically so?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #61

challenges.content: For that, you need examples, from real-life, to illustrate your points or sub-points.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #62

challenges.content: I've got lots of examples from my course readings.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #63

challenges.content: I suppose I could use them.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #64

challenges.content: But remember, whenever you use an example,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #65

challenges.content: or facts or figures that are not commonly known,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #66

challenges.content: you must give a reference.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #67

challenges.content: That's an academic necessity, without which your writing will automatically fail.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #68

challenges.content: So, it's necessary to give these. Right.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #69

challenges.content: Absolutely! And with that, your essay will be fine,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #70

challenges.content: but always ensure that you format it clearly.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #71

challenges.content: What do you mean?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #72

challenges.content: I mean the practical considerations,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #73

challenges.content: as written in the university style guide,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #74

challenges.content: such as leaving appropriate margins,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #75

challenges.content: using double spacing, Arial font, and so on.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #76

challenges.content: You see, your writing must look good, as well as be good.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #77

challenges.content: I can certainly do that.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #78

challenges.content: And, finally, related to the previous point,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #79

challenges.content: you need to respect the number of words required.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #80

challenges.content: Your individual lecturers will give you a word-count figure,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #81

challenges.content: so follow what they say, making your essay neither too long, nor too short,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #82

challenges.content: perhaps 10% either way should be acceptable.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #83

challenges.content: 15% was common when I was younger,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #84

challenges.content: but it's a lot stricter now,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #85

challenges.content: and 20% would be pushing the boundaries just a little too far.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #86

challenges.content: I guess I can do all that. Thanks for your advice.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 3 - challenge #87

challenges.content: Hello everyone, and welcome to the Stanfield Childcare Centre.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 2 - challenge #1

challenges.content: Now I know you're all new mothers, and you like to cling to your children.
challenges.explanation: cling to something: hold something tightly, try hard to keep something
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 2 - challenge #2

challenges.content: You've certainly spent a lot of time raising them to the age of four
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 2 - challenge #3

challenges.content: and are perhaps reluctant to leave them here at our centre.
challenges.explanation: reluctant: hesitant or unwilling or unsure
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 2 - challenge #4

challenges.content: Well, one of the first things you should understand is that here it is safe - very safe.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 2 - challenge #5

challenges.content: Look around and you'll see that every room has padded walls.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 2 - challenge #6

challenges.content: Other centres have standard painted walls,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 2 - challenge #7

challenges.content: but here, we have invested a lot to ensure your children will not hurt themselves
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 2 - challenge #8

challenges.content: when running around and possibly tripping over.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 2 - challenge #9

challenges.content: This padding extends around all corners
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 2 - challenge #10

challenges.content: that is, the areas most likely to bruise and cut your active little child.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 2 - challenge #11

challenges.content: So, you can rest assured that any accidents of a physical nature are not likely to happen here.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 2 - challenge #12

challenges.content: Now, you don't want to dump your child at this centre and let them waste their time.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 2 - challenge #13

challenges.content: You want them to learn, and that's one of the greatest assets of our establishment.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 2 - challenge #14

challenges.content: Our staff are not only trained childcare workers,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 2 - challenge #15

challenges.content: but all of them have a special skill, which they can impart to your child,
challenges.explanation: impart: communicate, convey, let somebody know about something
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 2 - challenge #16

challenges.content: whether it be teaching the ABC, some basic mathematics,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 2 - challenge #17

challenges.content: artistic skills, or physical education.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 2 - challenge #18

challenges.content: We are particularly known for our pre-school literacy program
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 2 - challenge #19

challenges.content: and have a wealth of learning toys, specially designed to develop your child's potential.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 2 - challenge #20

challenges.content: Of course, one concern many mothers have is that,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 2 - challenge #21

challenges.content: in environments such as these,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 2 - challenge #22

challenges.content: colds and flus and other viral nasties can be easily spread around.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 2 - challenge #23

challenges.content: It's a very legitimate concern,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 2 - challenge #24

challenges.content: and one which we take seriously,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 2 - challenge #25

challenges.content: and we pride ourselves on our precautions.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 2 - challenge #26

challenges.content: For a start, unlike most centres which clean with standard detergents,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 2 - challenge #27

challenges.content: we disinfect every surface at the end of every day,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 2 - challenge #28

challenges.content: using a special disinfectant wash.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 2 - challenge #29

challenges.content: Some places just wipe surfaces daily with a damp cloth,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 2 - challenge #30

challenges.content: but not us. And that's just the start.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 2 - challenge #31

challenges.content: We also physically check your children when they arrive every day,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 2 - challenge #32

challenges.content: and if we feel your child is sick,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 2 - challenge #33

challenges.content: we ask him or her to wear a face mask to ensure germs are not transmitted.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 2 - challenge #34

challenges.content: If your child is noticeably sick, then we ask you to take them back home to recover.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 2 - challenge #35

challenges.content: This might sound a little unkind,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 2 - challenge #36

challenges.content: but we hope parents can understand that these measures are for the benefit of all.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 2 - challenge #37

challenges.content: Now, at Stanfield Childcare Centre we have excellent childcare officers,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 2 - challenge #38

challenges.content: and let me briefly introduce them.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 2 - challenge #39

challenges.content: We have Susan, Andrea, Bella, Cathy, Lisa, and Liz.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 2 - challenge #40

challenges.content: They're all fully trained and come with some individual assets which make them even better.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 2 - challenge #41

challenges.content: Bella, for instance, knows children very well, having worked here for five years,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 2 - challenge #42

challenges.content: and Cathy has her own family - two little girls
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 2 - challenge #43

challenges.content: so she can talk to you with first-hand knowledge of what it's really like to raise children.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 2 - challenge #44

challenges.content: But getting back to Bella, she often relaxes here after work,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 2 - challenge #45

challenges.content: spending long hours chatting to parents, as does Cathy in fact.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 2 - challenge #46

challenges.content: But in terms of hours, nothing can compare to Andrea,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 2 - challenge #47

challenges.content: who will sometimes spend the night here, staying in our overnight room.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 2 - challenge #48

challenges.content: Why? Because this centre is very friendly, and simply a great place to be.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 2 - challenge #49

challenges.content: Bella, for example, used to be quite shy herself
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 2 - challenge #50

challenges.content: but now is marvelous with the little kiddies, as outgoing as any of them.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 2 - challenge #51

challenges.content: We let Cathy, though, deal with the particularly quiet and introverted children,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 2 - challenge #52

challenges.content: since having her own family, she knows what can really bring them out.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 2 - challenge #53

challenges.content: Of course, what better way to do this than with yummie homemade cakes,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 2 - challenge #54

challenges.content: and Cathy often gets these from Bella, who can make some of the best in town.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 2 - challenge #55

challenges.content: Yes, everyone here brings something special,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 2 - challenge #56

challenges.content: which is why we're one of the best childcare centres in the business.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 2 - challenge #57

challenges.content: Okay Mary, I know I'm putting on weight with all my bad eating habits.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #1

challenges.content: That's right. Chocolate bars, pizzas, and all washed down with litres of soft drink.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #2

challenges.content: And with all the sugar in soft drink,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #3

challenges.content: I think we can say you're definitely overindulging, don't you think?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #4

challenges.content: I know, I know.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #5

challenges.content: I intend to definitely stop drinking that from now on.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #6

challenges.content: And that's part of the sensible eating plan that we have agreed we need to formulate -
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #7

challenges.content: one that we can both follow.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #8

challenges.content: That's right, sensible, and practical -
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #9

challenges.content: allowing us to indulge in some sweet foods on occasions.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #10

challenges.content: On rare occasions,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #11

challenges.content: and we're going to cut out all the pizzas and hamburgers.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #12

challenges.content: Well, not totally.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #13

challenges.content: I thought you said pizzas could be eaten once a week.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #14

challenges.content: You know how I like pizzas.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #15

challenges.content: No. I said once every two months.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #16

challenges.content: Once a week was ice cream, not pizza.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #17

challenges.content: Yeah, that's because you like ice cream.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #18

challenges.content: I prefer pizza.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #19

challenges.content: Peter, if you want to lose weight, you need to be disciplined,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #20

challenges.content: in both what you eat, and what you do,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #21

challenges.content: which brings us to the issue of exercise.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #22

challenges.content: That's right.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #23

challenges.content: So, jogging twice a week, and hiking on Saturdays, right?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #24

challenges.content: No, hiking is Sundays,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #25

challenges.content: allowing Saturdays for the light walking exercise.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #26

challenges.content: I've investigated, and discovered there are a lot of walking trails around this suburb,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #27

challenges.content: with many beautiful places if you just look around.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #28

challenges.content: So what's happening this Saturday?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #29

challenges.content: A walk around the city?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #30

challenges.content: That's later in the month.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #31

challenges.content: This Saturday we'll visit Pine Park.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #32

challenges.content: Hill Park is nicer, with great views, too.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #33

challenges.content: Yes, but we have to travel too far to reach Hill Park,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #34

challenges.content: so I ruled that out, and I love the smell of pines.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #35

challenges.content: And what about the weekday meals?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #36

challenges.content: Salads every night, I suppose?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #37

challenges.content: No, it's important to vary the meals so that the food remains interesting and fun.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #38

challenges.content: The only common factor is the fruit juice,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #39

challenges.content: but otherwise we'll have a variety of healthy fare,
challenges.explanation: fare: a range of food of a particular type.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #40

challenges.content: from salads, to fish, to lean meat.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #41

challenges.content: I'd rather have meat every night, but you're the boss.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #42

challenges.content: If you want to lose weight, you'll have to accept this program, okay?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #43

challenges.content: Okay.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #44

challenges.content: Now Mary, you said we could have a little treat in our diet plan three times a week:
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #45

challenges.content: specifically, Tuesdays, Thursdays, and Sundays.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #46

challenges.content: Yes. A very small treat, but something to reward us for all the discipline shown.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #47

challenges.content: Such rewards will motivate us to continue the diet.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #48

challenges.content: So, on Tuesdays, what can I choose?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #49

challenges.content: You have a choice between a small serving of chocolate, ice cream, or biscuits.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #50

challenges.content: Okay, well, I'll go for the biscuits.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #51

challenges.content: I love those crunchy little things with my cup of tea.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #52

challenges.content: So do you, right?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #53

challenges.content: I do indeed, so I'll have them, too, saving the ice cream for later.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #54

challenges.content: But I know how much you like ice cream,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #55

challenges.content: so why don't you save it for the end of the week?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #56

challenges.content: That will give you the motivation to keep going,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #57

challenges.content: and you can have chocolate midweek?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #58

challenges.content: That's a good idea,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #59

challenges.content: but I think the most important thing is for you and I to eat different things on those other two days.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #60

challenges.content: Well, if you think that way,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #61

challenges.content: I'll eat the ice cream on Thursdays, not the chocolate. Okay?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #62

challenges.content: Well, if you're having that, then I can't have ice cream.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #63

challenges.content: In order to be different, I'll have the chocolate.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #64

challenges.content: So, we can compare our different snacks,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #65

challenges.content: and maybe even share a little with each other.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #66

challenges.content: Exactly! And the variety and fun involved will take our minds of wanting more.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #67

challenges.content: Eating for fun! A good idea!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #68

challenges.content: And then you can have the chocolate on Sunday, right?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #69

challenges.content: But I like biscuits?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #70

challenges.content: Actually, I want biscuits again - to have with my cup of tea.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #71

challenges.content: But you have the biscuits on Monday, remember, and we can't repeat.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #72

challenges.content: Ah come on! This isn't fixed in concrete.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #73

challenges.content: I can have them again instead of chocolate.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #74

challenges.content: You might like variety, but I don't.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #75

challenges.content: I'm a creature of habit.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #76

challenges.content: Well, the whole point of this was to taste different snacks,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #77

challenges.content: but if you want the same thing, okay.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #78

challenges.content: I, for one, am sticking to the original plan,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #79

challenges.content: with ice cream to finish the week, and not another dose of chocolate.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 2 - Part 1 - challenge #80

challenges.content: Most of us are familiar with a local park.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #1

challenges.content: We spend time there, play there, and have some of our best memories in these places.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #2

challenges.content: But what is a park?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #3

challenges.content: Basically, it can be defined as a natural, or at least semi-natural, piece of land,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #4

challenges.content: planted with a variety of trees, bushes, and flowers,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #5

challenges.content: protected and reserved for the enjoyment of all citizens.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #6

challenges.content: There are usually regulations about the sorts of behaviour that can take place within.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #7

challenges.content: And sometimes there are facilities such as children's playgrounds,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #8

challenges.content: or fields for ball games and other sorts of activities.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #9

challenges.content: For this reason, if there is grass, it is kept short,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #10

challenges.content: and this also discourages the breeding of insect pests.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #11

challenges.content: A well-maintained park actually needs a lot of people to look after it,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #12

challenges.content: and more so if the park showcases special plants,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #13

challenges.content: flowers, or trees, in which case it is called a 'botanic garden'.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #14

challenges.content: In complete contrast, if the park is big and remote enough,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #15
