challenges.content: it is sometimes designated as a wilderness park,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #16

challenges.content: to be left completely alone and untouched,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #17

challenges.content: protected from all development in order to allow wild species,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #18

challenges.content: both plant and animal, to live undisturbed.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #19

challenges.content: But it is the urban park - the sort of park that most people are familiar with,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #20

challenges.content: that I want to talk about now.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #21

challenges.content: These preserve natural landscapes for the pleasure of the urban population,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #22

challenges.content: most commonly just for passive recreation
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #23

challenges.content: in other words, allowing people just to observe the trees, and lie in the grass,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #24

challenges.content: and such passive recreation is certainly needed.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #25

challenges.content: Continuing on the subject of parks,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #26

challenges.content: it might surprise you to know that once there were none.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #27

challenges.content: A thousand years ago, there was no need,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #28

challenges.content: since there were already extensive open spaces,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #29

challenges.content: forests, and wilderness surrounding most cities and towns - for example, in Europe.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #30

challenges.content: These dark dank forests were large and even dangerous,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #31

challenges.content: full of wild animals and with the potentially fatal result of getting lost.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #32

challenges.content: Hence, fairy tales evolved about witches living in these areas,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #33

challenges.content: and the wolves and bears, which could threaten young children.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #34

challenges.content: However, with the rapidly increasing human population,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #35

challenges.content: the original wilderness and natural open spaces were intruded upon.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #36

challenges.content: Forests were cut down as populations spread,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #37

challenges.content: and with them, urban pollution and further deforestation.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #38

challenges.content: But it was only with the advent of the Industrial Revolution
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #39

challenges.content: that people realised natural areas needed to be preserved,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #40

challenges.content: to give the populace access to the sort of nature that was fast disappearing
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #41

challenges.content: due to the uncontrolled development and demand for resources.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #42

challenges.content: The first park, expressly designed for that purpose,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #43

challenges.content: is usually considered to be Princes Park in Liverpool.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #44

challenges.content: This was in 1841, on land donated to the public by a rich iron merchant.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #45

challenges.content: With such a generous donation (worth about £50,000),
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #46

challenges.content: the council decided to invest £5,000 of its own money in making it look good.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #47

challenges.content: Consequently, they hired a landscape designer, Joseph Paxton,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #48

challenges.content: who designed twisting turning pathways among shade-giving trees,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #49

challenges.content: all based around a central lake.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #50

challenges.content: In many ways, it became the prototype for all later large parks,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #51

challenges.content: including the famous Central Park in New York.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #52

challenges.content: But, if we were to pick the park that most people are familiar with,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #53

challenges.content: it would be the much smaller neighbourhood park.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #54

challenges.content: These can be tiny, but, by being in the midst of extensive development and dense populations,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #55

challenges.content: they are increasingly seen as a refuge,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #56

challenges.content: where one can get a glimpse of true nature.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #57

challenges.content: Many psychologists now maintain that this glimpse is necessary,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #58

challenges.content: for ultimately, as a species, we have an innate affinity for nature,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #59

challenges.content: and the concrete urban zoo clashes with our inner being.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #60

challenges.content: This has seen the rejuvenation of many urban parks that were once left to decay,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #61

challenges.content: for example, in New York or London,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #62

challenges.content: and indeed, some cities, such as Melbourne,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #63

challenges.content: are known all over the world for their abundance of carefully maintained parks,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #64

challenges.content: including a world famous botanic garden.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 4 - challenge #65

challenges.content: Hi Liz. How do you feel about starting university here?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #1

challenges.content: A little bit nervous, but I'm confident I can handle it.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #2

challenges.content: This orientation program seems like it will help us a lot.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #3

challenges.content: Sure. I'm looking at the timetable here myself.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #4

challenges.content: It seems that there are choices available.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #5

challenges.content: I can see.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #6

challenges.content: So, what are you going to do Monday afternoon?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #7

challenges.content: In the morning we all have the opening lecture,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #8

challenges.content: but it looks like we have a choice later that day, as you said.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #9

challenges.content: Well, the 'Careers Lecture' might be helpful,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #10

challenges.content: but I am interested in the 'Uni Tour'.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #11

challenges.content: It's probably too early to be thinking of careers now, anyway,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #12

challenges.content: and I want to know what's what at this new university, so I'm doing the tour.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #13

challenges.content: Alright. I'll come along with you.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #14

challenges.content: Might learn something interesting.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #15

challenges.content: After all, we haven't seen much of this place yet,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #16

challenges.content: and we will be spending four years here.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #17

challenges.content: Tuesday is another full day, too.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #18

challenges.content: In the afternoon there's a lecture about study skills,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #19

challenges.content: but that morning offers another choice.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #20

challenges.content: 'Library Tour' or 'Student Union Induction'.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #21

challenges.content: What do you think?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #22

challenges.content: I think the student union is very important,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #23

challenges.content: but we can go there any time, right,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #24

challenges.content: so we should take advantage of the library tour while it's being offered.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #25

challenges.content: Maybe the week after, you and I can go to the student union.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #26

challenges.content: Library it is, then.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #27

challenges.content: Now, Wednesday has a free session in the morning,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #28

challenges.content: but after lunch there's a choice between visiting the computer lab,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #29

challenges.content: or attending a lecture on our legal rights.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #30

challenges.content: Well, law and rights are important,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #31

challenges.content: but computers are the basis of everything these days,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #32

challenges.content: so I'm going to the computer lab.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #33

challenges.content: Don't you think knowing our legal rights is equally, if not more, important?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #34

challenges.content: We live in a very litigious and complex society now.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #35

challenges.content: Sure, but it's something we can pick up later,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #36

challenges.content: so let's leave that one out.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #37

challenges.content: Okay.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #38

challenges.content: Let me see the timetable.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #39

challenges.content: Thursday is a free day, and the week winds up with some celebrations on Friday afternoon.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #40

challenges.content: It looks like a fun choice, too.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #41

challenges.content: There's either a BBQ on the main lawn, or the dance.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #42

challenges.content: I never pass up the chance to eat something. What about you?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #43

challenges.content: If I can get a free meal, I'll take it any day,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #44

challenges.content: and I'm not good at dancing anyway.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #45

challenges.content: Well, that's that decided. Right?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #46

challenges.content: Right!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #47

challenges.content: Guess what Liz?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #48

challenges.content: There's another interesting thing in this orientation booklet,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #49

challenges.content: and it looks important - about a 'style guide'.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #50

challenges.content: What's that?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #51

challenges.content: Take a look yourself.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #52

challenges.content: It seems to be a set of rules regarding how to present written work -
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #53

challenges.content: essays, and that sort of thing - to the lecturers.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #54

challenges.content: They want a uniform style of presentation.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #55

challenges.content: I can see. So, everything we hand in must have a header and a footer.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #56

challenges.content: A what?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #57

challenges.content: A header and a footer.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #58

challenges.content: The footer is at the bottom of the page, and the header is at the very top.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #59

challenges.content: That's why they call it a 'header', you know,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #60

challenges.content: that little bit of writing giving details about the work.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #61

challenges.content: And they also want the word count.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #62

challenges.content: Why do they need that?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #63

challenges.content: I guess because the lecturers will specify the number of words they want for their assignment,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #64

challenges.content: and they want to be sure students follow this.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #65

challenges.content: And even the heading on the page has to be a specific dimension.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #66

challenges.content: 16 points, and bold print, and underlined.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #67

challenges.content: And subheadings are 14 points, and the font has to be Arial for everything.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #68

challenges.content: Yes, the main text is Arial, too, as you said, and the size is 12 points,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #69

challenges.content: with the header and footer being slightly smaller, at 10 points each.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #70

challenges.content: Well, it seems logical.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #71

challenges.content: The size of everything is in proportion to its importance,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #72

challenges.content: but why do they need the spacing of the main text to be one and a half?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #73

challenges.content: The header and footer are different.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #74

challenges.content: They're only single-spaced.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #75

challenges.content: Probably to allow the teacher to insert comments, or corrections,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #76

challenges.content: or just to make it all more readable, I suppose.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #77

challenges.content: And we need wide margins on the left, right, top, and bottom,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #78

challenges.content: probably for the same reason.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #79

challenges.content: Lots of space to allow the addition of comments.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #80

challenges.content: That's a bit scary, actually.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #81

challenges.content: It seems to assume we will be making mistakes.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #82

challenges.content: And look what they want in the header and footer.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #83

challenges.content: The header has the name of the work.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #84

challenges.content: Not the name of the teacher?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #85

challenges.content: No, the work, but surely the teacher's name must go somewhere.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #86

challenges.content: Ah, here it is. It goes in the footer.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #87

challenges.content: Okay, I'd say this is all logical.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #88

challenges.content: If a page is lost, say, falls to the floor,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #89

challenges.content: then with all this information, it can always be traced back to the teacher involved.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #90

challenges.content: Right - as you say, all very logical.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 3 - challenge #91

challenges.content: Hello everyone.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #1

challenges.content: Now, you're here because you're interested in travel, right?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #2

challenges.content: And you're in the right place,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #3

challenges.content: for at EasyTravel, we have the best deals for the best locations.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #4

challenges.content: We specialise in eco-travel,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #5

challenges.content: or holidays designed to get you amongst nature,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #6

challenges.content: ignoring the hustle and bustle of big cities.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #7

challenges.content: So, whether you want to hike in Nepal, as many people do,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #8

challenges.content: or follow some jungle paths in the rainforests of Queensland,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #9

challenges.content: we can give you the best deal.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #10

challenges.content: If you look at our office here, you'll see our overseas consultants.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #11

challenges.content: That's for trips overseas, obviously, to Europe, to North America,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #12

challenges.content: but primarily for the Asian market,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #13

challenges.content: which is generally more popular in this part of the world.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #14

challenges.content: Most people like that touch of the Orient, right?
challenges.explanation:
"a touch of something" means "a small amount of something"

The Orient is the eastern part of Asia. The Orient includes countries and regions like Japan, China, Korea, Hong Kong and Taiwan, etc.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #15

challenges.content: But they also like the domestic market,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #16

challenges.content: since this country offers its fair share of beautiful natural vistas.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #17

challenges.content: What about the deserts, anyone?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #18

challenges.content: What about some striking red-rock gorges?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #19

challenges.content: Then, talk to our domestic consultants, who can arrange anything you want.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #20

challenges.content: But they deal with the accounts in the morning,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #21

challenges.content: so you'll need to talk to them in the afternoon.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #22

challenges.content: And remember, our office doesn't open at night, sorry to say.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #23

challenges.content: Now, around the outskirts and outer regions of this city,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #24

challenges.content: there are many beautiful places that you might not be aware of.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #25

challenges.content: And the advantages of these regional locations are many.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #26

challenges.content: Mostly, by being closer, some of them can be done in a day tour.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #27

challenges.content: Yes, it's fast and convenient, with none of those long-haul bus trips
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #28

challenges.content: which often leave you cramped and uncomfortable,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #29

challenges.content: and stuffing heavy suitcases into luggage racks.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #30

challenges.content: But, I should tell you about our buses,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #31

challenges.content: those that are needed for the somewhat more distant holiday destinations.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #32

challenges.content: They definitely do not suffer from those problems I just mentioned.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #33

challenges.content: We use the services of the famous Sleek Line Company,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #34

challenges.content: whose buses are known as the very best.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #35

challenges.content: Yes, they are big, yes, they are comfortable,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #36

challenges.content: but what makes them especially different is the personal attendant,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #37

challenges.content: who accompanies the driver, ready and willing to serve you,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #38

challenges.content: and ensure that your trip is the very best.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #39

challenges.content: So, whether it's overseas or local, we can certainly give you what you want.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #40

challenges.content: Now, do you have any questions?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #41

challenges.content: Right, let me orient you to our main EasyTravel office here.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #42

challenges.content: On this table right beside us are travel magazines for you to browse through,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #43

challenges.content: and on the wall next to that are many more, for all parts of the world.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #44

challenges.content: Our four travel consultants sit over there, on the other side of that long counter.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #45

challenges.content: That's right, four of them, side by side,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #46

challenges.content: all serving various regions.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #47

challenges.content: Now, let me tell you their specific functions.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #48

challenges.content: Firstly, the consultant on the left, next to the plant,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #49

challenges.content: is the 'Local Tours' consultant,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #50

challenges.content: serving tours in the immediate vicinity of this city.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #51

challenges.content: Next to her is what we call 'Regional Tours',
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #52

challenges.content: targeting the state-wide options.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #53

challenges.content: Next to her is the 'Interstate-Tours',
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #54

challenges.content: and that can involve either buses or planes,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #55

challenges.content: in the former case, utilising the SleekLine Bus service, as you know.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #56

challenges.content: And finally, next to her, in the corner, is 'General Enquiries',
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #57

challenges.content: which is self-explanatory.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #58

challenges.content: If you have questions of a general nature,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #59

challenges.content: rather than one relating to specific destinations, you can go there.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #60

challenges.content: Now, as I said, we can do international tours,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #61

challenges.content: and for that you need our big office, just through that door -
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #62

challenges.content: the one between those two plants.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #63

challenges.content: However, if your international tour is in the Asian region,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #64

challenges.content: which is generally our most popular option,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #65

challenges.content: then we deal with that in a separate room
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #66

challenges.content: the one opposite International Tours, but not; the corner one.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #67

challenges.content: Just go through that door on the left - the one next to that cupboard.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #68

challenges.content: The door next to that is, in fact, our General Office,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #69

challenges.content: so please don't go through there.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #70

challenges.content: That's reserved for staff members only.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 2 - challenge #71

challenges.content: Well, we have this school excursion planned, but when exactly is it?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #1

challenges.content: Is it this Tuesday or Wednesday?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #2

challenges.content: Well it can't be Tuesday, with the English tests taking place.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #3

challenges.content: Ah, right. Not Tuesday, but Wednesday.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #4

challenges.content: That's right - all day Wednesday - taking a bus outside the city.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #5

challenges.content: And where are we going?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #6

challenges.content: Ah, last month we went to Arthur Island,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #7

challenges.content: so this time we're going to the... Animal Park
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #8

challenges.content: Arthur Island was okay, but it was too cold.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #9

challenges.content: Let's hope the weather for this week's excursion is better.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #10

challenges.content: I don't suppose animals care about bad weather, but I certainly do.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #11

challenges.content: Have you heard the forecast?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #12

challenges.content: Yes, and it's not too bad.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #13

challenges.content: Basically, they're saying Monday will be sunny.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #14

challenges.content: Good...
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #15

challenges.content: But then the weather will change.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #16

challenges.content: Not so good.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #17

challenges.content: Yes, Tuesday we'll have some showers,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #18

challenges.content: but by Wednesday, the day of our excursion, it will be...
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #19

challenges.content: well, their words are "cold and cloudy".
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #20

challenges.content: Cold and cloudy. Well, as long as it isn't 'wet and rainy', I'm happy enough.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #21

challenges.content: We won't need umbrellas, just warm clothing.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #22

challenges.content: And what time will we get there?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #23

challenges.content: Let's see. The bus picks us up at 8:30 am,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #24

challenges.content: and then it's an hour and a half on the road, so we arrive at 10 a.m...
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #25

challenges.content: sorry, with the 15-minute break, that will actually be 10:15 a.m.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #26

challenges.content: That's early enough.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #27

challenges.content: Then all our students can see the animals, have their fun, and do whatever they want to do.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #28

challenges.content: Well, one fun event planned that day is 'Birds of Prey'.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #29

challenges.content: What's that?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #30

challenges.content: That's when they bring out several birds of prey:
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #31

challenges.content: eagles, falcons, kites, those sorts of birds,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #32

challenges.content: and throw pieces of meat into the air,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #33

challenges.content: and the birds swoop down and eat them.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #34

challenges.content: It's quite impressive.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #35

challenges.content: Sounds great. 'Birds of Prey'.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #36

challenges.content: Are there any other activities?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #37

challenges.content: There's a catered lunch, at the park restaurant.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #38

challenges.content: We've already paid for that, and in the afternoon there's...
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #39

challenges.content: well, I had a choice between the 'Reptile Display' and the 'Koala Handling'.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #40

challenges.content: In the reptile display, the students can handle live pythons and various other snakes.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #41

challenges.content: Surely they'd rather hold koalas?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #42

challenges.content: I'm sure, but the koalas can't be handled unless the weather's sunny, and given the forecast,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #43

challenges.content: I thought it better to choose the reptile display.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #44

challenges.content: Ummm, that's a shame.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #45

challenges.content: These Asian students would love the 'Koala Handling'.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #46

challenges.content: Yes, I know, but we can't control the weather.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #47

challenges.content: And, then we get back. What time will that be?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #48

challenges.content: We leave the park at 4:30, but then we face traffic,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #49

challenges.content: so we won't get back until well after 6 pm.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #50

challenges.content: It will most likely be 6:30.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #51

challenges.content: But that's better than the last trip: we didn't get home until 8:30 that time.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #52

challenges.content: Yes, that was a bit too late, wasn't it?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #53

challenges.content: Andrew, I understand you've been doing some research regarding the breakdown, by nationality of our student body.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #54

challenges.content: That must've produced some interesting results.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #55

challenges.content: You're right. I got some statistics from head office.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #56

challenges.content: I would imagine that most of our students are either Japanese or Chinese.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #57

challenges.content: You imagine right.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #58

challenges.content: But it's the Chinese who constitute the majority, but only just.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #59

challenges.content: I had thought Koreans might be second,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #60

challenges.content: but it's actually the Japanese, quite close behind.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #61

challenges.content: It's somewhat surprising, but obviously all those Study Tours that our university markets in Japan are bringing in students.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #62

challenges.content: What's the breakdown exactly?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #63

challenges.content: Japanese are a quarter of the whole, which is considerable.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #64

challenges.content: Last year they were only 16%, so that market has grown nicely.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #65

challenges.content: Ah, the only other proportions of some weight are the Indonesians and Koreans - about the same.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #66

challenges.content: Indonesians at 15%, and...
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #67

challenges.content: the Koreans are a little higher -
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #68

challenges.content: not like last year when they were less than 10%.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #69

challenges.content: I thought we'd have more Indonesians than Koreans?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #70

challenges.content: Well, as I said, they're about the same
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #71

challenges.content: just like the Saudi and Thai student numbers, almost the same also -
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #72

challenges.content: both just under 10.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #73

challenges.content: Which one is bigger?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #74

challenges.content: Thai students number just a fraction more.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #75

challenges.content: As for the other nationalities, collectively they're only 3%,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #76

challenges.content: so it wasn't worth giving each of them a separate category.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #77

challenges.content: I just grouped them under 'other'
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #78

challenges.content: that's Vietnamese, South American, a couple of Russians, and so on.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 1 - Part 1 - challenge #79

challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #1

challenges.content: Today, we will continue our study of Crocodylus niloticus by talking about its living habits.
challenges.explanation:
Crocodylus niloticus

The Nile crocodile (Crocodylus niloticus) is an African crocodile, the largest freshwater predator in Africa.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #2

challenges.content: We've already discussed the evolutionary attributes that set it apart from its crocodile relatives.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #3

challenges.content: Does everyone remember that?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #4

challenges.content: Yes, it has an extremely narrow snout, and 3 or 4 rows of protective scales on its back,
challenges.explanation:
snout

the nose and mouth of some animals, humans don't have snouts

A dog with long snout and a dog with short snout
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #5

challenges.content: as compared to 2 rows on other members of the Crocodylus genus.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #6

challenges.content: Let's take a look at how these carnivorous man-eaters live,
challenges.explanation:
carnivorous

a carnivorous animal is an animal that eats meat or other animals
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #7

challenges.content: where they live, and finally, whether they really deserve their vicious reputation.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #8

challenges.content: To start, I'd like to address a great question posed to me by a student during yesterday's office hours.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #9

challenges.content: We talked about the distribution of crocodiles in Africa
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #10

challenges.content: and saw that they are highly concentrated in the South and West of the continent.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #11

challenges.content: This student noticed that on the map displaying the distribution of crocodiles across Africa,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #12

challenges.content: there were no crocodiles in the Northern Region,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #13

challenges.content: and found no mention in the literature of the existence of crocodiles in the North of Africa.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #14

challenges.content: Why might there be no crocodiles in North Africa?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #15

challenges.content: Let's save this question for later in the lecture.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #16

challenges.content: To find out more about the social habits of the African crocodile,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #17

challenges.content: one researcher named Tara Shine of the University of Ulster in Northern Ireland
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #18

challenges.content: conducted a survey of the wetlands in Mauritania
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #19

challenges.content: and received reports of 46 crocodiles living in one group,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #20

challenges.content: or float as we say when referring to crocodiles,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #21

challenges.content: though the usual number is a little less than half of that.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #22

challenges.content: In general, crocodiles are more highly concentrated in wet, subtropical environments
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #23

challenges.content: near bodies of water and rich vegetation.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #24

challenges.content: While South American crocodiles thrive in cool rainforests,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #25

challenges.content: the African crocodile is more equipped for heat.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #26

challenges.content: Though they can survive at the hot temperatures found in some deserts,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #27

challenges.content: they're not equipped to handle dry climates
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #28

challenges.content: and thus cannot survive in places like the Sahara Desert of North Africa.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #29

challenges.content: As cold-blooded animals,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #30

challenges.content: crocodiles' core temperatures fluctuate from their average of 38 degrees Celsius as external conditions change,
challenges.explanation:
fluctuate

if something fluctuates, it changes continuously in number or amount
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #31

challenges.content: thus they need to avoid extreme temperatures.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #32

challenges.content: Others live an underwater life, keeping a body temperature close to that of the water.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #33

challenges.content: As their own unique method of regulating their body temperatures,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #34

challenges.content: some African crocodiles have made dens
challenges.explanation:
den

a den is a home of some types of wild animals, usually a hole
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #35

challenges.content: by digging holes in the ground to provide themselves with a cool, dark place to retreat from the hot African sun.
challenges.explanation:
retreat

to go away or escape from something, to avoid something
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #36

challenges.content: Speaking of the hot African sun,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #37

challenges.content: let's go back to the question asked at the beginning of the lecture.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #38

challenges.content: We know that there used to be crocodiles in Northern Africa, yet today there are none.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #39

challenges.content: What are some possible explanations for this?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #40

challenges.content: Some students have suggested that the African crocodile has evolved
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #41

challenges.content: from a desert creature into a wetland creature,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #42

challenges.content: thus causing them to migrate south for more appropriate conditions.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #43

challenges.content: Others presume the crocodile was hunted out of Northern Africa by a fiercer predator.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #44

challenges.content: While these are intelligent guesses, the real story is a little bit different.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #45

challenges.content: The key to this migration is that the Sahara Desert did not always cover the North of Africa.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #46

challenges.content: About 8,000 years ago, the land was fertile wetlands perfect for breeding crocodiles.
challenges.explanation:
fertile

a fertile land is a land that's very good for plants to grow
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #47

challenges.content: Over time, though, the area dried out and the wetland slowly turned to desert,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #48

challenges.content: leading the African crocodile to migrate south to the marshlands they call home today.
challenges.explanation:
marshland

wetland, a land that is usually at the edge of a stream or river, with many plants
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #49

challenges.content: Some crocodiles did, however, adapt to living in dry conditions.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #50

challenges.content: In Mauritania, some crocodiles have learned to survive in an area where they can go up to 8 months with no water
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #51

challenges.content: by spending the driest of times in what's called a torpor, or short period of hibernation.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #52

challenges.content: To utilise every bit of rainfall,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #53

challenges.content: these desert crocodiles dig underground caves that collect runoff,
challenges.explanation:
runoff

water that flows from high areas to low areas
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #54

challenges.content: thus staying cool and hydrated.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #55

challenges.content: During the mating period in November and December,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #56

challenges.content: males attract females to their viciously protected territory through a number of behaviours
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #57

challenges.content: that range from snapping their jaws all the way to sending infrasonic pulses through the water.
challenges.explanation:
snap

make a quick, sudden sound

finger snapping


infrasonic

an infrasonic sound is a sound with very low frequency that humans cannot hear but some animals can hear
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #58

challenges.content: Afterwards, the female digs a hole up to 60 centimetres in depth
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #59

challenges.content: to store the eggs for an 80-day incubation period.
challenges.explanation:
incubation

when an animal incubates its eggs, it keeps them warm until the baby comes out
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #60

challenges.content: The female protects these eggs during the period,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #61

challenges.content: and sometimes even helps crack the eggs with her snout at the end.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #62

challenges.content: These teeth-gnashing carnivores are softer than we think.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #63

challenges.content: Although these vicious creatures have attacked humans on a few occasions,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #64

challenges.content: the residents are not afraid of them.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #65

challenges.content: In fact, they show a great deal of reverence towards these wondrous creatures.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #66

challenges.content: Some say that crocodiles bring water to their habitat,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #67

challenges.content: so if they leave, they will bring the water with them.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #68

challenges.content: Obviously this is not true,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #69

challenges.content: but it demonstrates the admiration the inhabiting people have for crocodiles.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #70

challenges.content: Generally, crocodiles do not predate on humans.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #71

challenges.content: They attack when humans populate the crocodiles' habitat,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #72

challenges.content: instilling fear and uneasiness in the crocs.
challenges.explanation:
instill

gradually create a feeling or an idea..
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #73

challenges.content: Like any other species, crocodiles are known to attack when feeling fear.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #74

challenges.content: There's still a lot more to be discovered about the African crocodile.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #75

challenges.content: Researchers want to know more about the population size,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #76

challenges.content: how many crocodiles inhabit Africa in all,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #77

challenges.content: how they form separate floats, etc.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #78

challenges.content: There is still also much to learn about migration patterns,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #79

challenges.content: and relations to other populations of crocodiles now found in other parts of the world.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #80

challenges.content: Next time, we'll examine a few specific case studies of crocodile populations in Southern Africa.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 4 - challenge #81

challenges.content: Welcome! Please come in and gather over here around the tables.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #1

challenges.content: My name is Adam Smith, and I'm the librarian here.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #2

challenges.content: I'll show you around today and explain how to use these facilities.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #3

challenges.content: Hopefully when I'm done with it, you'll know the ropes,
challenges.explanation:
know the ropes

understand or know how to do something
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #4

challenges.content: and please feel free to let me know of any questions or concerns that you may have.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #5

challenges.content: Now, we're at the gate of the library.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #6

challenges.content: Upon entering into the door, you'll find that the restrooms are on your left-hand side,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #7

challenges.content: and opposite them is a Photocopy Room.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #8

challenges.content: Many of you are wondering about the check-in and check-out process.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #9

challenges.content: What you have to do is go to the Circulation Desk,
challenges.explanation:
Circulation Desk

Also known as the checkout counter, the circulation desk is where you can borrow materials, pay fines, and pick up requests, usually, it's near the entrance of the building.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #10

challenges.content: which is to the east of the Photocopy Room.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #11

challenges.content: The Reading Room is a really large area in the centre of the library,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #12

challenges.content: just to the north of the Circulation Desk.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #13

challenges.content: I'm sure you won't miss it.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #14

challenges.content: If you're here to do research, this is where you should bring books to look through.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #15

challenges.content: However, if you're here to do any group projects or other interactive activities,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #16

challenges.content: I advise you to use one of the study rooms,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #17

challenges.content: which are just to the east of the Reading Room.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #18

challenges.content: Moving on to the southeast corner,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #19

challenges.content: we have the Periodicals Section, just next to the study rooms.
challenges.explanation:
periodicals

magazines or newspapers that are published regularly
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #20

challenges.content: We have a collection of different newspapers and magazines in this section.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #21

challenges.content: You can get last week's weather reports, or all the top stories 5 years ago,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #22

challenges.content: our periodicals can be traced back 20 years to the time when our school library was built.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #23

challenges.content: Ah, our first question! Yes?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #24

challenges.content: Can we check out magazines from the library?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #25

challenges.content: I'm sorry, but you cannot take any periodicals out of the library.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #26

challenges.content: You're welcome to read them for as long as you want while you're here,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #27

challenges.content: but you cannot check them out.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #28

challenges.content: I wonder if there is any place where we can get some food in the library.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #29

challenges.content: Do we have a store here?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #30

challenges.content: Of course.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #31

challenges.content: The Food Service Centre is just metres away from the study rooms.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #32

challenges.content: It's on the northeast corner as you look at the map.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #33

challenges.content: The Food Service Centre offers different kinds of snacks though it's not big.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #34

challenges.content: Well, moving on along to the west,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #35

challenges.content: you will find the Video Resource Centre on your right hand.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #36

challenges.content: We have educational videos and documentaries, as well as major motion pictures.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #37

challenges.content: We ask that you pay attention to the tag on the video that you pick up,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #38

challenges.content: as many of our documentaries are for on-site viewing only and may not be taken out of the library.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #39

challenges.content: To the west of the Video Resource Centre is our Satellite TV Station.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #40

challenges.content: Here we stream the news from Channel 19 for most of the day.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #41

challenges.content: How many channels does it have?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #42

challenges.content: It does have nearly 200 channels,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #43

challenges.content: but we generally will give top priority to channels with some big events,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #44

challenges.content: like presidential addresses or other breaking news.
challenges.explanation:
presidential addresses

speeches or written statements, usually formal, from the president of an organization or a country.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #45

challenges.content: During the coverage of the presidential debate,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #46

challenges.content: students will take a break from studying and flock to watch it.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #47

challenges.content: Last but perhaps most important is the Enquiry Desk.
challenges.explanation:
Enquiry Desk

A section of an office, business etc, which answers questions or provides information for visitors or customers.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #48

challenges.content: It's just on the left-hand side when you walk into the library,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #49

challenges.content: so it's impossible to miss it.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #50

challenges.content: If you have any questions about how to use equipment or where to find something, come and ask the assistant.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #51

challenges.content: Don't be shy, because that's what they're here for!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #52

challenges.content: Speaking of questions,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #53

challenges.content: one of the questions we get asked is how to actually check out a book once a student has picked one out.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #54

challenges.content: If it's a fiction or non-fiction book,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #55

challenges.content: look for the pink and yellow check-out card inside the back cover of the book.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #56

challenges.content: You can also find information about the book on these cards,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #57

challenges.content: including its publishing date, genre, ISBN, and a log of dates it's been checked out before.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #58

challenges.content: Present this card to me or any library assistant,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #59

challenges.content: and we'll stamp it and then the book can be kept for 3 weeks.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #60

challenges.content: You can find general information on a field of study by using one of our subject guides.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #61

challenges.content: We have them on paper here, but any of our computers will allow you to search within fields as well.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #62

challenges.content: What if the library doesn't have a resource we're looking for?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #63

challenges.content: Great question, I'm going to address that.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #64

challenges.content: Our library is a network with a number of other universities in the area,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #65

challenges.content: so if there is something you're looking for and it's available somewhere in the area,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #66

challenges.content: we'll be able to get it for you.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #67

challenges.content: However, there are universities which are not part of the network,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #68

challenges.content: so we do not share resources with them.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #69

challenges.content: If you want more information about the library and its resources,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #70

challenges.content: you'll find it in a labelled blue folder on my desk in the enquiry section.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #71

challenges.content: Okay, so that's a lot of information all at once,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #72

challenges.content: and I don't expect you to remember it all.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #73

challenges.content: The most important thing is, please be respectful of the staff
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #74

challenges.content: and if you need help with anything at all, come and ask me or one of the assistants.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #75

challenges.content: Alright, any questions?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 3 - challenge #76

challenges.content: Hi everyone, and welcome to Sydney Airport.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #1

challenges.content: Today, I'll be giving you the inside information on the day-to-day operations of the Australian Quarantine Service here.
challenges.explanation:
quarantine

isolate, separate people or animal that might have a disease
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #2

challenges.content: We hope to provide you with a better understanding of why such heavy security regulations are necessary
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #3

challenges.content: by educating you on how we operate and why we do the things we do.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #4

challenges.content: We're not here to try to persuade you to fly through Sydney Airport,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #5

challenges.content: though we hope you'll find your experience relatively stress-free and comfortable.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #6

challenges.content: First things first, our personnel.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #7

challenges.content: Can anyone guess how many people work at Sydney Airport?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #8

challenges.content: We have 200 alone working in Terminal 2,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #9

challenges.content: so can you guess how many in the whole airport?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #10

challenges.content: I heard someone say 360, that's getting closer...
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #11

challenges.content: What?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #12

challenges.content: Did someone say 2,000?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #13

challenges.content: That's way too high.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #14

challenges.content: Sydney Airport actually employs 440 people.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #15

challenges.content: A lot, right?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #16

challenges.content: And about half of those employees work in security-related matters.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #17

challenges.content: Moving on to our not-so-human employees,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #18

challenges.content: let's come and see our favourite pooch, Milton.
challenges.explanation:
pooch

pooch is a slang term for "a dog"
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #19

challenges.content: Milton is our best drug-sniffing dog on the force.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #20

challenges.content: He's friendly to most people - you can even come pet him at the end of our tour.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #21

challenges.content: Burnouts beware, though, he'll find everything.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #22

challenges.content: Notice that even though there are so many of us around him, Milton stays quite calm.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #23

challenges.content: This is the precise reason he was chosen for the job.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #24

challenges.content: Dogs that are chosen are not predisposed to sniff out different narcotics,
challenges.explanation:
predisposed to

likely, inclined, willing

narcotic

a drug or other substance affecting mood or behavior and sold for non-medical purposes, especially an illegal one.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #25

challenges.content: that's something we teach them already.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #26

challenges.content: So here's a part of the airport most people never notice - the cargo transport terminal.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #27

challenges.content: This is where packages are shipped to and from.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #28

challenges.content: Normally we ship around 4,400 packages per month.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #29

challenges.content: In this airport alone, over 52,000 packages were shipped in and out over the past year.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #30

challenges.content: We ship to and from 170 different countries.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #31

challenges.content: Not bad, eh?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #32

challenges.content: Probably it will go up to over 72,000 packages this year.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #33

challenges.content: And despite over 100 flights in and out of here daily,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #34

challenges.content: the number of lost or delayed packages is impressively low.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #35

challenges.content: If you send your package through here, rest assured we'll get it where it's going.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #36

challenges.content: Let's move on to the area most of us are familiar with, the passenger terminals.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #37

challenges.content: In order to be allowed into this area, you must pass through security with your ticket
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #38

challenges.content: and if you're travelling internationally, your passport.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #39

challenges.content: If you're travelling domestically, you just need a legal form of ID.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #40

challenges.content: If you don't have those, you will not be allowed to pass through security and board your flight.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #41

challenges.content: During the security scan,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #42

challenges.content: your carry-on items will be checked for dangerous items such as weapons,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #43

challenges.content: sharp objects, and liquids that exceed our specified limit.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #44

challenges.content: If you attempt to pass any of the prohibited items on this list posted at the entrance,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #45

challenges.content: you are still allowed to board the plane,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #46

challenges.content: but you'll be given a warning and your item will be confiscated.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #47

challenges.content: Don't worry, we will not arrest you for having too much shampoo in your bag, or anything like that.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #48

challenges.content: We also search your carry-ons and parcels for any perishable items.
challenges.explanation:
perishable
