(especially of food) likely to spoil or go rotten quickly.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #49

challenges.content: We prohibit the transportation of local vegetation
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #50

challenges.content: and prohibit parcels containing any insects in them.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #51

challenges.content: You may or may not have learned about this in Biology class,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #52

challenges.content: but when some plants are introduced to a new environment,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #53

challenges.content: they spread wildly and wipe out the current species around it.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #54

challenges.content: It is important to control the introduction of new plants into an ecosystem,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #55

challenges.content: so we must prohibit the transport of any fertile seeds.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #56

challenges.content: So what happens to parcels containing possibly suspicious items?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #57

challenges.content: It's of course something we do not take lightly here.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #58

challenges.content: If an object passes through the scanner that appears suspicious in any way,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #59

challenges.content: it is separated out for manual search by a member of our trained security personnel.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #60

challenges.content: If an illegal plant or simple sharp object like a pocket knife is found,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #61

challenges.content: it is simply disposed of in our biohazard waste containers,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #62

challenges.content: and the package itself is returned to the sender
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #63

challenges.content: (or passenger, if it is for a passenger flight).
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #64

challenges.content: More serious weapons are reported to higher authorities for investigation.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #65

challenges.content: As far as parcel security, the material of the parcel is important.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #66

challenges.content: For shipped goods, the most common material used (and the most widely accepted) is paper.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #67

challenges.content: Make sure it is packed sturdy enough, with no rips or tears.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #68

challenges.content: We've definitely had packages rip open before due to haphazard packing.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #69

challenges.content: A more common problem, though, is the package labels.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #70

challenges.content: When an item does not make it to the right place, this is the most common reason.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #71

challenges.content: The label may not be in the right place or marked clearly enough.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #72

challenges.content: If you're receiving any items from abroad that must be declared,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #73

challenges.content: please remember our guidelines in order to ensure the timely delivery of your item.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #74

challenges.content: Make sure it is packed correctly,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #75

challenges.content: and we ask that you notify customs between 2 and 10 days within the item's scheduled arrival date.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #76

challenges.content: Okay, before we move on, are there any questions?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 2 - challenge #77

challenges.content: Good morning. City House Services. How may I help you?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #1

challenges.content: Good morning. I'd like to arrange to have my house cleaned.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #2

challenges.content: Certainly. I just need to ask a few questions.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #3

challenges.content: First, could I take your name?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #4

challenges.content: Yes, it's Barbara Hill.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #5

challenges.content: Thank you. Next, is your house in London?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #6

challenges.content: Yes, it's in Kingston in Southwest London.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #7

challenges.content: OK, Southwest London and... er, what's the postcode?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #8
IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #9

challenges.content: And what is the square footage and what rooms will we be cleaning?
challenges.explanation:
square footage

the measurement of area in square foot
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #10

challenges.content: The whole house is 268 square feet,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #11

challenges.content: and there is no need to clean all the rooms.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #12

challenges.content: I only want to have my bedrooms cleaned.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #13

challenges.content: OK, how many bedrooms does the house have?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #14

challenges.content: 3 bedrooms.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #15

challenges.content: Oh no, sorry, we used to have 3 bedrooms, but we only have 2 bedrooms now.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #16

challenges.content: Are those single bedrooms or doubles?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #17

challenges.content: Doubles.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #18

challenges.content: Fine, 2 doubles...
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #19

challenges.content: There's one more room which needs cleaning.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #20

challenges.content: It was used as a bedroom before, and now we have converted it into an office.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #21

challenges.content: I understand.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #22

challenges.content: 3 rooms have got to be cleaned, and are all of those rooms upstairs?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #23

challenges.content: Yes. Then, downstairs we have a kitchen-diner, conservatory, and lounge.
challenges.explanation:
conservatory

a room with glass walls and roofs


lounge

a room to sit and relax
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #24

challenges.content: The kitchen-diner is quite large and has the usual equipment:
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #25

challenges.content: cooker with oven, refrigerator, cupboards, and worktops.
challenges.explanation:
worktop

a flat surface in a kitchen where we prepare food
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #26

challenges.content: The conservatory has a lot of plants, but there's no need to take care of them.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #27

challenges.content: The lounge has a leather three-piece suite and a large coffee table.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #28

challenges.content: Thank you. And do you keep any pets?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #29

challenges.content: Yeah, I really love keeping them.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #30

challenges.content: I've got 2 dogs and 3 cats.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #31

challenges.content: OK, then if our staff come over to offer the service, please take your pets away.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #32

challenges.content: Have you looked at our service packages?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #33

challenges.content: Yes, I have one in front of me.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #34

challenges.content: Excellent.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #35

challenges.content: Any extra services you need,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #36

challenges.content: switching bed linen, working in the garden, cleaning the glass in the conservatory, that kind of thing?
challenges.explanation:
bed linen

bed sheets, pillowcases, and duvet covers...
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #37

challenges.content: Err... no... err...
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #38

challenges.content: actually, replacing the bed linen...
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #39

challenges.content: yeah.. that would be good.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #40

challenges.content: No problem. I'll just make a note of that.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #41

challenges.content: How about curtains, mats, and carpets?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #42

challenges.content: What would you like us to do with those items?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #43

challenges.content: The curtains... I'll have to think about that.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #44

challenges.content: I think we should have the carpets cleaned really well every quarter.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #45

challenges.content: Mats can just be done with the laundry.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #46

challenges.content: Of course.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #47

challenges.content: How about clothes?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #48

challenges.content: We can have our staff wash and iron them,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #49

challenges.content: or we can have them taken to a dry cleaner.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #50

challenges.content: Washing and ironing. No, just ironing. That'll be OK.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #51

challenges.content: OK, fine. I know quite a bit about what you want now.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #52

challenges.content: I should let you know that we are located on 12 Amyes Road,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #53

challenges.content: that's A-M-Y-E-S.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #54

challenges.content: And we work on from Monday to Sunday except Tuesday and Wednesday.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #55

challenges.content: Could you let me know when is convenient for you?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #56

challenges.content: Next Friday...
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #57

challenges.content: err... no, oh, that's no good.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #58

challenges.content: My son invites his friends over in the afternoon that day.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #59

challenges.content: Perhaps next Thursday or next Saturday.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #60

challenges.content: Let me check, OK, next Thursday.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #61

challenges.content: When is it convenient for us to come over and provide the service?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #62

challenges.content: Is it OK if we come in the morning?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #63

challenges.content: Or we may come in the afternoon? It depends on your schedule.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #64

challenges.content: I'm OK with any time.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #65

challenges.content: Just give me a call to let me know you're coming before you arrive.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #66

challenges.content: Sure, we will.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #67

challenges.content: By the way, how long will it take for the service?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #68

challenges.content: We usually work 1 to 3 hours for house cleaning,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #69

challenges.content: and the work will take 3 hours at most.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #70

challenges.content: And of course, if it takes more than 3 hours, you should pay extra for it.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #71

challenges.content: Er... fine.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #72

challenges.content: So, let me just do some calculations...
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 34 - Part 1 - challenge #73

challenges.content: Good morning and welcome to yet another lecture in Environmental Science.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #1

challenges.content: I don't think I'm telling you a secret when I mention that water is a big worry here in Australia.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #2

challenges.content: The stuff is scarce.
challenges.explanation:
scarce

rare, not easy to find or get
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #3

challenges.content: Perhaps that's why we drink so much beer, eh?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #4

challenges.content: Seriously, though, a safe and reliable source of water is one of the great concerns of people everywhere.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #5

challenges.content: Moreover, as the world population grows,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #6

challenges.content: the pressure on existing water supplies grows greater and greater.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #7

challenges.content: Think about it.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #8

challenges.content: Our economic system demands that there be more and more consumers.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #9

challenges.content: The growing number of people has been tied to climate change, including droughts.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #10

challenges.content: So more people means less water.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #11

challenges.content: But our economic system demands a high birth rate.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #12

challenges.content: Forget about oil. Soon enough you will see wars for water.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #13

challenges.content: Mark my words.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #14

challenges.content: But today, I'm going to confine my remarks to Australia.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #15

challenges.content: As noted already, here down under, the water supply is extremely scarce.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #16

challenges.content: The only drier continent is Antarctica
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #17

challenges.content: and remember, no one really lives there anyway.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #18

challenges.content: Moreover, in recent years, the wind patterns have changed.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #19

challenges.content: Rain that used to fall on the country now falls out to sea hundreds of miles to the south.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #20

challenges.content: Now, when I speak of people needing water, most of you probably think of drinking.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #21

challenges.content: Certainly everyone needs water for drinking.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #22

challenges.content: But surprising as it may sound,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #23

challenges.content: drinking is not anywhere near being the main use for water.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #24

challenges.content: Most water is actually used for washing.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #25

challenges.content: When you take a shower, you probably use well over a hundred litres of water.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #26

challenges.content: Every time you flush your toilet, that's about 8 litres.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #27

challenges.content: But most people drink no more than two litres or so per day.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #28

challenges.content: So, where to get water?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #29

challenges.content: It could be obtained from rainwater,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #30

challenges.content: but often rainfall consists of other harmful pollutants that evaporated with the water.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #31

challenges.content: In fact, acid rain, an intense example of this,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #32

challenges.content: causes harmful effects on the wildlife of the habitat on which it falls.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #33

challenges.content: Water from underground could also be used,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #34

challenges.content: though it is more difficult to contain
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #35

challenges.content: and often must go through an extensive cleansing process.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #36

challenges.content: The purest water is found in rivers, creeks, lakes, and dams.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #37

challenges.content: And, sad to say, Australia has precious few of these.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #38

challenges.content: Really, how many of your home towns have rivers?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #39

challenges.content: Year-round rivers, I mean.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #40

challenges.content: The soil tends to be sandy, so water soaks into the ground.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #41

challenges.content: Many places are rocky too,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #42

challenges.content: so 87% of the rainfall is lost to evaporation.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #43

challenges.content: That's almost twice the evaporation rate in my native Canada!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #44

challenges.content: Speaking of rain, we already heard how rainfall is diminishing here in Oceania.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #45

challenges.content: The quantity itself isn't the only problem, either.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #46

challenges.content: Going back to the problems with obtaining rainwater,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #47

challenges.content: a further problem is that rain is a useful source of water only if air pollution is fairly mild.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #48

challenges.content: Again, you're in a situation where you can't win.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #49

challenges.content: You need water where most people live.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #50

challenges.content: People tend to build cities where rainfall is adequate.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #51

challenges.content: But then modern cities tend to feature polluted air
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #52

challenges.content: which renders the rain far less easily usable.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #53

challenges.content: OK, let's take a look at the table here,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #54

challenges.content: you'll see it showing the relative pollution of rainfall in the world's cities.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #55

challenges.content: The more people, the dirtier the rain.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #56

challenges.content: This is becoming a huge concern for people in the West,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #57

challenges.content: who want their water to be pure and safe.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #58

challenges.content: Though reliable drinking water is important everywhere,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #59

challenges.content: the concern in the West is reflected in all the government regulations and political campaigns aimed at solving this problem.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #60

challenges.content: In contrast, there are not as many demands made on the governments in Asian and African cultures to improve the water,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #61

challenges.content: as their focus is on other issues.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #62

challenges.content: Now, whatever the source of water,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #63

challenges.content: we can never afford to forget that all water is highly vulnerable to contamination.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #64

challenges.content: Whether we're getting it from the ground, from bodies of water, or rainfall,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #65

challenges.content: it is susceptible to a variety of toxins.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #66

challenges.content: In fact, that's why we clean it before using it:
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #67

challenges.content: water carries with it filth and dirt.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #68

challenges.content: This problem shows up in a number of different ways.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #69

challenges.content: As humans and all other animals need water to survive,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #70

challenges.content: it's no surprise to us that one of the most important domestic uses of water is for drinking.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #71

challenges.content: Yet if you have old-fashioned lead pipes,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #72

challenges.content: you may slowly be poisoning yourself by drinking that nice clear water.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #73

challenges.content: The industrial pollution, farm chemicals, and leaky landfills
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #74

challenges.content: are well-known sources of contaminants as well.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #75

challenges.content: So what is being done to ensure we Australians a safe and steady supply of drinking water?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #76

challenges.content: There are a lot of initiatives that make admirable efforts to remedy this issue.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #77

challenges.content: We'll be talking about this when we meet again on Thursday.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #78

challenges.content: But, as a preview,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #79

challenges.content: I can tell you that so far the amount of real solutions that have been produced is not nearly adequate.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #80

challenges.content: Traditionally, we've been very free in this country.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #81

challenges.content: That means that every person and every province tend to go its own way.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #82

challenges.content: So the mechanisms for water management are, in a word, insufficient.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #83

challenges.content: To begin seeing how this is so, I want you to read something before our next class.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #84

challenges.content: Though a lot of previous data on water usage and water management are inconclusive
challenges.explanation:
inconclusive

uncertain, incomplete, ambiguous, up in the air...
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #85

challenges.content: and have thus caused quite a concern,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #86

challenges.content: we can learn a lot from the contents of reports written on the subject.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #87

challenges.content: The basis for the government's water policy is the 1989 White Paper
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #88

challenges.content: reporting on "Water Use: Present and Future".
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #89

challenges.content: If you compare the numbers offered in the paper with those in the text,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #90

challenges.content: you'll find that the report is rather untrustworthy.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #91

challenges.content: Truth being told, I'm being too kind when I say that!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 4 - challenge #92

challenges.content: Hi, Julie, it's Ricky.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #1

challenges.content: Hi, Ricky, how are you?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #2

challenges.content: I noticed you weren't in Psychology today.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #3

challenges.content: I'm feeling sick, so I didn't go to school today.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #4

challenges.content: Would you mind telling me what I missed in class?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #5

challenges.content: Sure thing. I'm sorry you're not feeling well!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #6

challenges.content: Anyway, we spent most of the class talking about a new essay that Professor Johnson assigned.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #7

challenges.content: You need to choose one of the bold headings from the note system and research it.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #8

challenges.content: Wow, I picked the wrong day to miss class, huh?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #9

challenges.content: You sure did.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #10

challenges.content: Could you tell me the specific requirements of this paper?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #11

challenges.content: Sure.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #12

challenges.content: You need to find scientific research that supports your claim as one of your references.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #13

challenges.content: It can be from some of the case studies we discussed in class, or you can find your own.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #14

challenges.content: Or even better, you can conduct your own research!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #15

challenges.content: I'm sure that would get you an A.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #16

challenges.content: Have you decided what you're going to do yet?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #17

challenges.content: Also, where are you getting your references?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #18

challenges.content: Yeah, I'm gonna research facial recognition by infants.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #19

challenges.content: I've already found a few experiments in scientific journals.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #20

challenges.content: That would probably be a good start for you - there are tons of journals in the library.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #21

challenges.content: Great idea, thanks.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #22

challenges.content: I'm considering writing my essay on the effects of one of the psychotropic drugs we talked about in class.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #23

challenges.content: I'm sure there is lots of stuff about it on the Internet.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #24

challenges.content: Are we allowed to use information from the Internet?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #25

challenges.content: Sure, you can use that as long as it's not your main source for information.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #26

challenges.content: You'll probably want to cite some of the experiments we went over.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #27

challenges.content: Good idea, thanks.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #28

challenges.content: I'm gonna try to find some information from a bunch of different sources.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #29

challenges.content: Are there any specifications on how the essay should be written?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #30

challenges.content: Yeah, Professor Johnson wants it double-spaced.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #31

challenges.content: It should be between 6 to 10 pages long.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #32

challenges.content: 6 to 10 pages? That's so much!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #33

challenges.content: Ah, it's gonna take forever.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #34

challenges.content: I know. The whole class groaned when he said that.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #35

challenges.content: Anyway, you also need to put the title in italics...
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #36

challenges.content: Wait, each section heading, or just the main heading?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #37

challenges.content: Only the main heading should be in italics.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #38

challenges.content: I think section titles are supposed to be in the same format, but maybe in bold.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #39

challenges.content: You'll have to check that in class next time.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #40

challenges.content: Oh okay.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #41

challenges.content: So I take it that the report has to be typed since there are so many requirements.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #42

challenges.content: What are the other formatting requirements?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #43

challenges.content: Yep, it's got to be typed.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #44

challenges.content: Aside from that, there are still a few more specifications.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #45

challenges.content: You should number each page.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #46

challenges.content: Make sure it goes up in the top right corner.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #47

challenges.content: Okay, I'll make sure to write that down.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #48

challenges.content: I always forget to number the pages.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #49

challenges.content: Do we need to title and date each page, too?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #50

challenges.content: You need the shortened title on every page, but no need to include the date.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #51

challenges.content: That should just be on the cover page.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #52

challenges.content: Okay, thanks.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #53

challenges.content: No problem.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #54

challenges.content: Also, make sure the margins are 3.25 pixels wide.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #55

challenges.content: What?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #56

challenges.content: I'm not even sure how to do that.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #57

challenges.content: Oh, it's okay, I can show you. It's really easy.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #58

challenges.content: I think that's all the directions he gave us.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #59

challenges.content: A lot of formatting requirements,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #60

challenges.content: but we have the freedom to research many things that we like, so that's good.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #61

challenges.content: Oh, I almost forgot,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #62

challenges.content: remember to put down your ID number on your report.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #63

challenges.content: Thanks so much for your help.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #64

challenges.content: I'll see you in class Monday!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #65

challenges.content: No problem, glad I could help. See you later.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 3 - challenge #66

challenges.content: Hi folks, my name is Loretta Johnston,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #1

challenges.content: and I'm here from the Baltimore Department of Public Waste.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #2

challenges.content: Thank you for coming out to our community meeting tonight.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #3

challenges.content: I've got a few words to say about the waste collection here in Baltimore.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #4

challenges.content: First, there's the sorted collection bins themselves.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #5

challenges.content: They're made of sturdy, solid material,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #6

challenges.content: so none of your trash can seep out or puncture the bin.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #7

challenges.content: Also, since these things sit out on the curb overnight rain or shine,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #8

challenges.content: they have to be waterproof.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #9

challenges.content: We can't have water getting up in it and filling up the bin.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #10

challenges.content: Remember to pay attention to which bin is which,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #11

challenges.content: and sort your waste accordingly.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #12

challenges.content: You should have a blue or green bin for recyclable garbage,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #13

challenges.content: a yellow bin for unrecyclable garbage,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #14

challenges.content: and a red bin for toxic waste.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #15

challenges.content: Our citywide waste management is divided into 2 services.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #16

challenges.content: The first is commercial waste collection, or trash collection from buildings.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #17

challenges.content: The majority of building waste is paper, which goes in the blue or green bins.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #18

challenges.content: You'll notice in your office buildings there are signs that warn you not to overfill these bins.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #19

challenges.content: All that paper adds up,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #20

challenges.content: and an overflowing bin is infinitely harder for collectors to carry to the truck and empty.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #21

challenges.content: Aside from paper, another large source of building waste is metals.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #22

challenges.content: Metals such as tin and aluminium can be put in the yellow recycle bins,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #23

challenges.content: but metals like lead and copper should be disposed of in the red bins.
challenges.explanation:
dispose of something

to get rid of something
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #24

challenges.content: These heavy metals are harmful to the environment
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #25

challenges.content: and exacerbate our city's existing pollution problem.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #26

challenges.content: That's about all the information you need for building waste.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #27

challenges.content: Moving on to the second service,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #28

challenges.content: household waste collection is probably what you primarily think of when you think of what we do here...
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #29

challenges.content: Many of the same guidelines apply - the sorting is the same, et cetera.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #30

challenges.content: Please remember to keep garbage like kitchen waste in a plastic bag.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #31

challenges.content: It makes collection easier and lessens the abominable rotten-trash smell.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #32

challenges.content: So after we take your trash away, what happens to it?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #33

challenges.content: We take all the garbage to one of a number of garbage disposal plants,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #34

challenges.content: each of which is located in the middle of an open space of some sort.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #35

challenges.content: No one wants to have their home or office right next door to a waste disposal plant, right?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #36

challenges.content: Waste is collected and then disposed of once every four weeks.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #37

challenges.content: A lot of trash can build up in that time,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #38

challenges.content: so we're in the process of developing a plan to fund collection more frequently.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #39

challenges.content: Ideally it would be collected weekly,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #40

challenges.content: but we will likely have to settle for biweekly.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #41

challenges.content: The garbage trucks make their rounds to clear the bins at night in order to avoid traffic.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #42

challenges.content: I'm sure you've seen how much waste your own household produces in a given week.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #43

challenges.content: Now imagine all the trash produced by all the households in Baltimore.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #44

challenges.content: It's a lot, right?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #45

challenges.content: It may surprise you that this amount is only marginal compared to commercial waste.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #46

challenges.content: Yep, the main waste producers are actually businesses, industrial facilities, retail, and offices.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #47

challenges.content: Hard to believe humans produce that much waste, right?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #48

challenges.content: No wonder we have pollution problems!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #49

challenges.content: Anyway, after all incoming waste is sorted,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #50

challenges.content: recyclables are sent to a recycling plant,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #51

challenges.content: while garbage and toxic waste are transported to their respective areas of the plant for treatment.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #52

challenges.content: Items such as stones, which should not be disposed of in our bins,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #53

challenges.content: are separated out and discarded.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #54

challenges.content: Once the trash has undergone the treatment process,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #55

challenges.content: it is compacted and disposed of with all the other trash
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #56

challenges.content: and finally, when the landfill space is full,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #57

challenges.content: it is buried deep underground and in time something new is built on the land.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #58

challenges.content: That's everything about waste collection.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #59

challenges.content: Thank you for listening.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #60

challenges.content: Are there any questions?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 2 - challenge #61

challenges.content: Good afternoon and welcome to Habitat Hunters.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #1

challenges.content: You must be Joseph?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #2

challenges.content: Yes, that's right. You said on the phone that I could come by at 2 o'clock.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #3

challenges.content: Sorry, I'm a little early.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #4

challenges.content: No, no problem at all.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #5

challenges.content: In Calgary's market, you have to move fast if you want a good apartment!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #6

challenges.content: Actually, I'd settle for almost anything.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #7

challenges.content: I've been here ten days and the hotel is ruining me.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #8

challenges.content: My father has me on a strict budget.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #9

challenges.content: Sit right down here now, sir.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #10

challenges.content: Let's talk a little about the places before we go have a look.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #11

challenges.content: Now, we have 4 apartments available.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #12

challenges.content: OK, could you tell me more about those 4 apartments?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #13

challenges.content: Sure. The first one is on Beatle Road, just a block off campus.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #14

challenges.content: It's a 3-bedroom with a bathroom and a living room and a great Italian restaurant right next to it.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #15

challenges.content: How much?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #16

challenges.content: Well, it's $435 a month, including Internet and utilities.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #17

challenges.content: Okay, that sounds reasonable.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #18

challenges.content: Any drawbacks to the house?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #19

challenges.content: There's a really big garden, but it hasn't been taken care of over the years and
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #20

challenges.content: is just too big to clean up nicely.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #21

challenges.content: Hmm. That sounds okay.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #22

challenges.content: Tell me about the next option.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #23

challenges.content: The other 3-bedroom apartment is on Oakington Avenue on campus.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #24

challenges.content: It is right near the building where you have classes,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #25

challenges.content: and the kitchen and living room are newly furnished.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #26

challenges.content: Wow, that sounds like a pretty good option.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #27

challenges.content: Well, it is a cool apartment,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #28

challenges.content: but since it's a dormitory, the living room, bathroom, kitchen, and washing machine are all shared.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #29

challenges.content: It would be nice not to have to buy living room furniture, though.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #30

challenges.content: And how much is this one?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #31

challenges.content: $400 per month for a bedroom with an air conditioner.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #32

challenges.content: For a bedroom without an air conditioner, you would pay less,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #33

challenges.content: $340 for it.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #34

challenges.content: Yikes, even with the air conditioner, it sounds really inconvenient to have to share facilities.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #35

challenges.content: I'll never cook if I have to walk down the hall to use the kitchen.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #36

challenges.content: Yeah, that's true.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #37

challenges.content: Anyway, the next place is a 2-bedroom on Mead Street.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #38

challenges.content: Oh, I like Mead Street - that's off campus, right?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #39

challenges.content: Yep. It's pretty cool, but it only has 2 bedrooms, plus a living room and a study.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #40

challenges.content: But I want to live together with my 2 friends.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #41

challenges.content: So you could make the study into a small bedroom if you end up living with them.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #42

challenges.content: Also, we guys want a TV and DVD player since we're all so much into movies.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #43

challenges.content: Well, this place has a great TV and VCR, but no DVD player.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #44

challenges.content: No DVD? That's so weird.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #45

challenges.content: Are any other facilities provided?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #46

challenges.content: As you said, weird enough, it also comes with a washbasin.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #47

challenges.content: Is there a washing machine?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #48

challenges.content: I think we need that more than just a washbasin.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #49

challenges.content: I'm afraid there's no washing machine in the apartment.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #50

challenges.content: Wow, that's so old-fashioned!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #51

challenges.content: Maybe it's not the best choice for 3 college guys.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #52

challenges.content: How much is it?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #53

challenges.content: Well, it's $600 per month,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #54

challenges.content: but of course it would be cheaper if you made it into 3 bedrooms instead of 2.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #55

challenges.content: Where is the apartment located?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #56

challenges.content: It's 2500 Mead Street, where there are a lot of bars.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #57

challenges.content: It would be affordable, but it would get pretty noisy.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #58

challenges.content: And that sounds really expensive for an old place in a noisy area.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #59

challenges.content: How about the last place?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #60

challenges.content: This one's on-campus in the Devon Close complex.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #61

challenges.content: It's a one-bedroom so it will be a little quieter than the Mead Street place.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #62

challenges.content: One bedroom huh? That could be good for focusing on my studies.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #63

challenges.content: What else does it have?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #64

challenges.content: It comes with a living room and a study,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #65

challenges.content: and includes a really nice lamp in the study that has a bunch of different settings.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #66

challenges.content: You know what else is cool?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #67

challenges.content: There's a dining hall downstairs so all evening meals are free.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #68

challenges.content: You can purchase breakfast and lunch, but meals after 6 p.m. are free.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #69

challenges.content: Wow, this place sounds too good to be true.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #70

challenges.content: Is it really expensive?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #71

challenges.content: It's alright - $500 per month, but there's no bathroom.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #72

challenges.content: What? No bathroom?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #73

challenges.content: Well, there's no bathroom in the apartment, but there's one at the end of the hall.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #74

challenges.content: Hmm. Thanks, I think now I just have to decide whether I want to live alone or not.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #75

challenges.content: Yeah, which one do you prefer?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #76

challenges.content: I think I'd choose either this apartment or the one on Beatle Road.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #77

challenges.content: OK. You'd better think about it, and then you can contact me ASAP
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #78

challenges.content: Fine, thanks for your help!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 33 - Part 1 - challenge #79

challenges.content: OK and welcome back.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #1

challenges.content: During the short break we just took,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #2

challenges.content: several of you approached me with questions.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #3

challenges.content: So, before going on with the orientation talk,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #4

challenges.content: I'd like to address those queries.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #5

challenges.content: As I've found, if one person asks a question,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #6

challenges.content: probably a dozen others are wondering about the same thing!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #7

challenges.content: The first question is whether Wassamatta University employs modules technology as an instruction method.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #8

challenges.content: The answer is yes, we do.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #9

challenges.content: At least that's what the university catalogue says.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #10

challenges.content: If some of you don't understand what "modules technology" is, don't worry.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #11

challenges.content: I googled the word but couldn't find it.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #12

challenges.content: Apparently, though, it's a method of broadband, wireless access.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #13

challenges.content: At least that's what an American company's website told me.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #14

challenges.content: But again, don't worry.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #15

challenges.content: If you need to know something more, your professor can tell you.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #16

challenges.content: Another question someone asked me
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #17

challenges.content: was what tomorrow's workshop on "Research Methods and Skills" was about.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #18

challenges.content: Well, research skills include any method you can imagine
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #19

challenges.content: for finding and presenting any information you need.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #20

challenges.content: That's not just schoolwork, either.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #21

challenges.content: Writing English - the native language for most of you,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #22

challenges.content: and finding a job are also research skills.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #23

challenges.content: And, yes, those will be addressed in tomorrow's workshop.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #24

challenges.content: As you know, Wassamatta University
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #25

challenges.content: is one of this country's premier universities for the study of "the dismal science", economics.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #26

challenges.content: Some of you, it seems, want to get a jump on their classmates.
challenges.explanation:
get a jump on someone/something

to get an advantage over other people by doing something before they do
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #27

challenges.content: During the break, half a dozen of you came up and asked me where to find economics tomes.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #28

challenges.content: I know it's odd, but this school's library holdings are divided up between two libraries.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #29

challenges.content: Economics books are in the old library.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #30

challenges.content: If you look out of the window behind me, you can see it.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #31

challenges.content: It's the red brick building.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #32

challenges.content: Oh, before I forget, you economics types also need a lot of math, am I right?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #33

challenges.content: Well, those Math books are neither in the old library nor in the new one.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #34

challenges.content: They can be found in the Maths Department Building.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #35

challenges.content: Why am I telling you this?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #36

challenges.content: Doesn't "the Invisible Hand" guide economists?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #37

challenges.content: Maybe it's good you asked:
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #38

challenges.content: in 2008, that Hand shoved most of the world economy off a cliff, didn't it?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #39

challenges.content: Now I realise that most of you couldn't bring a computer printer or a photocopier from home.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #40

challenges.content: So I'm sure you're already wondering where you can copy things like term papers,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #41

challenges.content: Internet articles, and things like that.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #42

challenges.content: I have some good news and some bad news.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #43

challenges.content: The good news is that there are a number of places you can make copies.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #44

challenges.content: These include both libraries and Student Union Building.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #45

challenges.content: Now the bad news. I'm sorry to say,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #46

challenges.content: most classroom buildings and academic departments do not have copiers students can use.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #47

challenges.content: So most of the large buildings you see around campus do not have copiers for students.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #48

challenges.content: The copiers there are reserved for professors and office staff.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #49

challenges.content: Oh, yes! I nearly forgot to tell you.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #50

challenges.content: If you need to have printing done, all the copiers available to students are laser printers.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #51

challenges.content: Plus, for your convenience, you can pay using prepaid cards.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #52

challenges.content: You can get those in the Student Union Building.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #53

challenges.content: That just covers the questions put to me.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #54

challenges.content: If you have more, please see me during the next break at 2:15.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #55

challenges.content: Right now, though, I'd like to start to give you a rundown on the various facilities here on campus.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #56

challenges.content: That way, you won't get lost so easily in the weeks to come.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #57

challenges.content: I've been told that this year's incoming class features a large number of married students and parents.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #58

challenges.content: So, you must be wondering where to put the baby while you're in class.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #59

challenges.content: OK, right now, we're in the Student Union Building, right?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #60

challenges.content: Remember the big doors in front where you all came in?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #61

challenges.content: If you go out of the building, you can see the Nursery is just on the other side of this building.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #62

challenges.content: It's only about 20 metres away!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #63

challenges.content: Convenient, eh?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #64

challenges.content: Next, we're all from different places around the country.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #65

challenges.content: Some of you are from other countries.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #66

challenges.content: That means we're pretty likely to get sick during the first months of school as we expose each other to many new viruses.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #67

challenges.content: So, where's the doctor?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #68

challenges.content: Of course, you need to find the Medical Services Centre
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #69

challenges.content: which is on the right as you leave the building.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #70

challenges.content: Remember, that's the second building on the right.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #71

challenges.content: And if you look out of that window,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #72

challenges.content: you can see a lot of antennae and satellite dishes on the roof.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #73

challenges.content: So that's what we call the Media Centre.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #74

challenges.content: Yeah, I know, I think it's confusing, too.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #75

challenges.content: The Media Centre is next to the Medical Centre.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #76

challenges.content: The chairwoman of the Journalism School on the first floor
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #77

challenges.content: doesn't like it when people who wander in there mistake her for a nurse!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #78

challenges.content: Chances are you'll have at least one Math class while you're here.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #79

challenges.content: That red building there just outside to the left is the Math Department Building.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #80

challenges.content: I know, it looks about as old as the subject of Math,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #81

challenges.content: but I assure you that the inside is equipped with state-of-the-art classroom equipment
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #82

challenges.content: including interactive chalkboards and surround sound in every room.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #83

challenges.content: Oh, can you see the back building there?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #84

challenges.content: Yes, behind the Media Centre. Quite new, isn't it?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #85

challenges.content: That's the new library, just decorated.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #86

challenges.content: They're back-to-back, you might say.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #87

challenges.content: If you look just to the left of it at the lower, older-looking building, you'll find the old library.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #88

challenges.content: It's nice and quiet - perfect for those marathon study sessions during exam week.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #89

challenges.content: Since the weather is so nice,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #90

challenges.content: why don't we stop looking at our maps but go for a walk around the campus?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 4 - challenge #91

challenges.content: Hello, are you Dr Lindsey?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #1

challenges.content: The Returning Students Advisor?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #2

challenges.content: Yes, that's right. Are you Frank?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #3

challenges.content: Your appointment wasn't until 2:00, but that's OK.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #4

challenges.content: Please come in and have a seat.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #5

challenges.content: Thanks, I like to arrive early whenever I have anything to do.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #6

challenges.content: That's certainly a praiseworthy habit.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #7

challenges.content: Let me see, it looks like you've taken a long break from school,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #8

challenges.content: and I understand you wanted to have a chat about what you should study
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #9

challenges.content: if and when you return for further classes.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #10

challenges.content: It's such a big challenge.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #11

challenges.content: I don't know if I'm crazy for doing this or not!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #12

challenges.content: Believe it or not, I know exactly what you mean.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #13

challenges.content: Before I began working here at the university, I taught primary school for nearly 10 years.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #14

challenges.content: It takes a lot of courage to go back to school!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #15

challenges.content: I feel more shy and scared than the primary students I teach!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #16

challenges.content: In the schools I taught, I found today's youngsters are very sure of themselves.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #17

challenges.content: In terms of intelligence, I have a lot to teach them.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #18

challenges.content: And the maturity level of much of my class leaves something to be desired.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #19

challenges.content: But in terms of confidence, wow!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #20

challenges.content: A lot more confident than I am now, that's for sure!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #21

challenges.content: Stop fretting.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #22
