challenges.content: "A brave man is a coward who refuses to run".
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #23

challenges.content: Let's talk about your strong points.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #24

challenges.content: You seem an intelligent man.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #25

challenges.content: What is it you would like to study?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #26

challenges.content: You see, I've been teaching children for a few years,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #27

challenges.content: but I think I'm happier teaching adults.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #28

challenges.content: I think teaching students in middle school is much more satisfying
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #29

challenges.content: because they end up being much more grateful for your work.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #30

challenges.content: If I may ask, what got you interested in teaching adults?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #31

challenges.content: A lot of things, I guess.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #32

challenges.content: I met my future wife back in my first year of college.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #33

challenges.content: She always complains that I was more interesting then.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #34

challenges.content: She says that now I talk like I'm 7 years old!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #35

challenges.content: That's probably from being with children all day.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #36

challenges.content: Haha! Again I know just what you mean.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #37

challenges.content: My husband used to say the same thing about me when I taught kindergarten.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #38

challenges.content: Anything else?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #39

challenges.content: Well, yes.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #40

challenges.content: Fairly often now I run into former students and we talk.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #41

challenges.content: Some of them are getting close to being grown up.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #42

challenges.content: I guess I think more and more about how people develop over time.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #43

challenges.content: So, I'm interested in the results of education, you know, the final stages.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #44

challenges.content: I see.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #45

challenges.content: Well, coming back to the university can be both difficult and very rewarding.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #46

challenges.content: There are some problems unique to returning students, you know, older students like yourself.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #47

challenges.content: What do you think is your greatest weakness?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #48

challenges.content: Well, I actually think my confidence is getting better.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #49

challenges.content: I'm definitely overcoming my introversion
challenges.explanation:
introvert

An introvert person is someone who is shy and quiet and likes to be alone or doesn't like to be with other people.

introversion

The noun of the adjective "introvert".
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #50

challenges.content: and starting to be much more comfortable in front of a class.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #51

challenges.content: To tell the truth, I'm afraid I'm rather behind the times about many things.
challenges.explanation:
behind the times

Old-fashioned, not modern, not aware of or using the latest ideas or techniques.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #52

challenges.content: It's more difficult for me to chase after the popular things youngsters are fond of
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #53

challenges.content: such as Iphone, Twitter, if you name it!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #54

challenges.content: I think I understand.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #55

challenges.content: How old are you, 35?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #56

challenges.content: People at your age still go back to school for further education.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #57

challenges.content: I was a bit the same way.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #58

challenges.content: I mean I didn't study at university till after I had a family: a husband and one child.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #59

challenges.content: My point of view was a lot different from your average eighteen-year-old girl's, I can tell you!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #60

challenges.content: Gee, that sounds pretty rough.
challenges.explanation:
gee

Some other words for "gee" are "wow", "phew", "oh my god", "oh dear"...
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #61

challenges.content: A family and college?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #62

challenges.content: Clearly you weren't unsuccessful though!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #63

challenges.content: It was, Frank. It truly was.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #64

challenges.content: My first term at school was extremely stressful.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #65

challenges.content: But excuse me! You're not here to listen to my life story.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #66

challenges.content: We're talking about your plans.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #67

challenges.content: Is there anything unique I should know about you or your past experience or plans?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #68

challenges.content: I'm afraid not. There is nothing interesting about my career or plans.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #69

challenges.content: It's really not too impressive.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #70

challenges.content: Now, I forbid you to talk like that.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #71

challenges.content: This is your one life, and if you're not interested, why bother living it?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #72

challenges.content: Don't be so humble, Frank.
challenges.explanation:
humble

not proud or not believing that you are important
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #73

challenges.content: OK, OK. My wife says I'm a wimp.
challenges.explanation:
wimp

A wimp is a person who is weak or not confident.

Coward.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #74

challenges.content: Let's talk about your dreams a bit.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #75

challenges.content: You want to teach adults, you said.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #76

challenges.content: What would you like to teach them?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #77

challenges.content: Well, when I first came to college, I really liked Languages and Literature.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #78

challenges.content: A lot of people have told me that for practical reasons,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #79

challenges.content: it'd be more rewarding to choose Business Management as my major,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #80

challenges.content: but I made up my mind to study Liberal Arts once I got the idea of going back to school.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #81

challenges.content: I must say it's refreshing to meet someone who knows there's more to an education than computers and finance.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #82

challenges.content: Let's have a look at the university course catalogue...
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #83

challenges.content: Excuse me, Dr Lindsey. Before we do that,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #84

challenges.content: could I maybe ask you some questions about changes in university life?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #85

challenges.content: I think I need to discuss that so I know what to expect.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #86

challenges.content: Of course. I'm here to help you.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #87

challenges.content: The biggest thing to get used to is the change in technology.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #88

challenges.content: Professors present things on huge screens,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #89

challenges.content: many of which are interactive computerised whiteboards.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #90

challenges.content: You can write on them still and use them like a touch screen.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #91

challenges.content: They're really handy!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #92

challenges.content: No more sloppy scribbled notes on the projector.
challenges.explanation:
sloppy, scribbled

careless, hard to read and understand
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #93

challenges.content: Let's see, I doubt you'll be living in student housing,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #94

challenges.content: so I won't go into all the improvements there.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #95

challenges.content: Another major change that you'll enjoy is the plethora of resources available for students.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #96

challenges.content: As a student, you have 24-hour access to the gym,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #97

challenges.content: and library privileges that include the use of school computers to scan, copy, and print,
challenges.explanation:
privilege

A right or permission or advantage that only some people have.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #98

challenges.content: and of course the Media Library, which contains movies from all genres
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #99

challenges.content: and most of the movies listed on AFI's Top 100 Movies of All Time.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #100

challenges.content: The dining facilities are also not what they used to be.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #101

challenges.content: They offer choices for all diets, and you can expect a hot meal any time of day.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #102

challenges.content: Wow, things really have changed!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #103

challenges.content: I'll be sure to utilise all those great facilities in my time here.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #104

challenges.content: Thanks for all your help, Dr Lindsey.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #105

challenges.content: I think that's all the questions I have for now.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 3 - challenge #106

challenges.content: Welcome everyone to today's seminar on "CV and Interview Skills".
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #1

challenges.content: Remember, your CV is probably the most important document you will ever write.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #2

challenges.content: It opens the door to your career!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #3

challenges.content: And that job interview is probably the most important meeting you will ever attend.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #4

challenges.content: It's like stepping through that open door.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #5

challenges.content: So let's roll up our sleeves and get down to work, shall we?
challenges.explanation:
let's roll up our sleeves

let's prepare for the hard work

sleeve

a piece of clothing that covers the arm
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #6

challenges.content: First of all, I cannot possibly tell you everything you need to know about writing a résumé in the time we have.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #7

challenges.content: But let me tell you that there are dozens of great websites on the Internet.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #8

challenges.content: These will give you all the suggestions you need.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #9

challenges.content: If you look at the paper I gave you,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #10

challenges.content: you will see a list of the dozen most popular sites.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #11

challenges.content: I can mention a couple of important points, however.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #12

challenges.content: One is that your CV or résumé should not be too long.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #13

challenges.content: A page is about right. Why?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #14

challenges.content: HR departments do not have the time to read long documents.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #15

challenges.content: Too many people are sending too many CVs!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #16

challenges.content: After all, the economic crisis of 2008 is still very much alive.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #17

challenges.content: Everyone needs a job now.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #18

challenges.content: No matter how short you make that résumé, though,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #19

challenges.content: you do not want to forget to tell HR how to contact your references.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #20

challenges.content: References are people who will give you a recommendation for a job.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #21

challenges.content: That's usually an ex-boss or a professor who knows you well.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #22

challenges.content: Do not use relatives!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #23

challenges.content: I don't care how much your mum loves you.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #24

challenges.content: Also, when you send that CV, be sure to include a typed cover letter.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #25

challenges.content: A cover letter is a letter where you, basically, are asking for a job.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #26

challenges.content: It's like introducing yourself.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #27

challenges.content: Make it brief.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #28

challenges.content: The real information about you is on that CV of yours.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #29

challenges.content: And, please make sure the letter is typed!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #30

challenges.content: It doesn't matter if your handwriting is beautiful or not.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #31

challenges.content: Companies only read typed letters.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #32

challenges.content: Another point about CVs is you should try to have an attractive layout.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #33

challenges.content: Maybe use different typefonts or colours to highlight information.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #34

challenges.content: Some people include a photo.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #35

challenges.content: You can find dozens of examples on the Internet.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #36

challenges.content: Whatever layout you decide to use, however, avoid all spelling and grammar errors.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #37

challenges.content: I used to be an HR manager.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #38

challenges.content: If I saw a mistake, that CV went into the garbage.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #39

challenges.content: Something you write in a CV is a description of your skills and experiences in an interesting way.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #40

challenges.content: Mention training, too.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #41

challenges.content: I mean these are what get you hired!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #42

challenges.content: Do not just say, "I have lots of experience." or "I have many skills".
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #43

challenges.content: Tell that boss what you did, for what company, and when.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #44

challenges.content: Better, tell him how well you did it!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #45

challenges.content: Don't just say, "I sold houses".
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #46

challenges.content: Say, "I sold two million pounds worth of houses in my first year".
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #47

challenges.content: That is, say something to make the person reading excited and curious.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #48

challenges.content: Finally, speaking of CVs, it's sad.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #49

challenges.content: But some people actually forget to provide a contact number.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #50

challenges.content: That's pretty silly.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #51

challenges.content: You wrote a great CV, you have HR dying to meet you...
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #52

challenges.content: and they don't know how.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #53

challenges.content: You forgot your phone number!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #54

challenges.content: Oh sure, if you apply online, they have your e-mail address.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #55

challenges.content: But you just showed them you're forgetful.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #56

challenges.content: Why are they going to want to talk to you after that?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #57

challenges.content: Alright, moving on to the actual interview,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #58

challenges.content: I'll go over what you need to know by the end of it,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #59

challenges.content: and what you can discuss and negotiate on later once it looks like you'll be offered the job.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #60

challenges.content: First, there's working hours.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #61

challenges.content: It's not that necessary to hammer out the hours off the bat,
challenges.explanation:
hammer out

to agree (usually after a lot of discussion or argument)

off the bat

immediately
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #62

challenges.content: especially since it's easy to come off as lazy when the first thing you bring up is how much you're going to have to work.
challenges.explanation:
come off as

to seem to be

bring up

to mention or to talk about something
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #63

challenges.content: You can also find out more about possible promotions later on.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #64

challenges.content: It is important, however, to get a feel for how much you'll be paid.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #65

challenges.content: You should make sure the salary range is commensurate with what you're worth,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #66

challenges.content: and if you're not, you can move on to better opportunities.
challenges.explanation:
move on to better opportunities

go and find better opportunities
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #67

challenges.content: Being sure you're going to make what you want to live on
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #68

challenges.content: is much more important than issues like your pension,
challenges.explanation:
pension

A regular payment made by the state to people of or above the official retirement age and to some widows and disabled people.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #69

challenges.content: you're all so young that your pension is not going to matter for quite a long time.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #70

challenges.content: You should find out about what skills you must know for the job and what they'll teach you.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #71

challenges.content: In addition, if the company will provide training,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #72

challenges.content: you should find out how long the training period is and whether it is paid.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #73

challenges.content: Beware of any jobs that want you to train for a long time without appropriate compensation.
challenges.explanation:
appropriate

Suitable or proper in the circumstances.

compensation

Benefits (money, awards...) that an employee gets after doing something.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #74

challenges.content: Speaking of compensation, find out about holidays as well.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #75

challenges.content: Do you get paid vacation time?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #76

challenges.content: Are you allowed to take personal days?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #77

challenges.content: Do you have to work on national holidays?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #78

challenges.content: Once you work out these main issues,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #79

challenges.content: you can move on later to details like the location and expected attire and whatnot.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #80

challenges.content: Wow, that's a lot of information!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #81

challenges.content: Let's take a break so you can think everything over and ask any questions you may have.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #82

challenges.content: Don't hesitate to come and see me if you need any clarification on all this stuff!
challenges.explanation:
clarification

an action to make things clear or less confused
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 2 - challenge #83

challenges.content: Hello, how may I help you?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #1

challenges.content: Well, I've been seeing these yellow boxes in front of a lot of houses in my neighbourhood.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #2

challenges.content: just wondered what they were for.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #3

challenges.content: I noticed your phone number on all of them, so I called.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #4

challenges.content: Could you tell me about your business?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #5

challenges.content: We do do recycling, but we're not a business.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #6

challenges.content: Gaea's Guardians is a non-profit group.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #7

challenges.content: We encourage recycling as a way of protecting the environment.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #8

challenges.content: I don't know.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #9

challenges.content: I mean it is a good idea.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #10

challenges.content: But I really don't read the newspaper every day or anything.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #11

challenges.content: And we don't come collect newspapers every day!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #12

challenges.content: In fact, we only do pickups every other week.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #13

challenges.content: Oh, well then maybe I could help.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #14

challenges.content: I mean in my neighbourhood, there's too much rubbish lying around everywhere.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #15

challenges.content: I'd like to help out, I guess.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #16

challenges.content: That's great, sir.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #17

challenges.content: You're doing the right thing.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #18

challenges.content: OK, I need to get your contact information.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #19

challenges.content: What's your name, please?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #20

challenges.content: Peter Wisrough.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #21

challenges.content: Peter... how do you spell your last name?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #22

challenges.content: Wisrow?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #23

challenges.content: No, actually it's Wisrough.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #24

challenges.content: Oh, I'm sorry. I'm a terrible speller.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #25

challenges.content: You're a good speller.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #26

challenges.content: It's just that my family are terrible pronouncers!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #27

challenges.content: You're quite a card, Peter!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #28

challenges.content: OK, now what's your address?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #29

challenges.content: No. 168 Bridge Road.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #30

challenges.content: That's here in London.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #31

challenges.content: How about if I have any questions?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #32

challenges.content: I'm sending you a copy of our booklet, too.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #33

challenges.content: The booklet has our phone number and our e-mail address,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #34

challenges.content: helpline@blackcat.com,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #35

challenges.content: that's helpline@blackcat.com
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #36

challenges.content: But I nearly forgot to ask, what's your postcode?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #37

challenges.content: BS97PU.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #38

challenges.content: PS97BU?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #39

challenges.content: No. That's B as in "boy" S-9-7-P as in "Peter" U.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #40

challenges.content: So, I'm guessing those yellow boxes I saw are for recycled newspapers?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #41

challenges.content: Yes, that is correct, and it's free of charge.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #42

challenges.content: Wow, that's good news!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #43

challenges.content: Do you recycle anything besides newspaper?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #44

challenges.content: Oh yes, we recycle most everything.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #45

challenges.content: Glass, plastic, paper...
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #46

challenges.content: Oh, so I can put like glass and plastic bottles in the box?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #47

challenges.content: Sorry again. Things like that you have to bring to our collection centre
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #48

challenges.content: And where is that?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #49

challenges.content: Our main centre isn't that far from you.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #50

challenges.content: It's actually right on the East Side of Central Park.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #51

challenges.content: That new blue building?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #52

challenges.content: That's the one!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #53

challenges.content: Cool. Hey, what's with all those different coloured boxes outside that place?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #54

challenges.content: Oh, that's for the different materials we recycle.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #55

challenges.content: The blue is for metal, the green is for glass and plastics,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #56

challenges.content: and the yellow of course is for paper.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #57

challenges.content: Hmm, okay. I'll try and manage to keep all that straight.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #58

challenges.content: Oh, no need, they're each labelled.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #59

challenges.content: Great. So which one would I put magazines in?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #60

challenges.content: Actually, they don't go in any of the bins.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #61

challenges.content: Unfortunately, magazines can't be recycled because of the material they're made of.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #62

challenges.content: It's such a waste.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #63

challenges.content: So would you be interested in volunteering?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #64

challenges.content: Um, I'll think about it.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #65

challenges.content: Could you send me some more info?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #66

challenges.content: Absolutely.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #67

challenges.content: Along with the newspaper box, I'll be sending you our booklet,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #68

challenges.content: "Savvy", that is S-A-V-V-Y.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #69

challenges.content: It tells you about what you can do to protect the environment in your daily life.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #70

challenges.content: Plus it lists things you can do as a volunteer with our group.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #71

challenges.content: Hey, that's cool, thanks!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #72

challenges.content: My pleasure.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #73

challenges.content: Do you have any other questions or concerns?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #74

challenges.content: Nope, that's it!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 32 - Part 1 - challenge #75

challenges.content: Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen, I'd like to take this opportunity to welcome you to our exhibition,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #1

challenges.content: "Two Centuries of the Bike".
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #2

challenges.content: Let's stroll around the exhibition, shall we?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #3

challenges.content: Although there were a few early efforts back in the 1700s,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #4

challenges.content: you didn't really see many bikes till, say, the 1830s in England.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #5

challenges.content: Bikes were a response to the rapid growth of cities early in the 19th century.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #6

challenges.content: Cities like London were getting too big to walk across!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #7

challenges.content: The early bike let people travel with less effort than walking.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #8

challenges.content: Plus a bike was a lot cheaper than a horse!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #9

challenges.content: Think of it. No one invented a bike for, what, 5000 years of human history?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #10

challenges.content: Why did people do it then?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #11

challenges.content: Probably because this was the start of the Machine Age:
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #12

challenges.content: people wanted machines to do all the work.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #13

challenges.content: There were some drawbacks, however.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #14

challenges.content: For one thing, there were no pedals.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #15

challenges.content: You simply pushed yourself along using your feet.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #16

challenges.content: Kind of like today's skateboard.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #17

challenges.content: That meant you went fairly slow.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #18

challenges.content: And uphill, you actually worked harder, pushing that two-wheeler.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #19

challenges.content: Plus, the wheels were made of wood covered with metal, as you can see from this model.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #20

challenges.content: So the downside was that the ride was quite uncomfortable on most roads.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #21

challenges.content: Only a few gadget lovers had or used them.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #22

challenges.content: By the 1860s, though, improvements were being made.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #23

challenges.content: As you can see from this specimen, metal frames had become the rule.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #24

challenges.content: They're more durable than wood, and they don't warp in the rain.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #25

challenges.content: The biggest improvement however was the development of the chain and sprocket system.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #26

challenges.content: They're connected.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #27

challenges.content: This meant you did not push the bike.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #28

challenges.content: You used pedals just like today.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #29

challenges.content: You had to try harder to balance, so it took some practice to figure out how to use the pedals.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #30

challenges.content: But it made the ride so much easier.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #31

challenges.content: As a result, the good thing was that you could ride a lot more smoothly and with very little effort.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #32

challenges.content: By the 1880s, another big change was the use of rubber wheels.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #33

challenges.content: These became pretty common at that time.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #34

challenges.content: Though the first ones were solid rubber,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #35

challenges.content: the ride was a good deal more comfortable than the old iron and wood system.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #36

challenges.content: This is a big consideration because the faster you go, the more you feel every bump.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #37

challenges.content: Air-filled tyres - "pneumatic tyres" - didn't really come into use till around the year 1900,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #38

challenges.content: as you can see from this exhibition over here.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #39

challenges.content: That made the ride even more comfortable.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #40

challenges.content: So, by 1890 or so, people were going a lot faster and a lot more smoothly.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #41

challenges.content: There was one problem when you were going quickly and comfortably:
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #42

challenges.content: "OH NO! HOW DO I STOP?"
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #43

challenges.content: Yes, we all laugh now.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #44

challenges.content: But for a long time, the only way to stop was drag your feet.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #45

challenges.content: That didn't work very well and it would be dangerous if you were going fast.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #46

challenges.content: In the crowded cities of those years - New York, Chicago, and so on,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #47

challenges.content: you'd get killed if you couldn't stop for, say, a streetcar.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #48

challenges.content: Plus look at this bike.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #49

challenges.content: The front wheel is nearly a metre and 2/3 tall!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #50

challenges.content: They made them that way so you could see over people and wagons.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #51

challenges.content: But you couldn't drag your feet.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #52

challenges.content: This model is called a "velocipede" - a "speed pedal".
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #53

challenges.content: Another characteristic of the bike in this period is that it has 2 equal-sized wheels,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #54

challenges.content: which signalled a big change in bikes.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #55

challenges.content: For with the velocipede, brakes appeared.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #56

challenges.content: If you wanted to stop, you just pushed the pedal backwards.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #57

challenges.content: Doing that stopped the back wheel of the bike.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #58

challenges.content: This technique worked a lot better than dragging your feet or jumping off the high seat there!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #59

challenges.content: This meant that bikes became a great deal safer.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #60

challenges.content: It would've been safer if people wore helmets,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #61

challenges.content: but the first bicycle helmet wasn't invented until years later,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #62

challenges.content: and even then it was little more than a leather ballcap.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #63

challenges.content: It really wasn't until the 1970s that the bike helmet was modified to provide some real protection.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #64

challenges.content: Before continuing on to look at developments since the 1890s, let's say a word more about safety.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #65

challenges.content: Everyone knows if you're going downhill, you can get going dangerously fast.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #66

challenges.content: To go more than a hundred kilometres an hour isn't all that difficult!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #67

challenges.content: But even on level ground it's easy to go too quickly.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #68

challenges.content: On a city street, today's bicycles can be ridden at a speed of over 40 miles an hour, over a short distance.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #69

challenges.content: That's about 64 kilometres an hour.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #70

challenges.content: Remember you're on a bike, not in a car.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #71

challenges.content: There's nothing to protect you.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #72

challenges.content: People are killed in single-bicycle accidents every day, just from hitting the road.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #73

challenges.content: A good rule to remember is, if you're going faster than the cars, slow down.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #74

challenges.content: And please wear a helmet.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #75

challenges.content: Nearly one quarter of the epilepsy cases come from head injuries in accidents on bikes and motorcycles.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #76

challenges.content: I don't mean to scare you, but safety is everyone's business.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #77

challenges.content: What? Now that's a good question.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #78

challenges.content: Why are today's bikes so much faster?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #79

challenges.content: Well, it's not just that today's athletes are faster.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #80

challenges.content: The answer is partly mechanical.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #81

challenges.content: If you look closely here, at the back wheel you'll see a number of gears.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #82

challenges.content: Changing gears is what makes those fast speeds possible.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #83

challenges.content: You can shift gears depending on the terrain and how hard you wish to pedal.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #84

challenges.content: So you can put it on a higher gear for downhill,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #85

challenges.content: and a lower gear for uphill travel to make it easier to climb that slope.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #86

challenges.content: You'll notice this gear-shifting mechanism is attached to the back wheel,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #87

challenges.content: and when the rider shifts on the handlebar gear shifter,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #88

challenges.content: the chain moves to the appropriate sprocket.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #89

challenges.content: And, speaking of changing gears,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #90

challenges.content: let's look over here at our "Tour de France" exhibit...
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 4 - challenge #91

challenges.content: Come in!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #1

challenges.content: Professor Dundee? We're ready to make our presentation.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #2

challenges.content: Oh, yes. I did say 1 o'clock, didn't I?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #3

challenges.content: Please, sit down.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #4

challenges.content: So, who goes first? Bruce? Or you, Betty?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #5

challenges.content: I guess I could. Bruce is always a little shy.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #6

challenges.content: Not after he's had a lager for lunch, eh Bruce?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #7

challenges.content: Heh, heh. No, Betty really should go first.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #8

challenges.content: OK. Well, I'm reporting on the effects of different marketing strategies on the cheese and oil markets.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #9

challenges.content: Different strategies obviously affect the sales volume differently.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #10

challenges.content: I looked at the sales in two countries, New Zealand and Colombia.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #11

challenges.content: And what did you find, pray tell?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #12

challenges.content: Well, in New Zealand, the sales of both oil and cheese have declined pretty steadily.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #13

challenges.content: And in fact, the sales have decreased more quickly than the population.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #14

challenges.content: On the other hand, in Colombia, the volume of sales for both products has remained the same.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #15

challenges.content: Wait, so you said sales in New Zealand have been going down?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #16

challenges.content: Correct.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #17

challenges.content: Suppliers have introduced two new upscale brands of each product,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #18

challenges.content: which are a bit expensive but very tasty.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #19

challenges.content: The big ad agencies are trying out a new series of ads that shift the focus from health to great taste.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #20

challenges.content: They think that will get sales moving up in New Zealand,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #21

challenges.content: where the population is less affluent and generally less health-conscious.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #22

challenges.content: Brilliant. Thank you. And Bruce?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #23

challenges.content: Uhhh... yeah. My report is about chocolate sales in Italy and Germany.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #24

challenges.content: The two countries' marketers have found out that you have to market chocolate differently in each country.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #25

challenges.content: For example?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #26

challenges.content: In Italy, "Kostig", the most expensive brand,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #27

challenges.content: pays shop owners to put the candy just about knee-high for an adult.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #28

challenges.content: I don't see...
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #29

challenges.content: For little kids, that's about eye level!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #30

challenges.content: That bright red candy is the first one they see, so they buy it!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #31

challenges.content: Even better, they start telling their moms to buy it, too!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #32

challenges.content: So, you mean...
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #33

challenges.content: Well, I mean, in Italy if you locate your product at the right location of shelves, sales do great.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #34

challenges.content: They say it doesn't matter much what brand of chocolate you're selling.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #35

challenges.content: As for Germany...
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #36

challenges.content: "Das Land der Schokolade".
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #37

challenges.content: Huh?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #38

challenges.content: That's German. It means "The Land of Chocolate".
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #39

challenges.content: Germans love the stuff, so people make a joke and call Germany that.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #40

challenges.content: Oh... uh, right...
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #41

challenges.content: So, you were saying?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #42

challenges.content: Well, like you pointed out, Germans love chocolate.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #43

challenges.content: But they're thrifty.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #44

challenges.content: For a long time, the biggest selling brand was "Schmutzig",
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #45

challenges.content: mostly because it was the second cheapest, but didn't taste too bad.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #46

challenges.content: Again brilliant!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #47

challenges.content: A pretty good job, both of you.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #48

challenges.content: Tell me, what do you plan to investigate next week?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #49

challenges.content: I'm especially interested in the effects of colour on sales of products,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #50

challenges.content: so I'll be looking at ads for cosmetics and cleaning products in the local market.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #51

challenges.content: You know, like the distinct orange colour of Mr. Muscle, lavatory cleaning products.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #52

challenges.content: And you, Bruce?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #53

challenges.content: I'm focusing on the effects of different containers on sales of cookies.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #54

challenges.content: So I'm going to look into packaging for cookies and how the materials they use will affect the image, and in turn sales.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #55

challenges.content: You know, most containers are paper,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #56

challenges.content: but some expensive cookies come in metal boxes.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #57

challenges.content: The shiny metal boxes catch people's attention
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #58

challenges.content: and the image remains in the memory longer.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #59

challenges.content: Well, it sounds like you two are all set.
challenges.explanation:
all set

ready, okay, no need for help
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #60

challenges.content: But as always in this course,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #61

challenges.content: I urge you both to pay much more attention to the advertisement extensions.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #62

challenges.content: That's often the key.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #63

challenges.content: Alright, any questions for me before you go?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #64

challenges.content: No, I think I'm all set. Thanks!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #65

challenges.content: Me too. Thanks, Professor Dundee. See ya later.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 3 - challenge #66

challenges.content: Hello everyone, and welcome to the University of New South Wales.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #1

challenges.content: The first thing I'd like to do at today's Orientation Session is get you all oriented!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #2

challenges.content: That means tell you the location of some useful facilities and services.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #3

challenges.content: So, first of all, take out the maps we gave you all as you came in the door.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #4

challenges.content: The map is the big yellow sheet of paper.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #5

challenges.content: As you can see on the map, North is at the top, South at the bottom, et cetera.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #6

challenges.content: Which way's North?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #7

challenges.content: Well, look through that window on my left, your right.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #8

challenges.content: See the rising sun?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #9

challenges.content: That would have to be East.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #10

challenges.content: So North must be directly behind me.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #11

challenges.content: Now, we are at the campus' Main Gate.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #12

challenges.content: The Recreational Facilities are on my right hand and its opposite is the Student Centre.
challenges.explanation:
Recreational Facilities

A place with equipment for outdoor activities such as sports...
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #13

challenges.content: No questions? Good. Pretty easy, right?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #14

challenges.content: OK, did everyone eat breakfast at the Student Food Service this morning?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #15

challenges.content: Was the food good?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #16

challenges.content: Yes, yes. I am joking. I've eaten there, too.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #17

challenges.content: So after a meal like that, you must be eager to go to a doctor. Right?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #18

challenges.content: Well, I have good news for you:
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #19

challenges.content: the Student Health Centre is located about half a kilometre straight north of here.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #20

challenges.content: Look on your maps.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #21

challenges.content: You see the street on the east side of this building?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #22

challenges.content: Ned Kelly Avenue?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #23

challenges.content: Just follow that about 500 metres,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #24

challenges.content: and the Health Centre will be on your left at the third cross street.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #25

challenges.content: Now, I know you all just got here.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #26

challenges.content: So you must be wondering how to tell your folks you've arrived safely,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #27

challenges.content: how much you miss the dog, and how you already need more money.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #28

challenges.content: If you don't have an Iphone, you probably are wondering where to find a computer.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #29

challenges.content: Well, I have good news.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #30

challenges.content: If you go straight out of this door and walk down the Garden Street,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #31

challenges.content: you'll see the Internet Unit on your left side, just next to the Gym.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #32

challenges.content: The hours are posted on the door, and the computers are free,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #33

challenges.content: but you must bring your student ID card with you.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #34

challenges.content: Like I tell everyone, if you need help with anything,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #35

challenges.content: you can probably find right here in the Student Centre.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #36

challenges.content: Do you see the 4 buildings there between the Student Centre and the library?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #37

challenges.content: Those are the dormitories.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #38

challenges.content: The men's dorms are the two on the south;
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #39

challenges.content: the women's the two on the north.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #40

challenges.content: OK, I'm sorry to have to tell you,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #41

challenges.content: but the university has been doing a lot of repairs and remodelling, and it's not all done yet.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #42

challenges.content: So there may be some small problems with your dorm rooms.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #43

challenges.content: Maybe the window doesn't open.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #44

challenges.content: Maybe an air conditioner is missing or does not work.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #45

challenges.content: If there are any problems, you can go to the Complaint Office,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #46

challenges.content: which is right beside the Teaching Building between the Parker Street and the Crammer Street.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #47

challenges.content: Just tell them your problem and they should have it fixed by the time you graduate in 4 years.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #48

challenges.content: I'm joking, but please be patient.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #49

challenges.content: There are a lot of little things they need to take care of.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #50

challenges.content: Tired of the school food?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #51

challenges.content: No? Give it a week.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #52

challenges.content: Or maybe you just need a place to get coffee in the wee hours of the night during one of those marathon study sessions.
challenges.explanation:
wee hours

the early hours of the morning, between twelve o'clock at night and the time when the sun rises
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #53

challenges.content: Either way, you definitely have to check out the little Cafe just past the women's dormitories.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #54

challenges.content: They've got free Wi-Fi, so a lot of students saddle up with coffee and a bagel for hours on end to get work done.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #55

challenges.content: As for the dorm rooms, I have some bad news and some good news.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #56

challenges.content: The bad news is the rooms are small and you'll probably be sharing space with at least three other students.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #57

challenges.content: The good news is that each room has its own bathroom.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #58

challenges.content: What's good about sharing a bathroom with three strangers?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #59

challenges.content: Hmmm... good question.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #60

challenges.content: OK, call it bad news and worse news.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #61

challenges.content: Hey, maybe try this for good news: each dorm has a kitchen.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #62

challenges.content: If you want to make snacks or meals, you can do it there.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #63

challenges.content: You can buy food containers at any campus convenience store, so you can store your food in the kitchen.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #64

challenges.content: But a word of warning: you should definitely write your name on your food containers.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #65

challenges.content: Sad to say, there are food thieves among your fellow students.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #66

challenges.content: Speaking of thieves, a word about security.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #67

challenges.content: I mean this is Australia and we do get drunken bushrangers wandering onto campus.
challenges.explanation:
bushrangers

criminals or thieves who live in bush
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #68

challenges.content: Each of you will be given a key for your dorm room.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #69

challenges.content: Don't lose it.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #70

challenges.content: You have to pay for any replacement and fill out a bunch of papers, too.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #71

challenges.content: Red tape, huh?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #72

challenges.content: Your key does not work for the front door of your dorm, however.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #73

challenges.content: To the right of each door, there's a keypad with numbers.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #74

challenges.content: When you move in, they will tell you the code you use to enter the door.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #75

challenges.content: Please do not tell the code to people who do not live in the dorm.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #76

challenges.content: Let's see. Have I forgotten anything?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #77

challenges.content: Oh, yes. Most of you are not rich, correct?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #78

challenges.content: So when your clothes get dirty, you can't just throw them away and buy new ones.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #79

challenges.content: That means you have to learn to do laundry.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #80

challenges.content: Or, men, that means you have to hurry up and get married.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #81

challenges.content: If you decide to wash those clothes and not get married, there are laundries in each dorm.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #82

challenges.content: Where? Oh, I almost forgot to tell you.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #83

challenges.content: The laundry for each dorm is in the basement.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #84

challenges.content: Some real good news this time: if you are a student, it is free.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #85

challenges.content: You do have to buy your own soap, however.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #86

challenges.content: The laundry closes, by the by, at 11:30
challenges.explanation:
by the by

Another way of saying "by the way".
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #87

challenges.content: And, now that I've mentioned 11:30,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #88

challenges.content: please remember the dorm doors are locked at 11:30 p.m.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #89

challenges.content: Your code will not work.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #90

challenges.content: If you want to get in, you'll have to call the night watchman.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #91

challenges.content: Don't worry, you can get that number at the Dorm Office.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #92

challenges.content: Yes, the Dorm Office and the Complaint Office are the same office.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #93

challenges.content: All right, then. Before we continue, are there any questions?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 2 - challenge #94

challenges.content: Hello, and welcome to "Under Pressure Enterprises", Customer Service Department.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #1

challenges.content: This is Kelly. How may I help you?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #2

challenges.content: Yes, I'm calling about one of your rice cookers I just purchased.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #3

challenges.content: What seems to be the problem, sir?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #4

challenges.content: Seems? There's no seeming about it!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #5

challenges.content: The blasted thing shoots hot steam all over the place, that's what!
challenges.explanation:
blasted

the word "blasted" is used to express an anger

the blasted thing = the damned thing
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #6

challenges.content: It nearly scalded my hand when I went to open it.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #7

challenges.content: While it could have killed the cat or something. It could have exploded and killed my wife and me!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #8

challenges.content: Sir, sir, please calm down.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #9

challenges.content: As long as the steam escapes the cooker, it won't explode.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #10

challenges.content: So you're telling me there's no problem!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #11

challenges.content: Are you calling me a liar?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #12

challenges.content: Sir, no one is calling you a liar.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #13
