challenges.content: Yes! So I demand a full refund!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #14

challenges.content: Under Pressure will be happy to refund your money, sir.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #15

challenges.content: Now I just need some basic information.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #16

challenges.content: OK, OK. Sorry. I do tend to get a little hot under the collar.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #17

challenges.content: My wife tells me to slow down...
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #18

challenges.content: So, what do you need to know?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #19

challenges.content: Sir, don't worry. I just need to ask you the model number of the cooker.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #20

challenges.content: Hmmm...
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #21

challenges.content: where are my glasses? Ah, here!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #22

challenges.content: Let's see...
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #23

challenges.content: It's R242.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #24
IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #25

challenges.content: And how much did you pay for the product?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #26

challenges.content: 89.99 pounds.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #27

challenges.content: It was on sale, I guess I should tell you.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #28

challenges.content: Thank you, that's honest of you.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #29

challenges.content: Now, where did you buy the cooker?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #30

challenges.content: Which store and which branch?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #31

challenges.content: At that big Electric Life appliance store downtown.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #32

challenges.content: The City Centre Branch?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #33

challenges.content: That's the one.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #34

challenges.content: And you say the problem is that the steam escapes?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #35

challenges.content: Yes, it does!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #36

challenges.content: No problem, sir.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #37

challenges.content: If there's steam escaping, clearly the cooker is broken or defective.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #38

challenges.content: So we have an R242 cooker with an escaping steam problem.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #39

challenges.content: It was bought from Electric Life's City Centre Branch for 89.99.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #40

challenges.content: Is that correct?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #41

challenges.content: Yes, that is correct.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #42

challenges.content: Oh, I nearly forgot. When did you buy the cooker?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #43

challenges.content: Just as soon as my wife got the crazy idea she'll live longer if she stops eating good English food: roast beef and mash.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #44

challenges.content: No, all she says she wants is rice and vegetables and sauces you'd not soak your feet in!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #45

challenges.content: Sir, sir! When did you buy it?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #46

challenges.content: Oh, there I go again. Let's see...
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #47

challenges.content: we bought it just 6 months ago!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #48

challenges.content: We hardly used it either.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #49

challenges.content: But 6 months? Is that too long?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #50

challenges.content: I mean for the warranty?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #51

challenges.content: Very well, that's well within the warranty period.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #52

challenges.content: Now, what's your name and address?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #53

challenges.content: Name and address! What for?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #54

challenges.content: Sir, it is company policy. If you want your money, you must inform me.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #55

challenges.content: Money you say?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #56

challenges.content: Oh, my name is Herbert Hewitt and my address is 84 Park Road.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #57

challenges.content: Is that here in Coventry?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #58

challenges.content: Yes.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #59

challenges.content: The postal code is B0241DJ.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #60

challenges.content: But I don't think sending things in the mail is very secure or very efficient.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #61

challenges.content: I mean...
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #62

challenges.content: Don't worry, Mr. Hewitt, don't worry.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #63

challenges.content: We can credit the money to your credit card.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #64

challenges.content: You do have one, don't you?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #65

challenges.content: Yes, that's how we paid for the cooker.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #66

challenges.content: Oh, yes. We still have the number on the computer.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #67

challenges.content: I only need to ask your card's expiry date.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #68

challenges.content: I'm afraid I never give that sort of information out.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #69

challenges.content: I mean, once you have that, anyone could go charging things and...
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #70

challenges.content: Sir! I said your expiry date, not your card's password.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #71

challenges.content: Oh, er, yes. Foolish me.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #72

challenges.content: Of course, you didn't say "password".
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #73

challenges.content: Let's see.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #74

challenges.content: That will be April 2008.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #75

challenges.content: April 2008.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #76

challenges.content: Very well, your card still has nearly 2 months left to go.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #77

challenges.content: We'll get that refund right to you, probably by 5 o'clock this evening.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #78

challenges.content: You had better!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #79

challenges.content: If I don't get my money...
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #80

challenges.content: wait, wait. Yes, I know I'm losing my temper again.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #81

challenges.content: I really am sorry.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #82

challenges.content: I haven't had my medicine today.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #83

challenges.content: And sir, just one more question for our record.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #84

challenges.content: How often do you go shopping at the City Centre Branch?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #85

challenges.content: Oh, well it's hard to say.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #86

challenges.content: I suppose maybe once a month.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #87

challenges.content: But I can tell you this, if I don't get my refund, I'll never shop there again!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #88

challenges.content: Oh.. I think it's time to start looking for another job!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 31 - Part 1 - challenge #89

challenges.content: Good afternoon, and welcome to Insect Biology 101.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #1

challenges.content: I'd like to begin this course with a few remarks about good insects and bad ones.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #2

challenges.content: Bugs are all around us and that's both a benefit and an annoyance,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #3

challenges.content: sometimes maybe even serious harm.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #4

challenges.content: First, let's talk about the good things that insects do for us.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #5

challenges.content: Probably the most important insect for humans, and maybe for all other life, is the bee.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #6

challenges.content: Bees help plants in the process of pollination,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #7

challenges.content: and thus are necessary to most flowers and fruit-producing trees.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #8

challenges.content: That is, they carry pollen from "male" flowers to "female".
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #9

challenges.content: If it weren't for bees, we'd have very few food plants and no fruit either.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #10

challenges.content: In fact, there would be no "we".
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #11

challenges.content: No less a thinker than Albert Einstein pointed out that,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #12

challenges.content: without bees, humanity would be dead within a year or less.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #13

challenges.content: We'd starve. It's that simple.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #14

challenges.content: That should maybe make us just a little humble.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #15

challenges.content: A little less dramatic is the fact that bees also make the honey we eat.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #16

challenges.content: Moreover, they produce beeswax, which is useful in candles
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #17

challenges.content: and it's also used as a first-rate furniture polish.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #18

challenges.content: Sure, these may not be vital to our lives,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #19

challenges.content: but they can serve as reminders of how important bees are.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #20

challenges.content: That's a point I keep coming back to in this course.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #21

challenges.content: Though, in all fairness, I should point out that butterflies aid in pollination as well as bees.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #22

challenges.content: Now, here in Michigan, what's the worst part of summer?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #23

challenges.content: Yep, that's right - mosquitoes.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #24

challenges.content: But I'm talking about helpful insects, right?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #25

challenges.content: So let's look at the dragonfly first.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #26

challenges.content: If there were no dragonflies, there would be even more mosquitoes!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #27

challenges.content: Dragonflies mainly eat mosquitoes and also a few other insects.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #28

challenges.content: Yes, that's right.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #29

challenges.content: They don't just fly around, and they also help to eliminate harmful insects.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #30

challenges.content: So, the next time you see a dragonfly, don't you dare kill it!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #31

challenges.content: Now let's talk a little about those harmful insects.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #32

challenges.content: Take the mosquitoes I just mentioned as an example.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #33

challenges.content: Not so many years ago, mosquitoes here in America weren't just annoying.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #34

challenges.content: Some were even deadly.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #35

challenges.content: They carried malaria and yellow fever.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #36

challenges.content: My own ancestor, the Confederate General John Bell Hood,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #37

challenges.content: lived through the worst battles of Civil War only to die at age 38 from yellow fever.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #38

challenges.content: A pest, not a bullet!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #39

challenges.content: Well, besides the mosquitoes, in summer there is also a kind of insect that never seems tired.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #40

challenges.content: Right, that is the fly.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #41

challenges.content: Before I go on talking, I must mention an African fly called the Tsetse fly,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #42

challenges.content: which feeds on blood and can cause serious diseases in the people and animals that it bites.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #43

challenges.content: Besides, it is still a bearer of sleeping sickness,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #44

challenges.content: which affects around 300,000 people every year in Africa
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #45

challenges.content: and can be treated only with toxic drugs that are hard to administer.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #46

challenges.content: Worse still, the drugs sometimes don't work.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #47

challenges.content: Other insects, of course, destroy food crops.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #48

challenges.content: In China, for instance, locusts continue to be a danger to the harvest in some areas.
challenges.explanation:
locust

a large insect, similar to grasshopper, found in hot areas that flies in large groups and destroys plants and crops
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #49

challenges.content: Less important, but still annoying, moths eat people's clothes and dust mites slowly destroy carpets.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #50

challenges.content: Worse, but still in the home, termites or "white ants" eat wood - the wood of your house.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #51

challenges.content: If they are not stopped, they can eventually destroy the whole building.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #52

challenges.content: Usually they seriously damage a building before anyone even notices them.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #53

challenges.content: So, as we all know, insects can be a real trouble.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #54

challenges.content: So, what to do?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #55

challenges.content: You can go ahead and start killing harmful insects.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #56

challenges.content: In the early decades after the communist revolution in China,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #57

challenges.content: Chairman Mao encouraged the people to swat every fly they could see.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #58

challenges.content: Slogans on the walls of buildings called them "Little Capitalists".
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #59

challenges.content: But flies reproduced too quickly for this to be a long-term solution.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #60

challenges.content: For some decades in the West, to kill insects with chemicals seemed a good remedy.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #61

challenges.content: Unfortunately, chemicals can only be used in a limited area for a limited time.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #62

challenges.content: It's a small-scale solution.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #63

challenges.content: The insects come back.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #64

challenges.content: Worse still, some of the poisons used like DDT were found harmful to the environment.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #65

challenges.content: Many kinds of wildlife, like hawks, were harmed.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #66

challenges.content: And people in chemical-using rural areas have one of the highest rates of liver cancer in the world.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #67

challenges.content: It's no secret that chemicals remain harmful to humans.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #68

challenges.content: Like all species, insects adapt to their changing environments at an amazing rate.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #69

challenges.content: When a new chemical is introduced to their habitat,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #70

challenges.content: the insects that survive are generally the ones with some way of resisting the harmful effects.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #71

challenges.content: They then breed with the other survivors,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #72

challenges.content: and just like that insects become resistant to most poison in a few generations.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #73

challenges.content: An insect generation, remember, is a couple of months at most!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #74

challenges.content: So, again we have to ask: what to do?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #75

challenges.content: Well, there are biological solutions.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #76

challenges.content: Some of these are pretty simple.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #77

challenges.content: One is destroying the insects' habitat.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #78

challenges.content: You take away their home or food.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #79

challenges.content: Cleaning your kitchen is the best way to prevent roaches.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #80

challenges.content: No garbage: no food.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #81

challenges.content: Getting rid of marshes and swamps eliminates mosquitoes.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #82

challenges.content: Other solutions might include bringing in dragonflies or bats in areas where mosquitoes are many.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #83

challenges.content: This is a cheaper alternative to chemicals.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #84

challenges.content: Biological methods like this also bring no extra pollution to the environment.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #85

challenges.content: But you have to be careful.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #86

challenges.content: If you change the environment too much, you might be hurting other forms of life accidentally.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #87

challenges.content: One recent method of controlling insect populations involves interrupting their breeding cycle.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #88

challenges.content: What does that mean?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #89

challenges.content: It means "birth control for bugs".
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #90

challenges.content: Insects are provided with food that makes them unable to reproduce.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #91

challenges.content: Since they can't have babies, the population disappears, or nearly so.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #92

challenges.content: And since no young are born,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #93

challenges.content: resistance is not a problem with no young insects developing increased resistance.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #94

challenges.content: Interrupt the life cycle, eliminate the bug!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #95

challenges.content: It's clear that we must have an understanding of the life cycle of the insect.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #96

challenges.content: At least, that's the plan.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #97

challenges.content: We'll go into more detail as the course goes along.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #98

challenges.content: Now I will stop here to see whether you have any questions or not.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 4 - challenge #99

challenges.content: Are you just leaving the library now?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #1

challenges.content: I saw you get there at 8 am!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #2

challenges.content: Yeah, I've been there all day.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #3

challenges.content: What for?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #4

challenges.content: They hired a cute new librarian or something?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #5

challenges.content: I wish.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #6

challenges.content: No, it's the presentation that I will give in Environmental Science the day after tomorrow.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #7

challenges.content: What's it about?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #8

challenges.content: I heard you were really excited about the class.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #9

challenges.content: And Dr Schnee also calls you for the "arcane" questions, as he calls them.
challenges.explanation:
arcane

understood on by a few people, mysterious or secret
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #10

challenges.content: It's about environmental damage in the Yucatan.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #11

challenges.content: Excuse me, what?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #12

challenges.content: Or is that where?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #13

challenges.content: Yucatan.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #14

challenges.content: It's a state in Southeast Mexico.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #15

challenges.content: So what's happening there?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #16

challenges.content: Agriculture is having a really adverse impact on the environment.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #17

challenges.content: There are too many farmers doing too much farming.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #18

challenges.content: It's really destroying the forests and ruining the soil.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #19

challenges.content: Deforestation is a major problem there now.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #20

challenges.content: How did you learn about this?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #21

challenges.content: I don't recall Dr Schnee saying anything about it in lecture.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #22

challenges.content: Yes, but my brother went there last month,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #23

challenges.content: you know, to look at the old cities like the Mayan Indians built.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #24

challenges.content: That's what first got me interested.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #25

challenges.content: Your brother Tom?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #26

challenges.content: No, Dick, Harry's twin.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #27

challenges.content: Anyway, he told me how few trees there were now and how much empty ground that grows almost nothing.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #28

challenges.content: He said the place looked more like the desert than jungle in some parts.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #29

challenges.content: It brought environmental damage.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #30

challenges.content: So I started looking for materials in the library.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #31

challenges.content: Here, look at this magazine.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #32

challenges.content: What's in it?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #33

challenges.content: It's an old issue of "National Geographic".
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #34

challenges.content: It includes interviews with tourists who've been there in the past few years.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #35

challenges.content: It's pretty bad. See the photos?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #36

challenges.content: I see the photos, but one or two photos don't prove anything.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #37

challenges.content: Then read what the article says. Right there.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #38

challenges.content: The first thing it points out is how soil samples show it's hard for anything to grow there.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #39

challenges.content: It says how an area of 21,000 square kilometres has lost most of its forest in the past ten years.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #40

challenges.content: See, there are graphs.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #41

challenges.content: As the number of farmers increases, the acres of forest have decreased.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #42

challenges.content: It's an inverse relation.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #43

challenges.content: So how big is that state?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #44

challenges.content: I'm sorry, but I've never really learned the metric system.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #45

challenges.content: It's bigger than the state of Massachusetts!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #46

challenges.content: That's shocking!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #47

challenges.content: Anything else?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #48

challenges.content: There's lots of else.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #49

challenges.content: Scientists say there's a "growing area" of about 10.5 square kilometres where nothing can grow at all.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #50

challenges.content: It's like the beginning of a desert.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #51

challenges.content: Oh yes.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #52

challenges.content: What Dr Schnee called "desertification".
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #53

challenges.content: But, why can't anything grow there?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #54

challenges.content: I've never really studied soil chemistry.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #55

challenges.content: I'm just starting to look into that subject,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #56

challenges.content: but my sister Marie is a geologist
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #57

challenges.content: and she says the problem is that the soil has too much saline,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #58

challenges.content: with no plants helping to adjust the chemistry.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #59

challenges.content: Apparently, that's a common problem with soil types throughout the areas with rainforest.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #60

challenges.content: Once you lose the plant cover, it's difficult to bring it back.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #61

challenges.content: Reforestation is almost impossible, even if the land is not being used for other purposes.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #62

challenges.content: Wait a minute. What is "saline"?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #63

challenges.content: Saline is salt dissolved in water.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #64

challenges.content: Scientists who've gone there have taken measurements.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #65

challenges.content: They do this by gathering a sample of the soil and running a simple test that shows the ionisation of the solution.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #66

challenges.content: The Geology Department in our own university has reviewed the soil at the site, too.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #67

challenges.content: They're right. It looks pretty bad.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #68

challenges.content: The level of salinity is going up.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #69

challenges.content: But the plants that would solve that problem can't be planted in soil like that.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #70

challenges.content: There is a narrow spectrum of salinity in which the plants will grow.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #71

challenges.content: And once you pass the threshold, there is no way to put the problem right?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #72

challenges.content: Exactly. It's possible that no one can do anything to stop the trend now.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #73

challenges.content: All because of human greed!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #74

challenges.content: Wait a second.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #75

challenges.content: How do you know these "scientists" can be trusted?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #76

challenges.content: What kind of reputation do they have?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #77

challenges.content: Are they reliable?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #78

challenges.content: Oh they're definitely reliable.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #79

challenges.content: They include four members of the faculty from the Geology Department right here at MIT.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #80

challenges.content: Here, study these photographs and check the damage yourself.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #81

challenges.content: That's what Dr Horst who wrote the book here did.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #82

challenges.content: He's newly appointed, but Dr Schnee says that he's brilliant.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #83

challenges.content: So, where are you going now?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #84

challenges.content: I'm headed over to the Geography Department to borrow a map for my presentation.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #85

challenges.content: You know, this whole problem could have been avoided!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #86

challenges.content: The farmers there in the Yucatan...
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #87

challenges.content: Uh, Pete??
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #88

challenges.content: What?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #89

challenges.content: Go take a break! Leave some studying for the rest of us.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 3 - challenge #90

challenges.content: Continuing our broadcast of public service announcements,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 2 - challenge #1

challenges.content: Worldwide Helpers announces upcoming vacancies for a number of volunteer worker positions.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 2 - challenge #2

challenges.content: All applicants must meet the following requirements.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 2 - challenge #3

challenges.content: First of all, applicants must be over 18 years of age.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 2 - challenge #4

challenges.content: The company apologises, but there can be no exceptions to this rule.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 2 - challenge #5

challenges.content: Second, persons interested in these positions may not have police records.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 2 - challenge #6

challenges.content: Minor traffic offences like a parking ticket are, of course, no problem.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 2 - challenge #7

challenges.content: But, and I quote, "past and present drug users and sex offenders" need not apply.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 2 - challenge #8

challenges.content: The employer will, of course, check with the police to verify your clean record.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 2 - challenge #9

challenges.content: In addition, applicants must supply references from past or present employers or teachers along with their recent CV.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 2 - challenge #10

challenges.content: These references must testify as to the applicant's work habits and/or character.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 2 - challenge #11

challenges.content: Remember, these are references from employers or teachers.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 2 - challenge #12

challenges.content: A note from your dear old Mum won't do.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 2 - challenge #13

challenges.content: Worldwide Helpers assures me that they will contact these references to confirm they are genuine.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 2 - challenge #14

challenges.content: Although all positions are volunteer, the employer will reimburse some of your expenses.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 2 - challenge #15

challenges.content: For example, they will pay for transportation to and from the job site.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 2 - challenge #16

challenges.content: Aside from that, the cost of phone calls is covered.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 2 - challenge #17

challenges.content: As for the positions themselves, there are three types.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 2 - challenge #18

challenges.content: The first involves assisting persons confined to wheelchairs.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 2 - challenge #19

challenges.content: For this position, volunteers must be physically fit and in excellent health.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 2 - challenge #20

challenges.content: They must be able to lift at least 150 pounds.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 2 - challenge #21

challenges.content: They should also have a current First Aid certificate from the Red Cross.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 2 - challenge #22

challenges.content: But the most important requirement is that the volunteer must have his own car.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 2 - challenge #23

challenges.content: On Tuesday afternoons, the volunteers take their clients to various scenic spots around the city to experience and enjoy nature.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 2 - challenge #24

challenges.content: If you don't drive, but you'd still like to get involved,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 2 - challenge #25

challenges.content: the centre has a number of openings for people to read to the blind.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 2 - challenge #26

challenges.content: Readers must, of course, read English clearly.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 2 - challenge #27

challenges.content: Persons with no foreign accent are preferred.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 2 - challenge #28

challenges.content: For these positions, you must be available on Monday mornings.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 2 - challenge #29

challenges.content: Oh, wait, I see a note here.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 2 - challenge #30

challenges.content: There is one opening for someone who can read Urdu.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 2 - challenge #31

challenges.content: Apparently, there is a Pakistani blind person who'd like to hear his or her native language.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 2 - challenge #32

challenges.content: But the other positions are all in English.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 2 - challenge #33

challenges.content: And finally, there are a limited number of volunteers needed to care for disabled children.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 2 - challenge #34

challenges.content: I'm sorry, but the information I've been given does not say how many children or what disabilities they have.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 2 - challenge #35

challenges.content: In any case, you are needed to care for the children for one week in August.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 2 - challenge #36

challenges.content: Apparently, this will be at the close of the summer holiday.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 2 - challenge #37

challenges.content: I would guess this involves helping them with the routine chores of daily life.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 2 - challenge #38

challenges.content: Again, volunteers for this position must know basic First Aid,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 2 - challenge #39

challenges.content: be in good health, and be able to lift up to 75 pounds.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 2 - challenge #40

challenges.content: All applications for this position have to be submitted no later than Monday, August 8th.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 2 - challenge #41

challenges.content: Applications may be made either by a regular postal service - the "snail mail" - or by e-mail.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 2 - challenge #42

challenges.content: The mailing address is Worldwide Helpers, Post Office Box 651,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 2 - challenge #43

challenges.content: East Surrey BY8 99C.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 2 - challenge #44

challenges.content: Please write "ATTENTION: Mary Smith" on the envelope.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 2 - challenge #45

challenges.content: Or you can send e-mail to
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 2 - challenge #46

challenges.content: acrawfor@worldwidehelpers.org.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 2 - challenge #47

challenges.content: That's A-C-R-A-W-F-O-R
solution: A C R A W F O R
jsonContent: A C R A W F O R
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 2 - challenge #48

challenges.content: @worldwidehelpers.org
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 2 - challenge #49

challenges.content: So get out there and do something good!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 2 - challenge #50

challenges.content: OK, our next announcement is looking for someone to "facilitate" tiger breeding at the London Zoo.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 2 - challenge #51

challenges.content: And, get this, it's a "strictly volunteer" position.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 2 - challenge #52

challenges.content: That means you don't get paid!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 2 - challenge #53

challenges.content: Oh my God...
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 2 - challenge #54

challenges.content: I'm sorry ladies and gentlemen, but I just have to laugh...
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 2 - challenge #55

challenges.content: Good morning. I've been looking at your holidays to Australia in your brochure.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #1

challenges.content: I'm thinking of going during the second half of next month.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #2

challenges.content: Good morning. As you can see from our brochure,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #3

challenges.content: we offer a wide variety of packages to various destinations in Australia.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #4

challenges.content: Is there anything in particular that interests you?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #5

challenges.content: Yes, my husband and I are very interested in the holidays in the Outback.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #6

challenges.content: These holidays are becoming increasingly popular.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #7

challenges.content: Would you like to arrange flights and accommodation with us, or just accommodation?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #8

challenges.content: Can you arrange flights from Sydney?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #9

challenges.content: Certainly.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #10

challenges.content: OK, flights and accommodation then.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #11

challenges.content: Right. You said that you wanted to travel next month.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #12

challenges.content: Which date would you prefer?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #13

challenges.content: I should point out that there are no daily flights available,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #14

challenges.content: so if you have a flexible itinerary, that's better.
challenges.explanation:
itinerary

a detailed plan of a trip or journey or route
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #15

challenges.content: Well, we arrive in Sydney on the 15th of April
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #16

challenges.content: and we were thinking of travelling to the Outback on the 18th of August, er... I mean April.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #17

challenges.content: OK. There's only one flight from Sydney to Alice Springs on the 18th, so I'll book you on that.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #18

challenges.content: It leaves at 10 in the morning, which is quite convenient.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #19

challenges.content: Shall I book two seats for you?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #20

challenges.content: Yes, please.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #21

challenges.content: As for your stay in the Outback,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #22

challenges.content: you can see from the brochure that we offer three packages:
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #23

challenges.content: budget, standard, and luxury.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #24

challenges.content: The budget package is about 500 Australian dollars.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #25

challenges.content: The standard package is about 700 and the luxury one is approximately 1,000,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #26

challenges.content: though it does depend on exactly what you would like regarding extras.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #27

challenges.content: Which one would you prefer?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #28

challenges.content: Well, we can't decide between the budget and standard options.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #29

challenges.content: Ah, well, actually, just looking at my computer here,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #30

challenges.content: on the date that you want to fly into Alice Springs,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #31

challenges.content: there is no standard accommodation available. It's fully booked, I'm afraid.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #32

challenges.content: That's OK.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #33

challenges.content: We think that the cheapest one should be fine for us.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #34

challenges.content: We don't mind roughing it for a few days and we don't expect to be spending much time at our accommodations.
challenges.explanation:
rough it

If you are roughing it, you are living without good conditions (water, food, bed...)
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #35

challenges.content: We prefer the outdoors.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #36

challenges.content: Right. Let's look at the room options.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #37

challenges.content: First of all, would you prefer a non-smoking room?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #38

challenges.content: Yes. Neither of us smokes.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #39

challenges.content: OK.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #40

challenges.content: Oh, before I forget,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #41

challenges.content: could you book everything in my husband's name, please?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #42

challenges.content: Yes, of course. Are you paying by credit card?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #43

challenges.content: Yes.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #44

challenges.content: In that case, I'll need your husband's name exactly as it appears on the card.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #45

challenges.content: Of course. It's John A. Smyth.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #46

challenges.content: That's Smyth with a "Y".
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #47

challenges.content: John... middle initial "A"...
challenges.explanation:
middle initial

The first letter of a middle name. The middle name is often abbreviated to the middle initial (e.g. Mary Lee Bianchi becomes Mary L. Bianchi). We also have "initial name", which is the first letter of a first name.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #48

challenges.content: surname Smyth, S-M-Y-T-H.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #49

challenges.content: Is that correct?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #50

challenges.content: Correct.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #51

challenges.content: Thank you. I'll just check the price.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #52

challenges.content: The room will cost $100 a night plus $10 tax,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #53

challenges.content: so $110 per night in total.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #54

challenges.content: Is that OK?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #55

challenges.content: Yes, that's fine. Book us for three nights, please.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #56

challenges.content: Most of the guests like to participate in some special activities and trips while they're staying in the Outback.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #57

challenges.content: Is there anything that interests you and your husband?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #58

challenges.content: Yes, there are several things we'd like to see and do.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #59

challenges.content: We'd definitely like to visit the Cultural Centre.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #60

challenges.content: Yes, that's very popular.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #61

challenges.content: It's within walking distance of the accommodation and it's free.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #62

challenges.content: It's also a great place to pick up souvenirs of your trip.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #63

challenges.content: We were thinking about visiting one of the nearby farms.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #64

challenges.content: There are two farms nearby - a sheep farm and a kangaroo farm.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #65

challenges.content: There is also an opportunity to ride camels in the desert.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #66

challenges.content: Have you ridden a camel before?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #67

challenges.content: No, but it sounds like fun.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #68

challenges.content: Could you give me some more details about the kangaroo farm and the camel ride?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #69

challenges.content: Certainly.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #70

challenges.content: The kangaroo farm includes information on how the animals are raised
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #71

challenges.content: whilst the camel ride provides information on desert flora and fauna.
challenges.explanation:
flora and fauna

flora and fauna are words originating from Latin. Flora is plants and fauna is animals.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #72

challenges.content: Which would you prefer?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #73

challenges.content: You can arrange to see the kangaroos in the wild if you like, rather than on a farm.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #74

challenges.content: That sounds perfect.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #75

challenges.content: OK, we'll go on the camel ride and see the kangaroos in their natural habitat.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #76

challenges.content: OK. I'll arrange that for you.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #77

challenges.content: I forgot to mention that the journey also includes a stop at a place of aboriginal artwork.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #78

challenges.content: It's a place well-known for its stone carvings of animals and mythical creatures.
challenges.explanation:
mythical

if something is mythical, it's not real, it's only imaginary and usually in stories.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #79

challenges.content: That sounds great!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #80

challenges.content: Are the carvings in the desert?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #81

challenges.content: Yes.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #82

challenges.content: Wonderful!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #83

challenges.content: Well, that's perfect then. I'm sure you'll have a lovely trip,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #84

challenges.content: but remember that you need to take care in the sun.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #85

challenges.content: Yes. We're really looking forward to our trip.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #86

challenges.content: We really want to try to experience the Dreamtime under the stars.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #87

challenges.content: Of course. That's what a trip to the Outback is really all about.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #88

challenges.content: Yes.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #89

challenges.content: Now, how about the cost...
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 30 - Part 1 - challenge #90

challenges.content: We've been talking about choosing building materials in the last week.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #1

challenges.content: Now, a great many factors influence the choice of building materials.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #2

challenges.content: You can't make a house of cards, right?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #3

challenges.content: And "people who live in glass houses..." and all that...
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #4

challenges.content: Anyhow, today I'd like to say a few words about flooring.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #5

challenges.content: Some artificial materials can be used, like plastic for instance,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #6

challenges.content: which offer mixed blessings when used as a flooring surface.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #7

challenges.content: On the one hand, plastic is cheaper than nearly any other alternative, short of bare ground.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #8

challenges.content: Plastic also does not warp like wood.
challenges.explanation:
warp

if something warps, it becomes damaged by bending or twisting

warped wood
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #9

challenges.content: On the other hand, the best that can be said about plastic is that it "looks like" wood or stone.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #10

challenges.content: However, it cannot replace the real materials.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #11

challenges.content: As I have mentioned, I'm fixing up a new house.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #12

challenges.content: The decorator my wife hired told me,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #13

challenges.content: "Plastic does a great job of looking exactly like plastic".
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #14

challenges.content: Besides, it scratches easily, fades or discolours,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #15

challenges.content: and starts cracking within a year or two.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #16

challenges.content: So, if you're fitting out a sleazy hotel or plan to live in a trailer park,
challenges.explanation:
fit out

if you're fitting out your house, you're preparing or putting furniture and equipment into your house

sleazy

dirty, cheap, low in quality

trailer park

an area where trailers are parked, people live in trailers as their homes

a trailer house
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #17

challenges.content: go with the plastic.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #18

challenges.content: Really, though, for all intents and purposes,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #19

challenges.content: this leaves us with wood or stone as choices for flooring.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #20

challenges.content: Stone and wood are alike in at least one respect:
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #21

challenges.content: both go through processing before they can be put to use.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #22

challenges.content: Since few of us cut our own lumber or quarry our own stone,
challenges.explanation:
lumber

wood that has been cut, prepared for building

quarry (verb)

to dig stone from a quarry

a quarry
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #23

challenges.content: this is not perhaps a pressing concern.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #24

challenges.content: Still, do-it-yourselfers would do well to remember to buy only properly seasoned wood.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #25

challenges.content: Unseasoned wood warps and a warped floor quickly becomes firewood
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #26

challenges.content: (and its owner quickly becomes poorer).
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #27

challenges.content: Likewise, except for dull-hued materials like slate or sandstone,
challenges.explanation:
dull-hued

dull-colored, colors that are not bright, like brown or grey

slate

a type of rock, they're usually dark grey

a slate wall
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #28

challenges.content: most stone floors are polished before installation.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #29

challenges.content: The choice goes well beyond just wood or stone -
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #30

challenges.content: each type requires many further considerations.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #31

challenges.content: A few special remarks are called for when considering wood, for example.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #32

challenges.content: As always, aesthetics, personal taste,
challenges.explanation:
aesthetics

the formal study of the principles of art and beauty
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #33

challenges.content: and layout all play roles as well as the type of house or room.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #34

challenges.content: Oh, and certainly don't forget the cost.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #35

challenges.content: When it comes to cost, a rule of thumb is that the softer and less exotic the wood,
challenges.explanation:
a rule of thumb

A rule of thumb is a rule or principle that you follow which is not based on exact calculations, but rather on experience.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #36

challenges.content: the lower the cost.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #37

challenges.content: In the US, for instance, pine is both ubiquitous and cheap.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #38

challenges.content: Mahogany is imported and exorbitantly expensive.
challenges.explanation:
Mahogany

a type of wood that is reddish-brown

exorbitantly

if something is exorbitantly, its price is much too high
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #39

challenges.content: If you're on any kind of budget when remodeling,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #40

challenges.content: it's really helpful to remember to go for the softer woods.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #41

challenges.content: Aside from cost, there are still lots of different factors that are important in choosing the best flooring for the job.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #42

challenges.content: Continuing with the example of wood,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #43

challenges.content: one must consider the effects of each type of wood on the mood of the room.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #44

challenges.content: When selecting the best wood to use,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #45

challenges.content: particular attention needs to be paid to its grain patterns, texture, and colour.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #46

challenges.content: In rooms where relaxation or deep thought is the aim,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #47

challenges.content: (say bedrooms or the study) dark, strong grained woods are the rule.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #48

challenges.content: Here the grain ought to match the furniture for a feeling of homogeneity.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #49

challenges.content: In rooms where activity and motion are typical,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #50

challenges.content: (dining room or living room)
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #51

challenges.content: lighter, finer-grained lumber is more suitable.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #52

challenges.content: In such a setting, the wood grain might be useful in offering a contrast to the furniture.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #53

challenges.content: This leads to a feel of subconscious excitement, in keeping with the room's function.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #54

challenges.content: In either case, though, consult a decorator.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #55

challenges.content: It is a decorator's job to know what materials to use to fit the function of the room.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #56

challenges.content: Though some things about putting together a room are subjective and based on one's individual taste,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #57

challenges.content: materials appropriate to a room's function are much more straightforward.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #58

challenges.content: A decorator takes the needs of the customer and uses a mathematical formula, rather than subjective words.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #59

challenges.content: Since feelings vary from person to person,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #60

challenges.content: verbal descriptions of wood types tend to be ambiguous.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #61

challenges.content: You want the wood you select, not something approximate!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #62

challenges.content: And if you do decide to do it yourself,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #63

challenges.content: remember that all wood must be treated with preservatives to enhance its appearance
challenges.explanation:
preservatives

chemical substances to prevent things from being damaged or spoiled
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #64

challenges.content: and preserve its natural beauty.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #65

challenges.content: In the case of stone, or "quarry tile" as flat-cut flooring stone is properly called,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #66

challenges.content: a new set of considerations must be weighed up.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #67

challenges.content: Simple colour aside, the degree of reflection must be kept in mind.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #68

challenges.content: This is called the "reflectance rate",
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #69

challenges.content: which is expressed in a number between 0.0 and 1.0,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #70

challenges.content: depending on the amount of light it reflects.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #71

challenges.content: At one end of the scale is polished silver.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #72

challenges.content: At a rating of 1.0, this shiny surface reflects nearly all of the light directed at it.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #73

challenges.content: Numbers closer to zero describe materials that absorb more light.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #74

challenges.content: Moving down the scale a bit,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #75

challenges.content: we see the plastic that has been painted white has a rate of 0.8, which makes sense.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #76

challenges.content: We know that the colour white reflects all other colours while black absorbs all colours,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #77

challenges.content: and plastic itself is a relatively reflective material.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #78

challenges.content: Materials that are denser and darker have reflectance rates much closer to zero.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #79

challenges.content: The quarry tile I mentioned a while ago has a rate of 0.1.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #80

challenges.content: As you may know,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #81

challenges.content: quarry tile is generally dark brown and made from clay so it is quite dense.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #82

challenges.content: Of course, there is considerable variation among types of quarry tile
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #83

challenges.content: because of the hue or treatment of the clay during its creation.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #84

challenges.content: Does anyone have any guesses as to what material may have a rate of almost 0.0?
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #85

challenges.content: We can guess most of these materials are black in colour,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #86

challenges.content: but plastic, wood, and even stone reflect some light.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #87

challenges.content: One material with a rate of almost 0.0 is black velvet.
challenges.explanation:
velvet

a type of cloth or fabric

a black velvet cloth
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #88

challenges.content: The texture produces almost no shine at all.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #89

challenges.content: Carrara marble, despite its white hue,
challenges.explanation:
Carrara marble

a type of marble, marble is like granite but granite is harder
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #90

challenges.content: is actually lower in reflectivity than black onyx!
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #91

challenges.content: In any case, the fact that tiles vary somewhat should not be forgotten.
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #92

challenges.content: A highly reflective floor would not be suitable in a library;
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #93

challenges.content: it would be indispensable in a ballroom (should your home be large enough to feature one).
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #94

challenges.content: Again, a rule of thumb is that "light means lively".
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #95

challenges.content: Since form and material follow function,
challenges.discussionName: IELTS Recent Actual Test 29 - Part 4 - challenge #96

challenges.content: one should only use the more reflective materials in rooms
